This place is awesome. The soft serve machine wasn't working so the staff stayed late to make it work so we could get our treats. Then they gave us extra truffles, Milk Bar Pie and a cookie because we had to wait! Such awesome service! I was so surprised by how delicious this was. Milk Quake was to die for! Like everything Tosi creates it's different, epic and delicious. What a crazy fun night!!!
The ice cream was great. A very original flavor. The portion was huge. Glad we came here.

I came here with some friends for breakfast because I heard good things about the place. I ordered the pecan sticky bun, because it looked delicious. It tasted, however, terrible. It was hard like a rock, not like a sticky bun ought to be. I had to ask for another one, and the lady realized all the other buns were hard too, so she had to take it back to microwave it to soften it. Didn't help too much. The chocolate croissant tasted like chocolate bread. NOT a croissant. Bread. The apple turnover was decent - it had some crispy texture to it with an ok filling. McDonald's makes better apple pies. The twice baked croissant with almonds was pretty good - probably the best thing I tried that morning. Salted caramel brownie was very dense. It had good flavor, but there's no way I could eat an entire thing, or even half of one, in one sitting. Maybe I just don't get the salted caramel craze. At least the coffee was pretty good. And you get a free refill. A little bit of redemption there. I'm just not sure why this place has such great ratings. Some may say decor, environment, convenience of it being 24 hours, etc. But if the food is no good, why should any of that other stuff matter? Just go to Waffle House. It's cheaper there.

I go here at least once a week. The owners and staff here go out of there way to treat you with kindness and respect. The want you to be satisfied. Highly recommend this place. Hidden gem in central Phoenix.

What a great bakery and coffee shop that stays open 24 X 7. Went here for the first time after seeing a show at the Evening Muse. There is a theater next door and the performance had just finished so the place was packed at 11p on a Sunday nite. I had the Creme Broulee which was excellent. They also roast their own coffee beans and the dark roast was exceptionally good. I like that it's so large and has so many tables and great if you have a group of people.

Soooo many amazing things to say about Novel. I've gone here too many times to count. The quality of ice cream to the staff is a 10/10! Also I'm guilty of leaving the house at 11 at night to grab some ice cream before they close. If you live in the valley and you haven't tried Novel, I'm going to assume you do not live here! but all jokes aside...10/10. Check them out!

WOW! We're from the land of Ben & Jerry's, and our family (including two teenagers) thinks this is the best ice cream we've ever had. The flavors included strawberry rhubarb crisp, honey lavender, black Raspberry chocolate chunk, and bing cherry chocolate chunk. In addition, they use environmentally sensitive practices for maintaining the building. Worth taking another trip to Cleveland from the Champlain Valley.
I am gluten free so my options were limited, but I was happy there were options at all! The gluten free birthday cake truffles were AMAZING!!!
Just Ok ice cream cookie sandwich. Enjoyed the vintage shop look and sold vintage candy.
Yes! They have vegan options! Super happy and satisfied; it's hard find vegan sweet spots in Las Vegas but this one was totally worth the drive and (calories) for!

ernahgawd the reviews are true. seriously, one of the best macaroons I've eaten! and they had this peanut butter cookie, yum!! i wish this place opened at like 5 am after i left the club. i'd be eating this or noodle asia in a heartbeat

As a long time Masterchef fan, I've been dying to try out the famous Milk Bar by dessert legend, Christina Tosi. Cue a long weekend trip to Vegas, offering the perfect opportunity to cross Milk Bar off my culinary bucket list. I shared a Milk Pie (formerly known as Crack Pie, but I guess that's not PC?) and Cereal Milk soft serve (with added cornflakes) with my partner. Both were fantastic. The "Milk" Pie (brown sugar and butter on an oat crust cookie) lived up to its former name, as it was so darn delicious. It offered every flavor and texture I'm looking for in a dessert. Sweet, buttery, salty, sticky, gooey, and simply delicious. Be warned that this is a very rich, sweet dessert. If I wasn't already in dessert heaven with my Milk Pie, my Cereal Milk soft serve brought me there for sure. I loved how the soft serve really did taste like cereal milk; like the sweet milk you drink after the frosted coasting on your cereal disintegrates into your milk. However, it wasn't overly sweet and the soft serve had a nice, mellow sweet flavor. The cornflakes were essential in adding a much needed textural element to compliment the creaminess of the soft serve. I wish there was a Milk Bar by me so I could always treat myself to one of Christina Tosi's fantastic creations. Not only is Milk Bar super cute and #grammable, but also outright delicious. I suppose my body...and wallet, for that matter, are happy that it requires a plane ride for me to get a treat at Milk Bar. If not, you'd find me here on the regular!

I crave the bakery at Batch. Bakery Heaven is how I would describe it. Croissants are tasty. The cheese and ham/meat pastries are also wonderfully baked, with the light oven-smokey taste that makes me want to go back time and time again. They also prepare different varieties of pastries depending on the mood of the chefs, and the day of the week. I am constantly surprised. This is a creative, local bakery shop. The prices are a little high ($3.50 for a croissant is a luxury, IMO, albeit delicious), and higher than the other shops near the capital. Also, it doesn't have ANY seat so the whole atmosphere of hanging out and reading at a coffee-shop is lost upon me. This place lives solely on the strength on its art on bakery. And lastly, there is no designated parking, it's a side street parking in a corner shop. Definitely recommended place to try! The baked goods are exceptional.
It's nice and clean the place but when I ordered ocean beach I asked for no whip cream and no salt and they put salt and whip cream !!!

Jack Frost Donuts is the BEEEST donut place ever. I am just glad I don't live too close or I would stop in every day for a donut (or 2). Donuts from the grocery store don't even compare to Jack Frost. I like the maple creme donuts. Cash or checks only here.

I've never been disappointed leaving here. The options are a plenty, something for every sweet tooth fix. Very eclectic frequented by almost everyone. Admittedly I'm not crazy about the chocolate croissants as everyone else is. I love to salted caramel brownie, German chocolate brownie, and honey buns

SUGAR RUSH in the LinQ Promenade Cupcake ATM-how did we miss this the first time!? This was our first experience with Sprinkles so we didn't know there was a cupcake ATM! We went back the next day and found it outside to the right of Sprinkles ice cream section. These might be a bit drier than the inside ones, so get one from the ATM for the experience, then buy the rest inside. Gluten Free Red Velvet cupcake available-I'm not sure if they rotate GF flavors. I tried this and it was definitely one of the better GF cupcakes I've had. The GF version has an edible-but-don't-eat "G" button on the cupcake to identify it from its flour containing friends. Ice Cream - as if the cupcakes aren't enough to put you into a pre-diabetic state, you can get ICE CREAM here too. Cupcake top sundaes...red velvet cones...unique flavors..but my son just likes plain vanilla so that's all we tried. If you're in the area near Flamingo/LinQ/High Roller and craving something sweet, this is your spot.
Phenomenal, tasted like cold ice cream The waffle cone tasted like waffles And the small house style surrounding makes it seem like a cool hipster village
The locals told me that this is one of the best places for good old fashioned Wisconsin ice cream here in Madison! I went and was scrumptiously delighted!!

Really love this place ! I've been to the one in SD many times! This place never disappoints and they always have awesome new idea to do with doughnuts. And there Ice cream doughnut is awesome! That's a much have!! Highly recommend this place !!

Lots of donuts, lots of cream! I tried the Samoa donut since it's my fav Girl Scout cookie! The donut was okay, but not the best I've ever had. The extra dollop of frosting on top of the samoa donut wasn't necessary. Sort of takes away from the Samoa flavor itself. Frosting was a bit extra. Stop by if in the area, but I wouldn't make a special trip. It's a small shop made just for pickup. No seating inside & did not see a restroom.

I was fan girling so hard and I had planned to stop here after we ate at Momofuku's but I was so incredibly full! We decided to comeback the next day when they opened and it was sooooo worth it! We got the crack pie, compost cookie, Birthday cake truffles, cereal milk soft serve with fruity pebbles, and the sky lark boozy shake (i may have the wrong name of the shake? It was a long week in Vegas lol). Since we were flying out we packed everything up but the ice cream treats into our carry on bag for our flight back up to Seattle. Everything made it! I would not recommend doing that for longer flights though as the crack pie and the truffles should be kept cold. The staff were super friendly! Thank you for the traveling tips with the food. For the treats - oh heck yes! That was a wonderful experience and I am going tell my husband to buy us some more cookies and truffles as xmas gifts for the family. The compost cookie was a hit with the guys because there is a slight hint of coffee in there. The crack pie was a hit for those who are not big sweet fans because it wasn't overwhelming. The birthday cake truffles were hands down my favorite. They tasted so fresh and not processed.

It's a great concept. The menu is creative and fun, and the product is tasty, although very sweet - and this is coming from an American. Beware of massive sugar highs and even bigger crashes lol! Firstly, Ingrid (I believe), has great customer service skills. She easily sold us on her favorite menu items, and was willing to answer my partner's many questions. She definitely had fun with us, and vice versa. She sold us on quite a bit of treats, and since we are locals, we don't mind taking stuff home. A box of a dozen cookies and a Crack Pie - because who doesn't get the Crack Pie? She had a lot of great ideas for enjoying the cookies. The Corn Sugar cookie warmed with honey? Yes, please! Now, my only complaint is the price point. I completely understand Strip prices, considering I live in Vegas and have worked on the Strip for years. However, $35 for a dozen average-sized cookies? That alone will ensure that I don't go back on a regular basis, even though I'm in the area quite often. It'll be a nice treat when friends or family come to town, maybe. But it's not going to generate any return business from myself, or many locals, really. It's too bad, because everything else was on point.

Good coffee, good sandwiches, so-so desserts (be careful, they're not all good), GREAT atmosphere. Considering Charlotte's lack of good coffee & cappuccino, Amelie's doesn't have to be great to do business as a coffee shop. It's their Parisian style decor and cafe-esque layout that stands it apart from every coffee shop I've been to in Charlotte and elsewhere :) It's no wonder this place has been around for years!

Yes, I'm a fan of Milk Bar! I didn't know too much about the desserts here when Milk Bar creator Christina Tosi opened up the first West coast location in the Cosmo. Then we got to meet her at a Yelp event prior to opening and try the birthday cake and truffles that are signature items as well as a few of the cookies. That's the first time I tried the birthday cake and from then, I've been a fan. Yes, the cake is on the pricey side, but it's great for a special occasion when you want to treat yourself. My friends and I ordered one for our July birthdays and shared it with a group of other pals because sharing is caring. The item that I've had multiple times is the cereal milk soft serve. My favorite flavor is the Fruity Cereal Milk soft serve because it really does taste like the milk at the bottom of a bowl of Fruity Pebbles. Apparently, this flavor is only available at the Vegas and Toronto locations so lucky us! The soft serve melts very quickly so have napkins ready. The cake truffles are tasty little nuggets of goodness and I've bought them as gifts for friends. I'm glad that we have this location here in town and look forward to another birthday occasion (mine or someone else's) for more cake. Yelp Review #800
The vegan ice cream options are really good! My wife's favorite is the key lime. I will really miss this place if we leave Cleveland.

So, my buddy at work was telling me about a "donut ice cream sandwich" that he had. Donuts and ice cream, together? Sign me up! My buddy Rick also had written a review of this spot a few months back, so I was excited to try it. I was in the area the other day, and decided to stop in. The shop is really small! It is a little tricky to find, too (if the sign was not out on the curb of Grand, you could easily pass it by). Once you do locate it though, you are in for a treat! I walked inside and was greeted by the owner, Brandon. He asked me if I had ever been before, how I heard about them etc. Really nice dude! I told him that I heard about their famous donut ice cream sandwich, and he smiled and let me know that's what they are famous for. He explained how they have an ice cream chef, and a donut chef with many years of experience between the two. He also let me sample whatever I wanted. I browsed the flavors and had my eye on two of them right away. The Cookie Monster, and The Fat Elvis. I had a sample of both, and decided to go with a donut sandwich with a scoop of Fat Elvis topped with Oreo cookie pieces (you get your choice of a topping, or a sauce/drizzle). He warmed up the donut, scooped out the ice cream and handed over the goods. Here is how it was.......................... Fat Elvis Donut Ice Cream Sandwich- Sometimes, when you get a "gimmicky" dessert, it doesn't work out and doesn't live up to the hype. I am happy to say, this ice cream sandwich TOTALLY lived up to the hype! The donut they use is a glazed donut. Texture was perfect. It wasn't a heavily glazed donut, which actually worked out better because it was not messy/sticky.. It sort of reminded me of a brioche roll, but more sweet. The ice cream stuffed inside was delicious! The Fat Elvis is a peanut butter/banana/bacon combo of flavors. It was really tasty and I would come back to just get a few scoops of this in a cup on its own. The Oreo pieces added that extra sweetness and chocolaty goodness to the sandwich. It was a damn fine ice cream concoction! I could have easily had 2 or 3 of these things! Might get a little pricey if I did that ($5.00 per sandwich), but if I had an extra $20.00 laying around, that would be a hell of a way to spend it, lol! Overall, I am glad my friend told me about this spot! Brandon was awesome, the donut ice cream sandwich was delicious, and I'm sure I will come back soon enough. I'm not down this way too often, but this is a spot that would be worth driving to! It was great!

Amazing ice cream and please expect a wait as you would at any other incredible small business that is very popular. The selection is vast and the staff is super friendly. I personally love the black cherry and the blueberry cheesecake chunk. As a dessert junkie I keep going back and am grateful for this place.

The best place to go if you're looking for a place to relax and not feel guilty about stuffing your face with baked goods sent from heaven. My go to is always the eclairs - whether you get chocolate, vanilla, or caramel, there are no misses! But. I tried the infamous salted caramel brownies last night for the first time - and they definitely live up to the hype. There's more to this bakery than meets the eye - no seriously, I couldn't believe how big the place was - and no matter what you order, you'll leave happy!

I had the pleasure of attending this location for outing recently. Upon entrance, much of the place is lit up well with lots of abstract lighting. I have always enjoyed visiting each of these locations as no two are the same and follow an unorthodox decoration style. We visited late at night so the staff was ready to get us out of there but always stayed kind and efficient. The pastries and deserts were absolutely delicious and come at a fair price for the quality. They offered a fair bit of outdoor seating along with having plenty of indoor seating. I love this place as it is perfect for any social gathering or if you prefer to just keep to yourself and get some work done.
The staff was friendly and the cookie cup was amazing. Would definitely come back again!

Hoboken, BABY!!! I was driving by and saw that Carlo's Bakery is now at the Venetian. After watching many seasons of Cake Boss, I was contemplating if I should order some of their goodies and have them shipped over to me. However, I can scratch that idea since there's a shop at Vegas. Inside Venetian, I have to say it was hard to find. There are signs everywhere, but nothing pointed to where they are located. When I did find it, it was like stepping into this store over at Hoboken, New Jersey! They did a great job decorating their store to look like their original shop. There's a line before you can get into the store. However, you can browse at their selection as long as you are behind the red velvet rope that separates the on lookers and those who are actually paying. When I was there, Friday around 3pm, the wait in line was only 15 minutes. When I finally got to the display, I ordered the cannoli and lobster tail (I couldn't order too much because I was on my way to Bacchanal for dinner). Buddy claimed that these were one of his top items! The cannoli...I enjoyed them, but that's because I like cannoli. Here at Carlo's Bakery, I didn't find them any special, but they were still good. The shell had a nice crisp. The cream was semi-sweet, the way I like it. The lobster tail, on the other hand, is not something you'd find at many other Italian bakeries (as far as I know). It was made of a large shell, somewhat shaped like a lobster tail. It was stuffed with more cream. I was glad I ordered this because I've seen this many times on his show, but I didn't enjoy it. The shell was too thick and the cream was too bland. I wasn't sure what I was tasting! My total was just under $10 for 2 items. Overall, I am giving them 3 stars. It was fun to be there, but I didn't find anything special. It was just overpriced baked goods. If you're a fan of the show, then I'd recommend checking it out once because the shop in Venetian is modeled after the original location. I think I would have been much better off at Bouchon Bakery!

Oh, Sprinkles, you were such a disappointment. Everyone raved about you. I love cupcakes. We were supposed to be a match made in heaven, but you were an awkward first and second date. First and foremost, there are two doors: Ice Cream Orders and Cupcake Orders. If you order only cupcakes, you can enter the other door (I was smart enough to ask). As it was about 11 PM at night, the line was still a bit long and the cupcakes were sparse. The counter staff was friendly, pleasant, and informative. I like that Sprinkles offers both traditional, vegan, and gluten-free options. I like that there is a Cupcake ATM for afterhours cupcake delights. I guarantee the drunken, twacked out people watching is 24k gold. Sprinkles is overhyped and overpriced. #sadcupcakeface

I visited Mason's during the winter months, so it had transitioned into a ramen shop. I had the chicken ramen. The egg was cooked very well, but the chicken lacked significant flavor. Overall, I would return for the ramen, and I look forward to their ice cream in the summer months.

Almond Croissant - It was hard and over baked. I had huge hopes but was very disappointed. This must be fluke, must be a one time mistake because I saw a picture of one of their half eaten croissants with airy hole pockets. But if they had messed up a batch, why not just throw it out? Where is the quality control? It really is not worth tainting their brand name.
So yummy. The only reason I did not give 5 stars is because they no longer sell the chocolate dipped macarons.

This "Cake Boss" offering is quite popular - LONG lines for pastries that are generally good, but not great. Very visually attractive but uneven quality. Cream in puffs felt oily and were certainly not fresh cream. Cakes were pretty good and sour cream based frosting was very good I would recommend visiting when the line is short - we lucked out about 11am. Not worth a longer wait in my mind

I've had Jeni's in DC before and honestly I could have tried new flavors but I went with old faithful: brown butter almond brittle and gooey butter cake. I noticed the single scoop is the same price as the two half scoop ice cream, But I feel like you get more ice cream with the single scoop. Let's see if I can resist getting two flavors next time and test this hypothesis.... Aside from that, the location is prime. TONS of space for hanging out in the south end with outdoor tables and a big patio. This is one of the coolest vintage ice cream places I've been to.

I was excited to try this place since I've been on a macaroon phase. I bought a box of six macaroons. They looked so pretty in their package but unfortunately they did not live up to the hype. The macaroons were HUGE compared to other places but I would probably not go back for them.

For me, it's the story behind Christina Tosiand her legacy she has made the food world. Yes, it's expensive af for a slice and is very questionable for non-foodies. However, highly recommend Chef's Table on Netflix (Season 4, Ep 1) before getting something from here. The original store is in NYC so this one does not have the same magic, but is good when you are craving some of her classic desserts and you happen to be in Las Vegas. We were celebrating my mom's birthday so I got a slice and surprised her in the hotel room. The Birthday Cake definitely hit the spot!!

Three stars are one each for creative flavors, use of natural ingredients and to support local establishments. That apart, what is all the fuss about? The icy almond brittle left much to be desired, and, the Belgian chocolate was passable, at best. They were skimpy with their hot fudge, which was actually pretty good, and, could have been a saving grace. Is it one of the better ice-cream places in the valley? Yes. Does that mean it's great ice-cream? Far from it.

This place is an institution in Charlotte. The brilliant move was when they decided to go 24/7. I thought it was crazy at the time. Instead, it really simply became a safe late night haven regardless of why you were out late. I like the diversity of the crowd and the sense that I am among intelligent, sensitive and discerning people who are engaged with that element of diversity. The pastries are excellent though a bit pricey and the coffee is always good. So, the only reason for four stars instead of five is the price. I swear I think I saw their pastries on the train ride in the Hunger Games.
For me, this place is A-ok because I'm not a big sweets person and the baked goods are a little over priced, but it's a great place to hang out with friends.
Wonderful place, great pastries and lunch items as well as desserts!
I do like their ice cream and flavors. I like their fun creations and new ideas that they try out!

We were very dissatisfied with the quality of the food/desserts we got from here. We were super excited to go to the "Cake Boss's" bakery but quickly became disappointed. We all got one of the famous cannolis but found the filling to be a little gritty and not very flavorful. The cannoli also left a greasy film in your mouth. I got the carrot cake and my friend got the strawberry shortcake. Both of our cakes were really dry and the only thing we ate was some of the icing and whipped cream. I would definitely not recommend this place. Save your money and go elsewhere.

Location is great because it's in the heart of The linq promenade outdoor mall. The reputation of Sprinkles comes from its Beverly hills original location in CA. I've had both give cream and cupcakes taste fine. Being right next to in-n-out helps bring in ton of traffic. Where they can improve is the speed of the service. This layout at this location is set up weird and makes you walk backwards through the waiting line for pick up. Also I don't understand why the server had to pick up each ice cream flavor bucket out of the freezer l?!?!?

I love this place! My sister and I tried it for the first time about 3 years ago and have been in love ever since! Customer service is always great even if it's busy, they get through the lines pretty quick! I love the rainbow cake and today I tried their lobster tale cookies and cream flavor and it was AMAZING!

Dear sweet baby Jesus, this place is good! We started out with a scoop of half "salty caramel" and half "peanut butter and jelly" as our gateway drug at this deviously unassuming den of sugary sex appeal. I ordered the ice a fore mentioned ice cream and my girlfriend got a peanut butter, choco chip, pretzel cookie. The cookie was really good. The ice cream was spectacular! So we made our way to the end of this little strip off of the strip and I realized that I had lost all my ice cream. This was an emergency situation and neither of us hesitated to do what had to be done as we immediately returned to Sprinkles for a refill on our Salty Caramel. We returned the following night for a brownie sundae made with, you guessed it; salty caramel. And I finally returned one last time before I boarded my flight so I could bid farewell to my new love! This time I had a naughty threesome with salty caramel and peanut butter cup. This place is very high quality and while the prices are a hair more than what you might pay at your local Baskins and Robins, they are hardly the "Vegas prices" we had come to expect during our visit. And it isn't just value and a quality product, but also a great staff. I was very impressed. We encountered at least three or four different employees in our several visits and each was nicer than the next, These ladies were perky, smiling, polite and fun. I'm a "particular" person according to some people and it's little things that make the difference. When I ordered for my first time, before I could even ask, she offered to put the two flavors side by side instead of on top of each other so I could experience each flavor untainted. I love it! We only tried a few things but I have to imagine that it's all good. Try the salty caramel, it's the best I've ever had where the salt really comes through and cuts the rich sweetness so that you can eat and eat and never get fatigued. Evil genius!
Has been a great place to get my French fix! Love their PÃ¢tÃ© de Campagne avec cornichons on a fresh baguette! Yummy!!! Soups are great! and of course their patisseries!!!

I love this place; unfortunately, I can never get anything when I visit because there is a 5 mile line that stretches into the other room. Come here when people are out of town (e.g. Spring break, holidays). I look forward to their other place opening to cut down on the overwhelming number of people who go to this one.

I went to the cupcake ATM (so cooooool by the way) because I didn't feel like waiting in line inside. There were about 10 choices of cupcakes to choose from and I picked the sprinkles. It looked great, frosting was caked in sprinkles so I didn't hesitate to dig in. Well...it was terrible. The frosting was almost inedible sweet where all I could taste was powdered sugar. The cake portion was flavorless even though it was laced with sprinkles. I ate half and threw it out, wasting a very valuable $4.50 on a less than mediocre cupcake. On the plus side, the packaging was really cute.
Scrumptious fresh desserts. Came to visit friends and stopped by to get dessert. We got a variety of delicious pastries and they were all fresh and delicious.

Visiting from Texas and fell in LOVE with this cutie of a coffee shop. The decor alone would make me come back but the customer service and delicious pastries really sealed the deal. The funky French style had me taking pictures like a true tourist. They even have the bike lock wall outside! They have an area for working/studying that was spacious and set to the side out of the hustle and bustle. We had just about every pastry...the pecan sticky bun situation thing was truly next level. The coffee was yummy and I learned that a medium roast actually has more caffeine than a dark roast. The more ya know, right? This shop was definitely a bright spot in a very long work day. Can't recommend enough. Oh and the yogurt with fruit had the biggest blueberries I've ever seen.
This is our favorite local ice cream spot. Fun atmosphere, friendly staff and always clean. My favorite is the Spumoni and my daughter loves the waffle cone sundae. Yum!

Love the unique ice cream flavors, they offer flights so you can get a sampling of multiple flavors too. Check out the seasonal offerings as well. Staff is super friendly and knowledgeable of the flavors. They also offer pints (pricey though), water, and apparel items too.

When I tell you this is The BEST homemade ice cream I am not lying l!! They have over 25 different flavors. The brownie sundae and Apple pie a la mode is deeeeelicious!!! And every Tuesday is $2 for a single scoop but it's so huge it's like a double!! Go here NOW!!!!
Love the unique flavors they have available, right alongside the traditional favorites. So rich and creamy!

They have amazing cake! I got the Italian cake and a napoleon. Both were amazing! The fruity pebbles and Cinnamon Toast Crunch macarons were delicious as well. The staff is very friendly and helpful as we went here for the first time. I can't wait to go back and try more!

Heard this place made the best ice cream. I have to disagree! Baskin Robbin's flavors are better. No place to sit and eat, there are only 3 benches. Its not a parlor where you can sit and enjoy a sundae if you so choose to get one. With all the hype, expected to have homemade sauces and whipped cream NOT. Brought my relatives from out of state, they were very disappointed... Do not recommend and will not go back.

The korean icecream here is delicious! You'll find a few Asian favorites on the menu such as Ube, Thai Tea & Matcha. They have Strawberry & Oreo flavors to name a few. I loved how adorable the pancake fishes are! My only complaint is seating... there is very limited seating here & I wouldn't recommend this place for a meet up on a busy evening. Unfortunately my family had to stand as we tried to enjoy each other's company and we really couldn't. I wish there were regular tables so people can converse.

Finally got to order a Jumbo box during covid and got super lucky. Her items are just legit and you can tell they were made with love. Unconditional love. It was a lot of pastries but the gf and I just nibbled on them day by day until they were gone. Everything tasted just as good days later with maybe the exception of the jelly roll (we'll eat that first next time haha). I can't wait to go try more things when she finally reopens and especially to get those oatmeal pies and cookies. Those were my highlights. Just be aware, she sells out quickly with almost everything she makes.
Best ice cream in town! If you need your ice cream fix go to Scooptopia!! This family owned shop always sweet and makes me feel welcomed!!

I wish I could go to 4 stars. But I am somewhat of a frozen custard snob. For the Champaign-Urbana area, this is definitely the best place to get frozen custard. I like the hometown feel of the place. But Jarling's loses one star for service. Every time I've been there, the lines seem to move at a snail's pace. They seem to have plenty of workers, but the wait is long nonetheless. It may be that customers don't know what they want before they get up to the register. Also, I love the idea of the cold fudge. Hot fudge is so delicious, but it has the irritating habit of melting the frozen concoction too quickly (especially a softer custard). But I would like to see Jarling's use a better quality fudge. It seemed to me that theirs is closer in taste to Hershey's chocolate syrup than to an actual thick hot fudge.
Closed at 9PM on the 4th of July! Fireworks hadn't even popped off yet. Walked in and were yelled at -- "We're closed!" -- without a hint of apology. Took my talents to Mason's Creamery instead.

So far, this is one of my favorite Italian Bakeries in Las Vegas. We walked in about 10:30 am and it wasn't busy at all. We talked with Austin while placing our order and he gave us a few great suggestions. I liked the Nutella filled cookie, Pistachio Biscotti, butter cookies, Cannoli, and the Boston Cream. The Cannoli sweet, with chocolate chips, a great filling and a fresh crunch. I hate soggy ones, so this made my day. We waited to pay as he wrapped our purchases in boxes and even tied them shut with a string. It wasn't a speedy transaction and it can be a little pricey for some (I got a lot of stuff for $26.00), but it's Vegas. Live a little. For great Italian baked goods, service and attitude, this is the place!
Much better than Champaign's Jarlings. Better service, better ice cream, and the lines usually significantly shorter. Worth the drive!!

This place is amazing. I have never been disappointed in any aspect, from products to service. The marble taro loaf is incredible! So many different items to choose from that are absolute delicious. Love, love, love the egg tarts! And the prices are incredibly reasonable. I usually stuff a box full of different breads and never spend more than $23. I really wish this franchise came further east than the CA/NV area. At certain times of day, be prepared for a line out the door. It's best to get there early before 9am. Otherwise the place gets so packed it's hard to move around inside with your tray and tongs. Enjoy the "FRESH BREAD!" and get out of their way when you hear it, because they're comin' in hot!

This is my second time at pages and I can't wait to come back again. Not only do me and Pages dairy mart share the same name they also have amazing ice cream and so many flavors to choose from. They also have dairy free options like oat milk ice cream. This time I got butter pecan soft serve on a sugar cone. It was wonderful! They also have blueberry soft serve that looked intriguing I'll have to try that next time.

I have watched Cake Boss for years since I am a cake decorator and baker as well. Buddy has always awed me with his creativity which made me want to try his products. I had the chance when we were at LV last week, there was no line and they had tons of pastries to choose from. But there are no sign or price as to what the items were. So it's hard to choose more so. We opted to just try the cookies, m&m and chocolate chips and a Christmas sugar cookies. Got 3 of each and 1 cheese danish. I was so surprised though that all of it rang to more than $40. The kids liked the cookies but they were like any other cookies that you can buy from bakeries that costs less. I didn't like the cheese danish because it was too sweet and the pastry itself was a bit hard, I'd prefer the ones from Panera bread. Maybe next time when I get the chance I'll try the cakes. We didn't get any at the time since we had some cakes already from another bakeshop.

Great selection of pastries and coffee, but the employees should be more attentive. They should be nicer, provide options instead of showing that they are "bothered" by people. When we went, there were only two costumers and like 4 employees!

This place is a Charlotte staple. The salted caramel brownies are amazing! I ask for one every day on my birthday. They also have great breakfast baguette sandwiches and coffees/teas. The decorations here are so unique and fun to look at. It's a great place to work remotely or have a meeting. They also have an event space for bridal showers, baby showers, etc.
Best ice cream in Cleveland. I wish they were open in the winter. But come st.patricks day I'll be back.
Wonderful eclairs and cream puffs, but the lobster tail pastry tasted off. Either burnt or stale or both. The filling was still delightful though.
This place is soo good super cute, highly recommend the Cookie Crisp ice cream. It was very cheap as well which I was surprised. I will definitely be back to try different flavors :-)
Loved it! Took my bf for his first time and he enjoyed it very much! Cookie Monster will definitely be my GO to!

This sprinkles has the worst cupcakes we have ever had from a Sprinkles location. The cupcakes at the Beverly Hills location and the La Jolla location taste nothing like these disgusting cupcakes they are serving in Las Vegas. I can't even believe that they are allowed to serve whatever this concoction considered and put Sprinkles name on any of it. Save your money and go to the ones in California.

2 people in the bakery at a time. They did a great job ensuring everyone's safety. Ordered the 2 macarons ( cotton candy and Nutella), pistachio cheesecake, and tiramisu. I give the tiramisu and cheesecake a 12 out of 10! They rock! The macarons I give a 7 out of 10.
Yummy!! This icecream was delicious. They are very fast working. We didn't have to wait long at all!

I was really looking forward to trying Milk Bar, but to my dismay, it really wasn't that great. It's not even that the prices are ridiculous or anything; the sweets just didn't live up to the hype. When we went around 1:30pm on a Sunday, there was about 10 people in line and it didn't take too long to get to the counter. They ran out of a few of the popular cookies so we ended up getting the crack pie, corn cookie, blueberry and cream cookie, birthday cake truffles, and the cereal milk soft serve with cornflake crunch. The crack pie was way too sweet for my taste, though I enjoyed the consistency of the pie.. The blueberry and cream cookie was kind of oily, and the corn cookie was pretty good. I only had a bite of the soft serve because I was so full, but my first impression was slight disappointment and that I've had better. So all in all, I may have expected too much, but it was simply a mediocre experience.
Great menu with a great selection! I ordered ice cream and a rose milk latte and both were phenomenal! Staff were super nice and helpful! The orders came out so fast
Was good wait was worth it good old school candies def come back when I'm craving a scoop again

Viens ici pour un rÃ©gal franÃ§ais...full disclosure that's Google translate for "come here for a French treat". There are many things that I "amour" and the top three, in no order. 1. GREAT FOOD AND DRINK whether you are getting just a sweet treat (which there are dozens of options), or feeling something a bit more "remplissage" they have a full breakfast and extensive sandwich menu. 2. The atmosphere here is perfect, it's trendy, French inspired, and often times makes me smile or chuckle with how they pull it all together. 3. They are open 24 hours. Need some good coffee and breakfast at 4 am before a flight but don't want fast food? They got you. Been out in NODA drinking craft beer and want a tasty nightcap? Come get a salted caramel brownie. This might be my top place to recommend here in Charlotte. Shoutout to Summer for being a great brand ambassador and Tony for being genuine and putting a smile to my face.

I have to say I am 100% Italian and I really wanted to love this place because I watch Cake Boss and i love the show. After I FINALLY found the bake shop, it was really small. The selection was limited and geared more for the Vegas tourist not authentic. I asked if they had a pasticiotta, and the girl taking orders looked at me like I was cross eyed. After I explained to her what it was she apologized. It looks like the bakery had more American features like cupcakes, cake slices, etc which is not traditional at all. It was really Americanized. I ordered cannoli, an eclair, and a sfogliatelle. The cannoli were good. The eclair was dry, barely any cream inside. The sfogliatelle was average. Nothing to write home about. I will stick to the bakeries in CT. Maybe the bakery in Jersey is better, but this was needs some help.
Was just passing thru the town. Ice cream was so good I would go back whenever I am in town.

I went for some boba tea on a Sunday afternoon. They didn't have any boba prepared and I waited almost 20 minutes for my Thai tea milk tea. I also was a little disappointed they got rid of their lightbulb drinkware. Not worth going back.
If looking for something other than yogurt this is a fantastic "real" ice cream parlor. My 3 & 4 year old LOVE it!

Oh man!! This place is SO good! It's a little ice cream shop near downtown phx. It's a cute cozy place. The owner, Brandon, is super nice, and very helpful. You could tell he loved his shop. He gave my boyfriend and I suggestions, and told us what exactly was in each flavor. There's eight total flavors, half is limited, while the other half their signature flavors. I had a limited flavor which was the Black Raspberry Cashew, boy do I tell you, it is the BEST ice cream I've had in awhile! I was contemplating on getting it in a warm glazed donut until the Leslie Knope (love the name by the way) caught my eye. It's a warm waffle sandwich. You also get a free topping with it, so I got the basic sprinkle (boring I know) but it was so good! Thinking about it now makes me wish I had one. My boyfriend had the Leslie Knope as well but with the Cookie Monster flavor (one of their signatures). That was also delicious! It is definitely a must try! You will not regret it!

Located in a shopping center with plenty of parking and a nice view of a body of water. The milkshake did not disappoint in taste and was aesthetically pleasing! The glazed donut stuff with icecream was perfectly made too! Nice and warm on the outside, but keeping the icecream cold and not melting everywhere. The menu has a great variety in flavors and options. The ordering process might need better structure though.
I absolutely loved this place! It was my first time ever coming but the atmosphere was very cute and quaint! I will definitely be coming back here in the near future!
We went to get ice cream and ice cream sandwiches it was so delicious but the wait was so long I love it but I don't think I like waiting that long in line for ice cream but it was so delicious.

Great ice cream and treats! It is a good late night stop when you really need a kick of sugar. The good - amazing store made flavors - cookies! - friendly and helpful staff - open late - decent amount of parking for a place on central - nice casual seating - always clean and bright The not so good - next to a high school, so maybe don't go during lunch hour

Simply very good ice cream. A wide variety of flavors, excellent size options and very good prices. The servers were welcoming, offered advise and quickly transacted our purchase. Just a very nice experience following our trip to Red Rock Canyon..

Of course whenever I go to Las Vegas (like once a year), I look up all the cool insta-worthy food places to try...LOL. This cute little place is located on the SECOND FLOOR of The Cosmopolitan Las Vegas. I had a bit of trouble locating this, but realizing the arrows on the signs I was able to find it haha. Keep in mind, this place is actually pretty small. The Milk Bar is directly right next to Momofuko which took part in developing this dessert place. I was super super anxious to taste their soft serve (that I've seen in pics on the insta from the NY location) so I could see just HOW good it really is. They serve pies, cookies, drinks (with or without coffee), and of course their soft serve ice cream. Their ice cream is actually pretty pricey starting at around $6-7. You get options for toppings such as fruity pebbles or cereal, chocolate chips, and even sprinkles. But still, pretty pricy. The amount they give you ALMOST makes up for that, but not quite all the way. My sister didn't really find the taste of the cereal soft serve appealing, but for me it was pretty dang good, but not enough to amaze me. Compared to other places I've tried, Milk Bar is definitely up in my Top 4. It's similar to MilkCow in Fremont but a more sharper/unique taste. It's simple yet so interesting and different. I'd give this place 3.8 stars, but rounded up to 4 because it was both aesthetically pleasing and appealing to my tongue.

If this is what you called service than I guess I should never have tipped! The service is definitely hit-and-miss at this location. I am a regular here when I stay at the Venetian. the cashier was taking my order and in the middle of my order taking she turned over to the two baristas asking/discussing about something - possibly about an order she took for the person in front of me. FINE! She continues to take my order. I asked "is your latte sweet?" She said no. So I said, "great, I will take a large iced latte. I will also have an iced tea, easy on the ice, please. And a double shots of espresso." Got my order. I was a bit confused why I got a hot latte opposed to an iced latte. So I told the barista (as seen in the photo) that I ordered an iced latte. OMG... here comes the condescending remark - "well, did you tell her that?" With her big eyes eyeballing at me. I responded, "yes I did." The barista turned around asking/telling the cashier. The cashier came toward me telling me, "you told me you wanted iced coffee, you said latte, you didn't say "iced" latte." I responded, "first, I asked you if the latte was sweet or not", you said unsweetened and that's when I said "I'd like an iced latte". I also said "iced tea, easy on the iced." (me: thinking to myself, how many times do I have to say "iced"???)... mine you, they are not even busy. After speaking with the cashier, she took away the hot latte and she told to the barista, "just make a new one". The barista took the hot latte and threw it right in the trash with FAT CHIP ON HER SHOULDER as if the world is coming to an end and that she needs to sacrifice her life to make me an iced latte! well, maybe I was exaggerating, but seriously, that was the attitude I got! I mean, gesh... She could just put the ice in a new cup and pour the hot latte over. I would have been fine.... but no, she wants to make it even harder on herself.
Salted. Caramel. Brownies. The best thing ever. Chai lattes are great too and the breakfast sandwiches are delicious and filling. Get some macaroons to go and have a great time.

Excellent small batch ice cream - owner scooped it up for us & was so nice & patient. I had a scoop of Butterbeer & a scoop of Bourbon Caramel Toffee Crunch & both were excellent. My husband & daughter enjoyed donut ice cream sandwiches. Parking is difficult but worth it!

The hype from the "Milk" in LA was what drew me to try Milk bar in the first place, so when I saw it here at Cosmopolitan hotel in Vegas, it made me excited; however, they didn't carry the ice cream macarons which was the reason why I liked the Milk in LA. Oops! My mistake...because the Milk is not the same as the Milk Bar, Duh! lol I did a little research (trusting the yelp reviewers) with their trusty recommendations, so I tried a slice of the birthday cake and a chocolate cookie. Talk about sugar rush...I guess I'm not into the super sweet, super rich and dense type of cake and both the cake and the cookie didn't taste fresh either.

Great atmosphere, good food, authentic service. We sat outside on a gorgeous morning... No wait was great! Ordered a Bloody Mary, extra spicy. Good drink, but not spicy AT ALL. Waiter was French and described the menu well... I ordered the foie gras with baguette. The foie gras was presented in a jar, and the baguette was extra crunchy. (I like it a little less so, but tasty overall.) My meal companion had a lamb sausage hash of sorts with poached eggs. He said the meal was good, but one egg was over cooked. We would come back. Great breakfast spot!
Just delicious! The giant cinnamon rolls are my favorite along with the maple donuts! Yum!

Really good pastries! I'm in love with their almond croissant ($4). I honestly wasn't expecting much but was very surprised. The almond croissant is very crunchy on outside but soft on the inside. It wasn't super sweet and had a million almond slices on it. Service - not the best. This place is a lot smaller than expected

JUST DON'T, we've been coming here since they opened. They raised their price twice in past 12 months. That would be ok if it was the best cupcake ever but it's not. Place was filthy, counter had more than one cupcake smeared on the counter. The tables outside were all dirty, every table. When we went first went here they were like Disney. The people made it nice and welcoming and just seemed like a really special place. That's all gone, it's dirty and the people seem overworked and uncaring. Sorry to say because it was good, pre mouse in the sprinkles window ( on YouTube) btw.

Nice little ice cream shop, visited with a group as it was recommended by some friends. Everyone with me thought the ice cream was really good. I don't know much about ice cream so I may not be the best judge but a couple tiny scoops of ice cream here a bit on the pricey side. It tasted like ice cream to me. Not noticeably better than any other ice cream I have ever had honestly but good. If you were an expert I am sure you would notice the difference in quality here but as a normal Joe I did not. The line was long and out the door at 9PM so people in this area obviously love it.

Oh my God. This place is beautifully eclectic, but let me tell you what won me over the most - the HEART with which this place was designed: 1. Has a special handicap elevator for wheelchairs 2. Gender non-specific bathrooms And so much personality! While it's VERY French inspired, the ambiance is really a hodgepodge. Sort of Paris, sort of hipster, sort of a lot of things! It's a HUGE SPACE! Lots of seating throughout and different areas of the bakery have a different vibe. Never seen a bakery/coffee shop like it before. The bakers work behind glass screens so you can watch them pour batter in and out of huge pots, and it's super fun. I tried their spiced chai and it was really great! They have an assortment of drinks and desserts. I didn't try any of their desserts after a heavy brunch beforehand, but will DEFINITELY be back when Im in Charlotte again! We went Saturday mid-afternoon, and there was no line!

Not really crazy about the ice cream. Some flavors are cloyingly sweet and hard to finish. Then there's the ingredients. This ice cream always tastes like it's got stabilizers and gums (and who knows what else) in it which I really don't like in my ice cream.
Cannoli!!! Omg these were so good. We also got chocolate dipped strawberries which were food as well.

Oh my goodness. I was blown out of the water by this locations delicious ice cream. I recommend getting their "trio" as you can get a taste of a lot off of their large menu. One flavor that stood at to me and is definitely worth trying is the "Gooey Butter Cake". The shop is also located in a beautiful part of Charlotte that is perfect for any day out.

This is one of the roomier locations! Cupcakes are always fresh, and their ice cream is served generously! Be prepared to pay a premium for these sweet treats, as they are considered sophisticated. There are also peak time when it's busy, so try to visit mid morning or mid afternoon! Their Red Velvet is amazing, and their Triple Cinnamon is off the charts! Download the sprinkles app so you can see the daily menu of cupcakes. Their menu has every day staples, and rotates other favors daily and monthly! You can even order from the app if you're wanting to place a special occasion order! **Discount Tip** follow Sprinkles on Instagram! They often post Buy On Get One specials! You usually have to whisper a catchy phrase to the store clerk! We love taking advantage of those specials! They post 1-2 BOGO specials a week, on average!

It's a neat place! I a little Ali Wong's definition of hipster. But my old age I felt comfortable. The donuts were huge and cooked like remember they were 35 years ago back in the dinosaur era. My choices were an apple bacon fritter and a maple bacon log! I don't care what my wife and mother in law got, I had bacon in front of me! They said, " it was good they'd come back and tell others". I had their coffee and yes!, they'll make you what that startakeyurbucks place can make I believe I like this place better. Place is located downtown Vegas and the area is really becoming a great place geared towards us locals and giving us the non-commercial franchise associated crap local Las vegans are looking for! Great little place! Big do-NUTS! Better caffeine beverages than StraveYourBucks!

Great quality and prices, friendly service. Best pastries I've ever had (recommend the danish, any or every croissant). Definitely need to stop in if you're in the area and buy some gifts to take home. Their macarons look the size of moon pies!
Came here for dessert after dinner, and the vegan ice cream was amazing. Tiffany was super sweet and helpful! I'll be back ;)

I like donuts and am always willing to try out different donut shops/bars, especially ones out of state. Las Vegas' Donut Bar is located in downtown, which is a bit out of the way if you stayed along The Strip. We ended up getting a Lyft there one morning for a quick bite to eat. If you follow them on Instagram, they post their menu daily. I was really looking forward to getting the strawberry split donut, however when we arrived - they were all out. Go early so you won't be disappointed like me. We ended up getting: Ohh My Birthday Cake Oreo ($2) Creme Brulee ($2) Caramel Latte ($3) Maple Bourbon ($3) Caramel Latte tasted a lot like coffee and we had a hard time finishing it. Same with the Maple Bourbon. Amongst the 3 of us, we demolished the smaller ones (Creme Brulee & Birthday Cake) but had to take the other two larger donuts (Caramel Latte & Maple Bourbon) back to the hotel. Their donuts are HUGE. It's kind of hard to try all the donuts unless you're with a group. I didn't really care for the Birthday Cake one. It tasted like a funfetti cake that had an oreo inside. At least it was small so we were able to finish. By the time I tried Maple Bourbon, I was already too full and on a sugar high. That was enough donuts for me. My favorites were the Creme Brulee and Caramel Latte, mainly because I love those flavors in general. Mmmmm the Creme Brulee was delicious with its crisp outer caramelized crust and custard filling on the inside. If I had known any better, I would have ordered a dozen of these and called it a day. Next time I'm in Vegas I already know what to get & hopefully they will have my strawberry split then....

It was my first time to Melt. And wow! Most delicious, amazing ice cream...the Cookie Monster, oh my! However, I have to say the customer service killed my overall experience. Music was jamming with a line out the door, but once you got inside you weren't made to feel welcomed. The two working didn't appear to have any excitement serving the anxious and excited customers making the nights most important decision; what flavor?! They had their heads down on their phones for the majority of check out. There was no "hey guys welcome to melt! Let us know if you have any questions." Or "thanks so much for coming in tonight...we'll see you back soon!" "Is this your first time in? If so we have punch cards." The only conversation I had with the girl was "make sure you bring your flight tray back inside." My dad has owned a restaurant for 30 years and from my experience I have learned that customer service can make or break your overall experience. Those working for you are supposed to represent your business in the most positive way possible; you kind of expect that being in the downtown Roosevelt district where people represent a chill, cool, and friendly vibe. With all of that said, keep making delicious ice cream at Melt! The flavors are inventive and who doesn't love the take-out containers with the crunch of the fortune cookie to end the party in your mouth. Here's to more happy scooping employees! #lovetheicecreambutnotheonesservingit

It's your average donut shop just w more fanfare than others. I didn't see the WOW factor honestly. I went there early morning so selection was good. I got 8 donuts for $22 felt like I overpaid for similar donuts I could of gotten at DD or other donuts shop. Won't be coming back.

Go here. Wait on the long line and eat some of the best ice cream ever. It's so good. And perfect beyond the traditional ice cream. Also the dairy free options are amazing. Perfect for date night or girls night out. Also check out the awesome heart confetti wall around the corner. This place won't disappoint.

We came here for the first time and the service was amazing and the owner was so nice! He was super friendly, and super passionate about his shop. He also let us try everything we wanted and it was overall an exceptional experience! Also, got the donut stuffed with ice cream. BOMB!
Typically I save all my empty calories for beer, but their glazed donut is well worth the years off my life LMAO
On a street packed with bars that close at 2am, this place closes at 11pm on Saturday. Genius. Good ice cream though.

The last time we were in Vegas and I noticed Milk Bar, I almost lost it. I read about them in multiple magazines and couldn't wait to try their treats out for myself. Being that we were there to celebrate my husband's birthday, I figured it was the perfect excuse to buy the birthday cake truffles. You can purchase them either in store (3 truffles to a pack) or online. Make sure that you have somewhere cold to store them if you aren't planning to eat them right away though as they require refrigeration. Because I bought them the day before as a surprise, I also got myself cereal milk soft serve to enjoy then and there with a corn flake crunch topping. It was not at all what I was expecting. Their soft serve is sweet, but not in the way vanilla ice cream is. It's more subtle and was almost tart alongside the crunchy cereal. The combination was so addictive, I couldn't put it down long enough to snap a picture. And those truffles? Worth every freaking penny. Here is a description taken from their webpage; 'vanilla rainbow cake mixed with vanilla infused milk, coated with white chocolate and rolled in rainbow cake crumbs'. Yes to all those things please! Unfortunately the lady working the night I went was annoyed with the world and practically rolled her eyes while taking my order. Nevertheless, the guy who actually gave me the items was very nice. It's more than I'm used to spending for dessert, but when in Vegas I suppose. Their cookies also looked ridiculously good, and I saw lots of people ordering the 'crack pie'. Having now tried the truffles from the store, I'm curious to see how well they hold up when ordered online. The next time a birthday rolls around I just might give it a try. Definitely a good option when your sweet tooth craving strikes and you're in the mood for something a little different.

now this place wasn't bad but I just don't see why it's so great. or maybe I just loved sweet republic so much? anyway a few flavors and definitely good ice cream, just not amazing. maybe I should have tried the chocolate but I felt like it was eating Talente ice cream (probably spelling that wrong) they have the same flavors....

Really cool spot. I tried the Campfire S'mores flavor - it was incredible! It even had a touch of smokey campfire flavor. Nuts! The building itself is a work of art and it's cool that you can watch them actually make the ice cream right then and there. Was worth the stop. And the line.

ordered three crunchy cereal milkshakes and they're all weird tasting. i've had this same milkshake at the milkbar in new york and it definitely did not taste like this. the milkshake tastes so salty. saltier than salt & vinegar chips. just read the recipe online and it says it's supposed to be milk, cornflakes, brown sugar, and a pinch of salt. pretty sure they replaced the brown sugar with salt and this drink is just milk, salt, and cornflakes... the soft serve with crunchy cereal was also a little salty. the milkbar pie was 10/10.
Trendy, artsy, fartsy place. Cake was dry to say the least. Drink selection rather limited. Go with a small group. Wear your favorite Bernie t-shirt

Our family favorites: *Strawberry milkshake, specify "made with real fruit" ~~A MUST TRY!!!~~ *Lemon custard in a waffle basket with raspberry topping *Banana split snowstorm made with strawberry custard I've been going to Jarlings all my life and it's always been a staple for my family. I adore their lemon custard and I order it every time. Unfortunately, last night my lemon custard tasted different, almost bland. Out of the hundreds of times I've ordered the lemon, this is the first time I have been let down. I'm sad to say that it seems that quality standards are slipping since the change in ownership. The new POS system is nice, but it's t doesn't really save time when the order is rung up incorrectly. We ordered in the drive through, an employee came out to the car and wrote our order down on a notepad. She tried to upsell my scoop of lemon in a waffle basket w/ raspberry topping as a sundae, and I had to explain a few times that I really just want a scoop of lemon in a waffle basket with raspberry topping. Otherwise, I would gladly order a sundae. My dad's giant milkshake was written down as a regular and had to be remade. Back when the employees had to take orders by memory I honestly think it forced them to pay attention to the order and care if it was right, I've never had a problem with my order in the past. I hope our experience last night was a fluke and not the new normal, I will be so sad to see Jarlings go out of business if these small issues continue to add up.

There's always a line here and I never understood why until I tried this place. This place is super cute. The way they make their deserts with the fish shaped taiyaki. It is filled with custard and soft serve! Place is clean and it really didn't take ther long for them to make my order. The ice cream melted fast but probably because of the Vegas heat. There's a few bar seating inside and a couple of tables outside. Will be back!

Very good ice cream made with everything all natural. The owners seem very hard-working and the mother of one of the owners is there working often too. The pricing is a little bit high but worth it. We only go here for an occasional treat partly because of the cost.

I have always been a Matcha lover but my wife always turned her nose up to it. Well not only does she love Matcha Cafe MaiKo, but she got everyone in the family gift cards for Christmas! I had my first taste this weekend. I had a swirl of matcha with black sesame and a latte. Both were very good and the latte was crafted with care. The service is amazing and friendly. The options and a description of all the choices were given as well as her personal preferences. I was offered samples of everything as well. This is a great addition to the area and I can't wait to go back.

Their chocolate cupcake was AMAZING. So rich and decadent. Their macarons were pretty good for the price of $3.50 each. And I have to say the fillings for the macarons definitely had a lot of flavor to it! It's certainly is a hidden gem!

The minicupcakes are cute and taste sweet but the vanilla has a strange aftertaste from the frosting. The black and white is good though. Meanwhile their ice creams (cap'n ' crunch, salted caramel, cherry vanilla) are all atrocious. I've literally never tasted ice cream this bad. The salted caramel just tastes like salt, the cap n' crunch is crappy soggy peanut butter mush and the cherry vanilla just tastes like a bad imitation of Ben and Jerry's. The worst by far is not using the berry cap n crunch. Holstein's and Momofuku is much better.

Meeeeeh! After a tasty and delectable dining experience at Scarpetta I suggested we walk right over to Milk for a post dinner treat. All 10 of us ordered something, you're welcome Milk.... Soft Serve was okay but oddly very salty and I am normally a salty cat. In fact, so were all the cookies we picked up (Double Chocolate and Compost cookies). I bought 2 Blueberry and Cream cookies but gave them away to friends so I couldn't tell you how those were but also didn't get any feedback from those I gave it to. So letdown by Milk and the $80 we spent on Soft Serve and Cookies. $80! Even the girl at the register was a little salty too. I will say that the Fruity Pebbles Soft Serve was the best because it had more dynamic flavor. Otherwise, I'm happy if we never go back. Glad we got to try it though.

I heard so much about this place, I had such high expectations... I ordered a chocolate cereal milk (milkshake) and it literally tasted like baby food, I couldn't eat it anymore... I had to throw it away. I felt like the people working there didn't know what they were doing. The place is overrated and overpriced, not worth it.

AmÃ©lie's is a favorite all day and night. Don't be surprised to come and find a line 20 people deep and then wraps around the corner. But don't leave! The staff does a wonderful job and the line moves fast. I've had sandwiches, coffees, teas, and lots of macaroons and other desserts at all locations. Yet this location was the first and is by far my favorite because of the decor. The macaroons are soft and delicious as they should be, they have some flavors year round with seasonal flavors. Tonight I had the pumpkin and it was so good. I bit into it before I realized I needed to stop and take a picture. The pumpkin e-something dessert was amazing! With a nice surprise of caramel falling out much like a lava cake. Yum yum yum. My least favorite was the sweet potato torte with pecans that my friend ordered. But I'm a huge fan of pumpkin. So if you prefer sweet potato over pumpkin like my friend does, then you will love it. The best thing about this location colors to the other three locations is the parking lot. There is ample parking. I also forgot to mention the larger patio which is also nice to enjoy and look toward the uptown skyline.
Place was little busy but service was fast. We got in and out with what we wanted. Would come back here again next time we are in town.
A must visit. Best butter pecan I've ever had! The staff was super friendly and we ended up taking pints home with us. Kids will love the Cookie Monster in more than one way .
Its hard not to order everything when I come here because its so good. You can also order on Instacart for delivery. They always get my order correct which I appreciate

This bakery deserves 5 stars! Everything is so reasonably priced and such high qualitty!!! Amazing customer service too. They have savory and sweet pastries. You grab your own set of tongs and help yourself. Make sure you check out the refrigerated case too - the caramel pudding and strawberry cake is so good!

Coffee and tea in a city that warrants coffee and tea - part 2 of 2 I admit to eating the same sandwich (the Vito - #5) that I always eat at Jimmy John's while I was in Pittsburgh, since there's a Jimmy John's located right outside the T (light rail) station in the city center. However, that was not going to deter me from wanting to find at least one more funky indie coffeehouse that offered either sweet or savory stuff to woof down along with a good cup of tea. This place wasn't recommended. I found it via a Yelp search. First, it's ButterWOOD. It's not ButterWORTH. Don't be coming here looking for pancake syrup. What it is (yeah, what it is, man) is the merging of a bakery and a coffee/tea shop. And the combination works. Let's get right to the desserts. They have traditional cakes, muffins, cupcakes, scones, and the like in various flavors. They are baked on the premises using healthy premium ingredients. In this way, they can satisfy all those health food crazed individuals via GF, vegan, and all those stipulations. For me, this can water down the potentially decadent (fine with me) taste of baked goods, but they were still very good. I also learned that vegan is pronounced "vee-guhn." I've always pronounced it as if someone was a Chevy Vega jockey. Then, this place, ButterWOOD, is hilarious on so many levels. They have bordello-like Victorian furnishings inside, complete with red velvet seating and those sorts of accessories befitting a whore house right out of the Wild West. It's in a funky area named Lawrenceville, which might have been on the decline in the past but the earthy-crunchy crowd has deemed it worth rescuing. Now, if earthy-crunchy types throw out attitude, and many of them do, I don't care for them. However, if they're affable and provide good customer service, I can overlook the demographic chasm. Here, the progressive employees and ownership are indeed nice folks. It is priced a little high. That's because they merge a specialty cake shop with the coffeehouse aspect. If not for that, ButterWOOD would get 5 stars. Maybe 4 stars is a better rating in this case because it aligns with the 4 word expression: "let them eat cake." It is a unique experience and their goods are good, so check it out at least once. I visited twice.

If you want fresh delicious coffee and possibly a tasty treat to accompany said drink, you've found the spot. I love stopping by Amelies in general but stop by often in the morning before work. I can always rely on the "two Emilys" for a good conversation and a delicious coffee beverage. Emily E and F thanks for all you do every morning! If it were up to me you'd get a raise!

Love this place for a quick, sweet snack. They have everything from cookies to cakes, just all things sweet and delectable. It's located under the escalators in front on the Venetian Theatre. Go ahead and get that something sweet and indulge yourself, it's Vegas after all.

We ordered a unicorn cake and didn't give Carlo's much to go on. They worked with the ideas we had and they hit it out of the park! The cake turned out beautifully!!! I am completely thrilled with the results and would not hesitate to recommend Carlo's to everyone. The service from start to finish was professional and beyond helpful. Thank you for helping make this a memorable 21st!!!

We were attracted by all the activity in Presti's Bakery in the middle of the afternoon during a visit to Cleveland's Little Italy. Even during that quiet time, we took a number that was 50 from the number being called and looked over the delicious looking baked goods on display. WOW! Pastries, cakes and an endless assortment of Italian cookies filled the display. We made our choices and took them to a delightful outside table with coffee. So many times we have made choices and been disappointed but not at Presti's. Everything, including the cookies we took along for the ride, was delicious and we only regretted not purchasing more. Great choice for dolci.

This place did not disappoint at all! I watch cupcake wars and purposely go to any of the cupcake bakeries in a city I visit- especially the famous ones. I love indicate and unordinary flavors such as lavender or chili chocolate etc. I found what I was wanting there! The plain flavors are there too. The cake was flavorful and moist and the frosting was the perfect amount. The whole store is organized perfectly and the staff was top notch. The boxes, the shirts, even the bags had the little details that matter too. Everything was like a little treat ... Just what a cupcake should be. Even the building structure was spot on in design. Going back tomorrow as the plastic bags will preserve the cupcakes for travel and they even include cupcake care instructions! Adorable.

Have you really been to Charlotte if you haven't been to AMELIE'S?! Amelie's sits perfectly into NoDa and is a definitive part of Charlotte's Art District. Walking in, you are welcomed with friendly staff and tons of quirky decor. Mismatched furniture adds to its fun vibes and makes an overall welcoming and great place to hang out, relax, or get some work done. Of course, the desserts and other edibles and drinks are always a delight and the vast arrangement is extremely pleasing to the eye and will make you want to buy more desserts than your body could take. The macarons are always a classic and I have bought tons for a party before and they are definitely a crowd pleaser! The salted caramel brownie is a classic favorite and one of my new favorites. The tarts are amazing and the espresso cake has the perfect dash of coffee. They also make cakes when you need one for a big event and the prices aren't too bad! If you haven't been to Amelie's and you live in the Charlotte area or you are visiting and don't know where to go, well girllllllll (and guys), this is it!

Ok, how adorable is this place? Parking is limited up front but there is a parking lot on the side with plenty of room. Walking in is like hopping back in time. It is a really cute little ice cream parlor. They have a bunch of fun nostalgic candy for sale too. My mom and I shared one of their seasonal freezes and it was so good. I am really glad we split it, they were nice enough to put it into two cups for us too. It was really good but also really sweet and I definitely would not have been able to finish one myself.

Tucked away in a little corner market is a cute little ice cream shop. When I first moved to Scottsdale, I didn't live very far from here and i could see myself walking over here to have lovely treats and often. Now, as you look for this place, don't blink, because if you do, you will miss it. It is not facing Miller Street, but faces the parking lot north of the building. (I did say tucked away...) I am not a person for sweets, but the kids that I took here LOVED it. The loved the optional toppings, specifically the marshmallow. I enjoyed the macarons! They were deliciously sweet and tasty. Return FActor: 65%

I watched Christina Tosi as a master chef judge and was curious to try her desserts. Although the hype for this place is good, the prices are outrageous, however the quality is better than other dessert places I been to. And for the size of the dessert, it's a no go for the price. I got the bite sized cookie dough flavored confetti and it was really good, it was one of their truffles. The others were the cookies and they tasted kind of like any other cookie but with a different flavor than your typical cookie. The three cookies ran for $11 and the flavors were confetti, marshmallow and blueberry. The cookie truffle was 7$ and you get three small balls. It was definitely an experience that will be remembered. Was it worth the price tag? Hell No! But was it worth the experience. Yes! I would say give it a one time try and call it quits. I wouldn't go back, but the dessert is very good. Service was nonchalant. The employee that served me was kind of boring and annoyed about the pandemic, but pretty much everyone is. They wore gloves as well as having a clear shield in front so you don't come in contact with the employee. It's a mess but it is part of history for us folks.

First time coming here, since I live in the PNW. My parental in-laws eat here often. Came here on a Christmas evening, slim pickings, I did get to snag a ham and cheese sandwich thing, it was delicious. Also got Thai tea drink. Definitely will eat here again
Neat little place. Very quaint, a touch loud, with some nice tasting snacks and treats. I would have no problem coming back again.

Tried this place after hearing about the hype. Had to wake up extra early so try all the flavors before they sold out. This was not worth the hype, we got a dozen doughnuts since we don't live in Vegas. The special doughnuts weren't anything special. The creme brulee didn't have enough filling nor did the other flavors. All the doughnuts tasted normal, flavors weren't special or "wow" about them compared to most normal doughnut shops. I've had better doughnuts in the east coast. This was such a disappointment.
A hole in the wall location serving up unique flavors of ice cream and sorbets. I had the Morning Mess and had a Fruity Pebbles macaron on top of that. Awesome sauce.

If you are in the neighborhood and like sweet food, this is a must try. Actually even if you don't like sweet food you gotta stop by. The pastries are so soft, yummy and fresh. The atmosphere is unique and people are humble and polite. If I'm in Charlotte again, I'm definitely stopping by even if I don't have time.

I'm pretty disappointed that I chose a cupcake without frosting. It appeared like it had frosting, but it apparently doesn't (the cinnamon sugar cupcake). A cupcake without frosting is a muffin! Additionally the muffin wasn't soft and spongy. Customer service was great.

Mmmmm Ice cream sandwich. This dessert is really great because it's really two desserts. I like that... a lot. So I went here this afternoon for 'dinner' and got the Vietnamese coffee ice cream between two chocolate chip cookies.... so good. It was a little salty and sweet and coffee -y... what more could I ask for. The BF got peanut butter ice cream with snickerdoodles.... also very very tasty. The thing is, the ice cream wasn't blow your mind awesome and the flavors were pretty ho hum.... I would definitely come back here if I were in the neighborhood, but I probably wouldn't make a special trip again.

One word, MACARONS! This place has been by far, the best Macarons bakery shop I've encountered. Although it's a little on the pricey side, I say 6 macarons for $17.50 is all worth it in my pocket. There about 7 macaron flavors total, which include: pistachio, vanilla, coffee, lemon, raspberry, chocolate, and one I can't seem to remember. All were my favorite except the chocolate and coffee. The vanilla one is extraordinarily delicious! I haven't tried anything else besides the macarons, but by the judge of it....it looks like everything they serve is definitely an A in my book. I've been hearing especially good reviews about their TKO. It's kind of a hidden place, it's right behind the escalators from when you first enter the Venetian through the parking garage. Stop by if you get the chance, believe me it's all worth it.

We were in North S-Dale last night for a poker game and lost on purpose so we could get to SR before it closed. Still great, still wish it weren't so far from me. I got a scoop of Mojito and a scoop of the ever-popular basil-lime. They were great together, the mojito is very minty and sweet. The Basil lime will kick you in the pants. Interesting how we always think of basil as a savory taste, but works so well in this sweet treat. Yum. Too bad it's not in a strip mall that has more going on so they could get more business.
