Talk about Ice Cream. Used to live in central Phoenix and it's one of my favorites. Now when in the area and it's warm out always enjoy some fresh ice cream. Look forward to my next visit. P.S the S'mores is amazing.

My god. Like, seriously, how did Madison get so lucky to have Batch in our lives?? If you can believe it, I lived in Madison for almost a year before trying Batch and now I am deeply regretful of all that time I wasted. But seriously.. The Gruyere croissants? I could eat one of these a day. The vegan caramelized onion foccacia? Just bury me with this when I pass on and I will live the best after life. On top of all the carby goodness, their desserts on unparalleled. I literally have not had a single one that I didn't like. Batch is the best, no doubt about it.

Absolutely the best customer service! I called 3 other supposedly great cupcake stores and no one answered or responded to my emails. Ashley was amazing and helped deliver cupcakes for a very special event. The competition needs to step up their game, Or not. I'll never go anywhere else.
The pumpkin cake with maple buttercream frosting was delicious. Looking forward to having the gingerbread tomorrow.
The butter pecan ice cream is heavenly and the waffle cones were amazing. I would definitely recommend this place for great ice cream.

Update: I came back and ordered the Cornflake Chocolate Chip Marshmellow cookie and of the three cookies I've tried there, it's my favorite. I took it to go and I wish I ordered a couple more. I love the texture of the cookie. It's chewy but has some crunch every now and then from the cornflake crunchies in it. And the taste isn't overly sweet which is what I liked. Get it. You can't go wrong :)

DRIPPS is my answered prayer and biggest blessing to the Chandler area this year. I'm not kidding when I say I come here at least once a week. When they first opened in September, it was even more than that, taking advantage of their soft opening and grand opening discount and BOGO. They are an awesome company, from the owners over at Pokitrition. The star here is CEREAL INFUSED SOFT SERVE. And no, it is not just some cereal just sprinkled into the ice cream. It is generous amounts of cereal of your choice literally DRILLED in and it is the best cereal ice cream in the world. I am a huge fan of Christina Tosi's Milkbar cereal ice cream, but Dripps takes it to a whole other level. I can assure you your favorite childhood cereal is among their choices. They do have signature creations you could choose from and mix and match toppings, but what I love to do is just choose a cereal and use the same cereal as topping. Their "supporting actor" I would say is their matcha drinks. If you love matcha, you will be in heaven. They use real QUALITY matcha. Great flavor, good caffeine kick without the jitters. Next favorite is the rose milk tea. It's not too "flowery" it is more milky which I love. Their milk teas are good as well. The only one negative thing is the boba balls are not as soft as I would love them to be but I enjoy milk teas without boba so they get a pass. The whole concept is just amazing and I'll shout it from the rooftops if I could. I LOVE DRIPPS!

This would have been a 3 star review but the strawberry cheesecake cupcake didn't taste anything like strawberries! We purchased 2 cupcakes that being the first and a salted Carmel one being the second. The salted Carmel was pretty good the cake was nice and soft but way over salted. The cheesecake one only had flavor in the frosting and it wasn't strawberry that's for sure. The girl helping people with the ice cream etc was very nice, friendly and outgoing. The girl at the counter who rang us up seemed like she might have been nice but kind of flighty. We got our cupcakes to go sit outside at the table since there was no where to sit at the inside. She put the cupcakes down on the counter in a box turned her back and that was it. Luckily I noticed next to the register was some wooden Popsicle stick looking thing which I hoped was a knife to cut the cakes in half and luckily it was. Needless to say I will NEVER give this establishment any of my money again. Oh and did I mention they were just a step above Albertsons and definitely way below the Hershey shop and Nothing Bundt Cakes.
Terrible. My friend and I both found small black hairs in our sandwiches. I have long brown hair and she has long blonde hair. Ewwww. Never going back.

Small shop with a lot of variety. They have a lot you can park in and a couple of tables with benches outside. Inside is just the baked goods, no area for seating. Baked goods: ranged from cake slices, macarons, to pastries. We shared: - lobster tail: crunchier than I expected but I enjoyed it a lot. The cream filling is light, airy, and not overly sweet. Together, my husband described it like eating cereal. With the almost milky creaminess from the whipped cream and the crunchy pastry shell - New York crumb cake: was worried the crumbs would be the only good part but the cake is very moist and good! Overall a solid cake - horn (strawberries and cream): my least favorite, the pastry tasted undercooked. It was almost good. The filling seemed like it was just packaged strawberry cream cheese.

Love the crew that works Churn. Always happy and so patient...even when you want to try every flavor! I'm a creature of habit so it is very hard for me to stray from the Vietnamese coffee ice cream - single scoop - in a bowl. I have ventured into the Ice Cream cookie sandwich game. And let me tell you these babies are for sharing. You can either have cookies as your sandwich or they have brownies. Go big or go home....choose the brownie! Also a favorite of this spot are all the classic toys and candy options displayed on their wall. Definitely a spot to walk in enjoy even if you choose to not partake in all the goodies!
Cool to watch being made, almost like an art. Ice cream was pretty good. Great post-dinner place, ambience was nice. Good for couples or a small group.
Worst sfogliatelle I have ever had; they are way too thick with little filling .. and are outrageously priced. Better get them at Siena's Trattoria

Okay, I still love this place, but I have some new input that I think is worth sharing: Desserts here are still awesome, I think. Not really cheap but totally worth it. Really great variety and they never seem to be out of what I want. I have never been let down by the sweets. However, kind of meh when it comes to dinner. I had gotten veggie stromboli in the past but they were out when I went this weekend.. They were also out of basically everything else that I wanted (Friday around 6 pm so I kind of get it but was still disappointed). Ended up getting veggie pizza. They warmed it up but gave it to me basically still cold. Also got a side salad that was pretty whatever. Basically - go somewhere else for dinner. Maybe grab lunch there but I was just unhappy that I picked Presti's for dinner. Come by for sweets after dinner, though!

Dessert here is the best! Though mostly what I get is the cereal shake and it's an accustomed taste but when you like it, you really like it! Always something I pick up when I come to Las Vegas for a vacation! I do wish they had more available but it's best to come earlier than late haha
One time is enough for me. Place is all hype. Taste wise, other bakeries or homemade ones can be better. They are instagrammable, but they don't click to me palate wise. My opinion.

This is a very tiny but tasty place. I had the "almost famous" cookie cup. I chose the banana peanut butter ice cream with a caramel macaron. It comes with a toasted marshmallow on top of the macaron. It's not a "jet puff" marshmallow either, so it's better. You get the cold creamy ice cream, the warm toasted pillowy marshmallow and the "crunchy with a good chew" macaron. If I wasn't on a diet I would have eaten 2 of these. #worthit We also had the honeydew green tea. It was just the right amount of sweet. The green tea wasn't an overpowering tea. It was a cup of fruity perfection. Y'all need to check this place out. I'm not normally a huge ice cream fan but this is one place you absolutely cannot miss. Sooo tasty omg

Saw the lineup and almost drove away. But then decided that it must be good if the line was that long. Glad we went because it moved quickly. Before we got inside, we could smell the waffle cones they make in house! Get the waffle cones!!! We decided that this was the best ice cream we have ever had. I had the brambleberry crisp scoop and the brown butter with almond brittle scoop in a waffle cone cup. My girlfriend had the salted peanut butter with chocolate flakes and salted caramel in a waffle cone cup. Id bet that any flavor is delicious! We will definitely go back for more.

Delicious dessert! Not quite like a French crepe but very tasty. We had the Super Crepe and the Chocolate Crepe. A bit of a wait for them to be made but worth it. Counter help fine but not super friendly, if you want a smile with your service.

You've probably heard of places to die for so this place is definitely a place to live for LOL :D In all seriousness, it's quite embarrassing that it's taken me this long to finally write a review for an amazing bakery that is probably the best bakery in my opinion in Charlotte. Okay so this place is kinda inconspicuous when I drove by because I almost missed it and its very possible depending on which direction you're heading in. When you get there it's only 1 customer allowed in the shop so there might be a line but you'll always see people carry boxes of sweet treats! That's always a good sign from the multiple times I've been here! Once I got it, holy guacomole! My eyes got big and my tongue started to salivate from all the goodies that were available. They had cookies, macarons, cheesecakes, cannolis, and so many different things. They don't do dessert small here, more like loaded! I was so shocked at how big the cookies were like it could be the size of your whole fist! I've gotten macarons, cannolis, cookies, etc. They are all amazing but the one thing I have to recommend getting here is the tiramisu and creme puffs that are out of this world! I have a big sweet tooth and love dessert but man those 2 knocked it out of the park with how flavorful it was. Not too sweet but just the right amount like goldilocks haha Price wise it was very fair and the ladies at the counter will help you if you have any questions with a great attitude! I would say take your time here and just a get a few things because it all adds up $$$ real fast and same for the calories lol I'd say make it a trip and try something new each time you're nearby and they surely will not disappoint! Parking-wise is super easy since it's an open lot but there are a lot rocks so heads up if one gets stuck in your tire. But yeah they're doing everything right and really are a diamond amongst the dessert places in Charlotte and are a MUST if you're in town! That's all now excuse me while I schedule my next trip here haha

Having watched all of Cake Boss and Buddy Vs. Duff, we were excited to finally get to try pastries from Carlo's. Unfortunately, we were very disappointed. The Lobster Tails were supposed to be one of Carlo's specialties. Two of us were splitting it but it was so hard it was impossible to cut. The filling had a good flavor but was a little runny. We also tried the Chocolate Fudge Cake, and it was just average. Maybe Buddy needs to consider some quality control.

Fun and charming atmosphere. The service is always good. Some of the lunch sandwiches are a little pricey but always delicious. I'm not thrilled with a lot of the desserts for the price. All the ones I've tried are just a disappointment. Too rich, or not as tasty as expected, and very pricey. One I do enjoy is the almond twice baked croissant. Drinks are all good and worth trying.

This place was alright if you needed a quick and semi cheaper breakfast place. Wife and I ended up getting a chocolate croissant and a ham and cheese croissant with a coffee and a latte. My ham and cheese croissant was warmed up and pretty good. Came with a coffee so it was about 10 bucks with their meal deal. The wife's chocolate croissant was pretty good too (but to me I feel like you could save a dollar and get a similar one from starbucks). That and the latte was like another 8 bucks or so. I wanted to try more things but I already lost a bunch of money playing craps that morning so had to cut my loses. I'll have to go back since that monkey bread was calling my name.
I really enjoyed my cereal milk soft serve, the cornflakes were subtly salty and complimented the milky ice cream!

This wonderful place was included in a Foodie Tour that my husband & I took while in Vegas last fall. Great donuts - we tried the French Toast, which was included in our tour. Enjoyed our donut on the patio out back. Glad that we found this hidden gem in downtown Vegas!!

I don't know why this gets so much praise. it's not that good. Maybe for people that don't have high standards, but I've yet to be impressed by this place. They are always packed though so someone must like it, but I really don't see it.

If you live in Charlotte or are ever in the area, please do yourself a favor and go to the Batchmaker aka the best bakery in the world! Every single thing I have gotten there (and it's been a lot) has been absolutely incredible! And the place is so adorable too - looks like you stepped in your grandmother's house. The Batchmaker is sure to satisfy all of your sweet treat cravings! No joke the best bakery I've ever been to! P.S. don't sleep on the draft latte. It's so good!
This place was fun and absolutely delicious. Quick walk from any of the downtown hotels. Staff was friendly and helpful. I have already recommended this place others!

We have gotten donuts there a few times, and its sooooooo good! I wish their hours were better, but man is it good when I can get it. The donuts always have a good taste, well made, and worth every penny you spend on them. My mother was the one that told me about them, and while I wasn't too sure about it at first, my doubts were proven wrong.

Thanks to Danny N. of West Covina, CA for giving me the 411 on this Hot and New business in Downtown Las Vegas! We don't have these fancy 6 inch donuts in Hawaii, so it was a fun discovery for me! We arrived at about 9am and the line was out the door, but it moved quickly since the workers are efficient, skilled, and friendly! We easily found metered street parking right in the front of the shop on Carson Avenue. I ran right in and was done before the meter maid caught me! Oh yeah for "free parking"! Donut Bar is a cozy place where the width of the shop showcases their eye-popping product. There's a row of stools along the counter on the far wall if you want to dine there. The colors, designs, and names of the donuts really intrigued me. It was so difficult to make a decision, but I finally settled on the Caramelized pineapple and the Coconut Dream. .. I'm from the Aloha State and I haven't seen a pineapple donut before. Mmm mmm... it was a delight! The Coconut Dream was even better because it reminded me of a Mounds candy with a thin layer of chocolate between the donut and the coconut layer. Yummy! Both donuts were $3 each. They did leave an oily spot on the wax paper that lined the box... and a bit of an oily feel in the mouth. The donut itself seemed a bit denser and less cakey in texture. I want to go back for the Mexican Hot Chocolate, creme brulee, chocolate bacon, and the Strawberry Split. .. (note: vegan options are available!) I heard that there is a Donut Bar in San Diego. .. oh oh...here we come!
First time here, and it was awesome! I came a couple minutes after they opened and it seems they were hard at work setting everything up, the display was jaw dropping.

Okay so after my last review of Ninety's about week ago for me (which I have removed to write this) I promised to give Ninety's another chance and did so. I can honestly say I still love there sandwiches, the 90's style names are great, I had the Carlton and the Uncle Jessy. They even changed the shop a little since my last review in the way that the sandwich menu is now out in the shop on a board like the Ice Cream and I was able to get a sandwich past 8:00 p.m. I'm absolutely in love with the thin mint cookie dough pops now that I've tried one, I'm in love with the regular cookie dough bits candy and it's like the bigger flavored version of one of those, so of course I love it. I even went back twice that day, which is how I ended up trying a second sandwich for a late dinner. I wasn't expecting to go back, but I ended up picking my friend/roommate up from her late class and then she complained about Charlotte not having any good milkshake places open... I wasn't sure where she got that, but I remember that Ninety's probably had milkshakes and decided to make a quackish stop there for her. They did have milkshakes and she loved every second of the frosting rolled milkshake. She's definitely a fan now and we will be going back.

I love the ice cream here. I always order thin mint -- which is great if you like a natural minty flavor. I've noticed it's actually cheaper to buy by the pint than the scoop, I'll have to do that in the future instead.

Excellent quality goods! Would highly recommend the soft serve Cereal Milk for the hot Vegas afternoons. The flavors gives you a sense of Saturday morning cartoon nostalgia. Don't be afraid to ask for a sample before ordering, staff are super friendly. Another great find!

Made the trek out from Gilbert, at the suggestion of some friends and oh my goodness am I glad I did! Many unique flavors of the most wonderful ice cream, that is then stuffed into a warm donut "bun" and topped with your choice of cereal. Holy yum. And the owners were fantastic. We will be back SOON! Try the Fat Elvis, you won't be disappointed!

I was expecting a little more from this place with more options. Maybe it was just the one I went too but wasn't that impressed with the selection of ice cream (or there lack of). Good nonetheless; however I guess I was just expecting more options...

I came to check this place out when wandering the Shoppes and seeing all the pretty, colorful pics of the macaron ice cream sammies. They were not doing the unicorn macaron ice cream sammie when I came in, so I decided to indulge in a Vietnamese Coffee Yum-ee Bun (I LOVE Vietnames Coffee so I figured I would love Coffee Ice Cream w/espresso infused condensed milk in between a warm glazed halved donut). I figured incorrectly. While good in theory, I just was not feeling this Yum-ee bun. The donut was not served warm, FYI, and I think for me personally the glaze + the sweetness of the condensed milk (I didn't taste any espresso flavor) + the ice cream (the coffee flavor was good) made it just way too sweet of a treat. I may come back and try one of their macaron ice cream sandwiches, if for nothing more than it makes a prettier insta-pic than the Yum-ee bun. Staff were quick & courteous and even though there was a line, I got served and was able to pay quickly.

MILK is good BUT sometimes its hard to justify the prices of the items. Cornflake Chocolate Chip Marshmallow Cookie: 4/5. My favorite cookie they offer. Too bad only the name is a mouth full. Their cookies are too small for the price IMO. But this one is yummy with a good balance of salty (cornflake) and sweet (everything else). Compost cookie: 2/5. Im not a fan of pretzels or potato chips in my cookies so its a hard pass for me. But it also has a "hodgepodge" of other ingredients such as chocolate chips, toffee chips, graham crackers and rolled oats. I usually purchase 6/$22 - which equals out to about $3.70 per cookie. Birthday Cake truffles: 3/5. Super duper sweet and prices at about ~$7 for a pack of three or four, cant remember. Crack pie: 3/5. Also super sweet and priced at about $7 for a slice.

The smell when you walk in is amazing! I brought home four different kinds of their amazing donuts for my family to taste...the chocolate bacon, cake batter, mud pie and French toast donuts. My favorite the French toast donut which was made to order, so hot and delish! The cold brew great too! I can't wait to bring my family.

Oh Mitchell's, how I love your ice cream! I particularly love the seasonal flavors that this place makes. On my most recent visit, there was an autumn apple ice cream on the seasonal board - a cider ice cream with caramel swirl and almonds, that I had as a caramel sundae. It was delightful. My only complaint is the amount of nuts used in the recipes - for those with nut allergies (not myself, but one of my friends who was with me), Mitchell's can seem limiting. He ended up with a scoop filled with brownie chunks that he was very happy with. Scoops are generous, the ice cream is rich & satisfying, and I have never been unhappy with a choice I've made at Mitchell's!

The best place in town to get your bread from. Most of the restaurants in Little Italy buy their bread here. Great pastries namely the Napoleon, crembrule and fruit tart. Everything else is great too, hot espressos and cappuccinos included, but it can get expensive...
This place was great! There were a ton of unique ice cream flavors to choose from, which were all amazing! Highly recommend this place if you're looking for good ice cream and great service.

My favorite ice cream shop in the country (over even Bi-Rite in SF and McConnell's in SB). The flavors range from classic to experimental (but nothing wild like what you might find at Salt & Straw), and each one is rich, thick, creamy and perfectly balanced. The waffle bowls/cones are perfection (never overcooked or soft and soggy) and the toppings are fantastic. The marshmallow is my favorite - toasted to perfection in front of your eyes, atop your scoops! It's worth a trek just to visit the shop. Love that it's also in the PHX airport now, though the selection is far superior in stores!
Best donuts I have ever tasted and I have tried almost every shop in town. Get there early otherwise you may miss out!

It's 41 degrees outside, not exactly the weather for ice cream! But when on vacation, and have the chance to try one the top ice creameries in the world...we will come, rain or shine! We ordered a BANANA SPLIT to share, three choices of ice cream. With 45 flavors to choose from, to select only 3 was daunting ! We finally chose, GRAHAM CENTRAL STATION--CHOCOLATE MALT w/ CARAMEL--and PEPPERMINT BARK. Three HUGE scoops of homemade ice cream, on a bed of sliced bananas, massive mounds of whipped cream, and the works of toppings! Not the prettiest presentation, but It was monstrously delicious! My husband prefers the purity of a single or double scoop, but because he loves me, he agreed to share this concoction! It fulfilled my banana split dreams! We ate the whole thing, and agreed, this was indeed world class ice cream!

The Melt was so cute! My friend and I were looking for an ice cream shop to get a sweet treat after dinner and couldn't resist when we saw how the Melt served their ice cream: in little Chinese to go boxes. It was so unique. They had unique flavors I'd never seen before. I can't quite remember them, but each had a Latin or Mexican influence on it. The prices were reasonable and the person who served us was welcoming and allowed us to try the flavors. Vibes in the Melt were relaxed and low key.

i got a vanilla confetti slice of cake and as soon as i got back to my room it was all gone because i instantly started eating. cant wait to visit vegas again cause ill be buying more than one slice next time

This place was okay. Prices are crazy expensive. Waffle cone was decent, but could've been fresher. The chocolate ice cream was really good. The cookie dough was bland. My husband really liked his two flavors. We also got a brownie and caramel apple to go. The brownie was pretty small and average for $5. The caramel apple was large, but the caramel was super thick and dark, which I didn't love. Also, I'm pretty sure $11 is by far the most I've ever paid for a plain caramel apple! In sum, I'd only come here if I didn't want to leave the strip and I'd skip the non-ice cream treats.
Cereal milk soft serve is what I usually get here when I'm at the Cosmo. I enjoy every crunch of cereal on my soft serve. It's the perfect combination.

Probably the best ice cream in town! There is a wait most times, but it is worth it. Coffee chocolate chip is my favorite but all of the others are just as good. I take my kids every weekend, it's our little treat to ourselves. Staff is friendly. They do have some benches so you can enjoy your ice cream right away.
I tried it out. I particularly didn't like it. The donuts were too high priced for what you got.

This place is just the cutest and I don't know how anyone wouldn't love it! I didn't get to stay when I went in yesterday, unfortunately, but I was able to snag a piece of their blueberry elderflower cake as I tagged along with a friend who was picking up a birthday cake for her boyfriend. I actually saved half of it for later which was a great idea, since the piece was rather large AND it was a lovely treat to look forward to. Amazing flavor and very moist cake. The icing is ...wowee. This would be a great place for some afternoon tea and dessert or a date night! Great music, lovely little patio, and awesome antique furnishings. I can't wait to try out some more delightful treats! The service was also very friendly.
The owners, and staff are extremely friendly and nice! I've been 3 times since they opened last week! The shakes are sooo yummy! I highly recommend the Cosmo & Wanda, and Scooby Snacks

Quick service, clean, and amazing ice cream and macarons. The cookie cup is a must have when visiting here. The ice cream, macaron, and toasted marshmallow is really a combination like no other. Each ingredient complimented the other. Already wanting to go back.

Came here because of the good reviews and delicious looking photos. There wasn't a lot of variety in either flavors or menu offerings. $4 is a lot for a single scoop of ice cream especially when it isn't very good. The chocolate flavor tasted sugary sweet, rather than having a rich chocolate flavor. The mint chip had a very strong after-taste that wasn't pleasant.

Hey Buddy... F You! When you charge $11 for a tiny slice of cheesecake you better be giving people the best cheesecake they had in their lives. That ship was the consistency of cottage cheese flavored like lemon. The cannoli barely had five or six chocolate chips in it, you cheap bastard. Save your money and go get anything from the supermarket at least that way they don't laugh behind your back as you're walking out.
The Bouchon Bakery had a variety of delicious treats. I had the variety of crossaints that they had and my favorite was the chocolate croissant, but the others were good too.

The place is clean and the staff were friendly. But: we waited for 15 minuets to get our order, and they were not even making ice creams to order as Jarlings does. I got the chocolate almond coconut and my friend got their lemon blackberry special. Mine was half melted when I got it! My friend's seemed better, but overly sweet! It seemed like they have mixed overly sweet blackberry jam with overly sweet lemon ice cream. It wasn't lemony and refreshing at all. We barely finished our expensive melted and overly sweet ice creams and left. Never going back.

My cousins Christina and Manny favorite spot, this place is amazing and delicious!! The donut melt is to die for with the banana ice cream and the cookie monster is out of this world!! (Warning it will turn your mouth blue ) give them a try and it's reasonable priced

Went in at a non-busy time. Two gentlemen working the counter completely ignored my family and we couldn't place an order. A family walked in behind us and was immediately served by calling the number system which clearly said was for busy times only and there was no one there else waiting to be served. Ok we grabbed a number and as soon as we approached the counter the other guy just left and went to talk to the other worker servicing the family behind us. We left without placing an order. The only conclusion I can reach is that they are racists that work at this store as my family is a mixed race family and the people behind the counter were white and seemed to be eager to help the white family who came in after us. Please be aware of this if you are thinking about trying out this bakery.

I feel like this place is a novelty, with very bad and overpriced desserts. I got a crack pie soft serve with cereal sprinkles as a topping. It was sweet, more sweet, and even more sweet. It was so sweet I felt like I was going to become a diabetic just from eating a tiny cup of soft serve. I ate probably two spoons and had to stop eating. I threw away the rest, as it was just way too sweet to eat. A friend behind me in line tasted my soft serve and decided not to order anything -- that was a wise decision. I also ordered a cornflake chocolate chip cookies, which was just like the soft serve, sweet sweet and more sweet. The cookies were already prepackaged in bags, and I'm not sure whether they are actually made on site. I asked for the cookie to be heated, which essentially meant they stuck it in the microwave for a couple seconds. It wasn't actually heated nearly enough. Oh, and did I mention that a tiny tiny cup of soft serve cost you six bucks, and a sprinkle of serial cost an extra two bucks? Totally not worth it. Go somewhere else.

This was my first time bringing my son. I adore ice cream and since we were in the area, I knew exactly where to come. The restaurant was busy as it was a busy holiday weekend and people were out enjoying the amazing 80 degree day. The restaurant was clean and it was really cool to see the big production in the kitchen of all the workers making ice cream through the various stages. Our ice cream was so good! The two single restrooms are gender neutral now, if you care about that. Shorter wait for me now as it used to be a line for the ladies and none for the guys. Courteous employees and amazing ice cream. Be prepared to spend $5 or so, but totally worth it.

The atmosphere and friendly service create a sincere atmosphere. As delicious as the many cookies appear in the well lit cases, they are tasteless. I am a baker and am consistently disappointed in the cute little nuggets of dough.

WOW it brought me flash backs of my childhood being in a candy store. One of the best selections of candy I've seen at $16.00 a pound but they did have a 25% off sale. They also have homemade ice cream that looked really good. It definitely worth going in and buying different candies you don't see everyday. Plus it's along the canals with Gondolas going past.

I'm only giving this place 4 stars because I'm in love with their crack pie. It is everything I want dessert to be...rich, sweet and decadent. Maybe it's me or my tastes have changed, but the cookies just don't hit the spot like they used to. Tried the crack pie soft serve this time around, but I dont think I'd order it again.

You hate to spend $8 for a slice of cake and not enjoy it. The people are wonderfully nice however the cake definitely fell short of expectations. I asked what type of frosting it was and they said buttercream; however, this is not traditional buttercream with a good flavor. The cake is not vanilla. It has a slight metallic flavor like something went wrong during the baking process and it was slightly over baked. I am very disappointed in the quality of this cake.

First I would like to begin by saying "TED is the man!!!" and 'TEd for PRESIDENT!". I guess you might be wondering exactly who "Ted" is. Well Ted works at Amelie's. He provides that type of customer service that is rare these days. Great listener and extreme professional!!! Last week was sort of a rough week for me. (Let's just say someone very close to be had a birthday on Tuesday and the anniversary of their death was Wednesday. Always two pretty rough days each year.) Anyway, do their best to try to cheer me up during those rough days. They know I LOVE the Vanilla Chiffon cake at Amelie's. When I got home from work I had roses, a cooked dinner and guess what?!! Yep. You guessed it! Vanilla Chiffon Cake from Amelie's!!! When it was time to enjoy my cake, I dug right in. For the first time in history, the cake was not good. I wanted to CRY! I thought about it for a moment. What was I to do? I have NEVER had anything from Amelie's that wasn't amazing. So, I took a chance and called. I was a little anxious because my mood wasn't the best and I was hoping not to get hassled. I called and "TED" answer the phone. He listened to my concern and immediately apologized for my dissatisfaction. He offered an immediate resolution that was beyond what I expected. (Remember, I have NEVER complained about anything at Amelie's so I had no expectations.) "TED" was pleasant, polite and attentive. At the end of such a heartbreaking day, "TED" provided a pleasant surprise. Might seem small to some, but he truly made my day! My daughter and I went back to Amelie's earlier this week and I had the pleasure of meeting "TED". I thanked him for the pleasant experience! He had no idea what he did for me that day, he was just happy to have the opportunity to provide superior customer service. He thanked me for my business and smiled as he welcomed the next customer. Ok, I was already in love with this place. But if Ted is the standard for their customer service, then I will continue to return. Amazing food AND amazing service? What more could you ask for? Get yourself to Ameilie

The Chocolate Shoppe provides quintessential Wisconsin ice cream. As they fully claim, it's not health food and not meant to be taken as such. It's simply good ice cream of a wide variety of flavors. They also have malts and ice cream sodas, as well as coffee. Basically, a great place, and an absolutely necessary place during the hot summer months.
Love jack frost ! We order from here often! Kiddos love it as do we ! No complaints !

Cute downtown location right off Grand Ave. I had heard a lot about this ice cream shop so I wanted to try it out. The shop is in a little cabin house type of building and I can probably say there is about 4 more business in separate little houses. Once you open the door you notice how small it is and probably has a max of 5-8 inside at a time. We were greeted as soon as we walked in and the guy serving the ice cream was very polite and explained to us the different options. He also told me that the ice cream was made by a vendor which really made great ice cream by batch. The Ice cream we decided was creamy and delicious and most definitely will return very soon!

After hearing about Milk & their looong lines in New York, I was excited for it to open in Vegas at the Cosmo. It finally opened in late December & I was able to see what the "hype" was all about. We got a slice of the Crack Pie, cereal milk soft serve with cornflake toppings & crack pie soft serve with cornflake toppings as well. I spent $20 for these three items. I also was confused about the toppings & thought the cornflakes already came with the soft serve but I was wrong. However, they were nice about it & didn't charge me $2 for the two toppings ($1 per topping). I tried my crack pie soft serve first. My first bite was good with the salty cornflake topping mixed with the super sweet soft serve. But after a few bites, especially when I ate all the toppings already, it wasn't that great. It was also messy to eat since they overload the soft serve onto a mini cup so be prepared with extra napkins or wet ones. I didn't even bother finishing my soft serve since it wasn't worth it anymore. Next, I tried their crack pie. I've read reviews on yelp about how good it is; however, when I took a bite, I wasn't impressed. There was nothing extraordinary or good about it. It was cold & mushy. It didn't taste like anything, tbh. I wish I could say Milk was amazingly good & too die for. But I would be lying if I said it did. It was disappointing. Maybe the original location in New York is waaaay better than this one.

Inconspicuous from the main road, I'd say this shop is a gem for the community especially transitioning vegans or vegans with a sweet tooth! Entering the shop is like going into a calm oasis. I loved the minimal, earthy, yet chic vibe. While no one was visible upon entry, I was still greeted almost immediately by two smiling faces that came from the back. With a perfect amount of options, this place has something for everyone, cake and yeast- based doughnuts with great flavors (both common and unique). The cookie butter is a cream filled doughnut and I appreciate the crumble on top. I love the passion fruit doughnut, but think it could've done without the sprinkles. However, they didn't detract, just didn't add to it. I'd recommend adding a fresh fruit like slices strawberries or blueberries if want to add color. The blueberry doughnut was a cake doughnut and familiar to taste, so good. Lastly, I went out on a limb and tried the lemon lavender and I must say it was magical! Sometimes less is more, and I think this spot has unlocked something great. IMO def better that Jack Frost and a contender with Duck Donuts. Thoroughly pleased and quite impressed. Vegan done right!

This place is worth it. The cup cakes are delicious. It was my birthday and we got the Dark Chocolate and Red Velvet cup cakes and it was yummy. The cup cakes are perhaps one of the best I have ever had.I also tried the fudge brownie but that was okay. The staff is very friendly and patient. They have birthday candles (50 cents) and also have a Happy Birthday sticker. I also loved the fact that they have small cup cakes for pets (dogs) too. LOL. Overall, a nice cute place among the hustle at Las Vegas strip.

I make an excuse to come here at least once every couple months, especially if a friend is in town visiting or if it's a date night and we're looking for dessert. This flagship location of Amelie's is by the far the best one in Charlotte. I remember when it was the only one, actually, and it was so packed you couldn't even find a parking spot. There's always still a line though so you KNOW they've still got it. Amelie's is decorated with eclectic furniture and decor, from quirky chandeliers to smashed Parisian plates on the wall to bird cages to a Van Gogh cutout by the door with a Santa hat for the holidays. Open 24/7, the French-themed cafe has everything from desserts to salads and juice. Everything is fresh, right down to the raspberries atop the merengue tarts (and we all know how fast raspberries go bad!) The dessert cases offer tons of options, up to 15 flavors of macaroons at once, even multiple flavors of eclairs, creme brÃ»lÃ©es, and fruit tarts. I stand there like an idiot every single time I come because I. Want. To. Eat. EVERYTHING here. There's something for everyone here, even if you just want a coffee. The staff is incredibly kind and patient with the long lines and patrons (sometime myself) who just need a minute to decide. They offer great recommendations and are incredibly knowledgeable about ingredients, flavors, and cooking and baking methods of everything they have to offer. Amelie's is hands-down the best dessert spot in Charlotte for its atmosphere, service, and sweet treats. *Pro tip: they offer one free eclair on birthdays!

One thing that makes this place special is I think the way the market is great. They focus on having different items on certain days so people want to try all the different things here. One thing that's cool is where they cut the top off of a cupcake and put ice cream inside and put it back on so it's a cupcake ice cream sandwich. Cupcakes are really good and haven't tried them all but my favorite is the banana and the brown sugar praline and of course red velvet. One thing I hate are the lines here.other than that it's great "Cupcake ATM" it's nice to have this option if you want a late night cupcake when it's closed.

So Handel's changed their cup design for their hot fudge sundaes. The cups are now designed to hold them in your hand easier but there is definitely less ice cream in them. Yet they still charge the same price. Not cool.
Always a classic town favorite. Whenever I have new friends come visit, we always go to jarlings

How cute was this place! I had a scoop of Salted Butter Caramel and a scoop of their Coconut Sorbet. Both flavors were awesome. I met the owners and they were very helpful and genuinely hard working. Basil Lime Sorbet? Surprisingly after sampling it, the flavor worked. I love trying non-traditional, thinking outside of the box flavors, and this Artisan ice cream joint is definitely getting it right.

I stopped by Sinful Sweets this past Thurs. at 7pm. I'd had Sinful Sweets bookmarked for a long while, but this was the first time I received the chance to stop by, given that they close at 8pm. Usually, if I'm downtown at this time, I'm headed to a show in the Cultural District, and am not quite ready for dessert yet. This time, however, I was headed back from a vigorous paddle at Kayak PGH, which allowed me to justify stopping by to indulge myself. In checking out the reviews beforehand, it seemed that the most popular items at Sinful Sweets are milkshakes and cake pops. Upon perusing the display case, there were surprisingly few cake pops left, so I decided to go with a milkshake ($5). The guy working (probably the owner) told me that the price included one mix-in (others are extra), and that I could have my milkshake made from two different types of ice cream if I wanted. After perusing the options, I ordered a milkshake with chocolate and cannoli ice cream with Andes pieces as a mix-in. My custom milkshake turned out to be a delectable creation. Its size and thickness were comparable to those of milkshakes from the Milkshake Factory, and the cannoli ice cream lent a nice creaminess to it in combination with the chocolate ice cream. Numerous small chocolate chips from the cannoli ice cream, as well as the Andes pieces, lent textural interest to the milkshake, culminating in a delicious pile of candy at the bottom of the cup for a sweet finish. Although Sinful Sweets doesn't stock as many different ice cream flavors as the Milkshake Factory, their milkshakes are more customizable if you account for the ability to mix flavors and the candy mix-ins, and they use the same brand of ice cream (Perry's). As was mentioned in a relatively recent review, I didn't receive a chocolate dipped straw, so perhaps they've stopped the practice of dipping straws in chocolate (I didn't ask). In addition to my milkshake, I received a dark chocolate dipped pretzel for checking in on Yelp. This was a nice bonus, esp. since I accidentally left behind some chocolate peanut butter dipped pretzels that I purchased last weekend at my parents' place, which were promptly devoured by my dad before I could ask my parents to ship them to me. :-( Overall, I was quite pleased with my visit to Sinful Sweets. Service was friendly, and the price of the milkshake was right in line with the Milkshake Factory. As others have mentioned, they have a daily milkshake happy hour during weekdays from 4-6pm (25% off), so if you're able to take advantage of it, you can get a milkshake for even less money. While I was very pleased with my milkshake, I'm not awarding a full five stars because of the lack of cake pops (I heard the owner explain to another customer that they were sold out because someone had made a large purchase of them earlier). However, this could be a good thing, as it gives me motivation to return and update my review! 4.5 stars.

Consistently great ice cream! They rotate through flavored frequently, so always a reason to come back. I would say this is easily a top 2 ice cream place in Madison, a pretty competitive ice cream town.

I would give this place zero stars but I didn't have that option. First of all, who pays $5 for a single scoop of ice cream?? When he rang me up with that scoop I literally thought I was paying for a free sample. Not worth my time or money. Never coming back.
The donuts were awesome! Great there early the sell out fast We got the nutella donut it was amazing

Long before visiting this bakery I had heard great things about the their Italian cream cake and a few months later I experienced a slice during a work event, and many months later I was able to visit the bakery. I must first say that the Italian cream cake is amazing with 3 layers and a creamy icing. The location is small but completely filled with all types of desserts and as much as I wanted to try a little of everything, it was just too much. I have such a crazy schedule during the week I love that they stay open late unlike some bakeries. On this trip I was able to try the fudge brownies, pound cake and the amazing oatmeal raisin cookies with walnuts, and everything was really good and there is still so much more to try but I would like to try the red velvet cake on my trip.

Good place for early morning pastries. Even though it's a Thomas Keller venture, the pastries were good but not French Laundry level. Their Almond Croissant was flavorful and flaky without being too buttery. Price is reasonable. Their coffee was nothing spectacular and something that will get you through the morning. Their macaroon was slightly bigger (about double the size) and their vanilla macaroon was good and light but the filling could've use a hint more vanilla extract.
May be the best ice cream in Las Vegas. Butter pecan is the best I've ever had. Expect a line, especially on a hot summer night. Tuesday still offers the $2.50 special.
Great service and ice cream. I HIGHLY recommend the apple pie milkshake. Absolutely delicious.

Came here the other night after the Naked & Famous concert at the Brooklyn Bowl. I love how it was still open too. I tried Sprinkles before in La Jolla and wasn't find of the red velvet cupcake but I am willing to give them another shot with their other flavors. When we came in weren't anymore cupcakes (except for maybe like one flavor) so me and my friends went for the ice cream. They serve different flavors most days. I know everyone been hyping up the red velvet ice cream paired with the red velvet cone but I just wasn't feeling red velvet that night. Luckily they had pistachio so I ordered a scoop of that in a cup. My friends ordered coffee flavor and the red velvet. ALL of them were good. The coffee flavor was strong but delicious. The red velvet had bits of cake in it and I enjoyed that as well. But man I REALLY loved that pistachio! They used real pistachio nuts in it too and they were not greedy with it. I think the entire time I was mostly picking out the pistachios lol. It tasted very rich and creamy, like buttermilk or something. I just wanna go back for that pistachio! I can't remember the price but for all three of us (2 cups, one scoop each plus red velvet ice in a red velvet cone) came out to be around $12 something. Not too bad but since they didn't disappoint me, I'd say it was worth it. :) Next time I go, I'll give their cupcakes another chance to redeem themselves.

Worth the long line and high prices. Crumb cake, carrot cake, and strawberry shortcake were out of this world. The line was about an hour when we went. They need to speed up their process which is why I couldn't give 5 stars. And unfortunately we didn't run into Buddy.

So I finally got the chance to try Sprinkles. It was the Saturday of EDC week and we were came to the Linq to return something when I saw the Cupcake ATM and thought, well why not. I went over to check it out and it looked super sun damaged, so we went inside instead. It was so hot outside we ended up getting ice cream first. I decided to get the capt crunch and salted caramel. They were kind enough to offer a taste of the salted caramel before they served it. Something about it being really salty. So I tried a little and just decided to go for it. I also ordered a red velvet cupcake to go. We grab what seats they had and just started crowd watching. As i said it was EDC week and all the color outfit were out and getting ready to get on the shuttle. It was nice to sit inside with the ac and just grub on something cold. We grabbed the seat in front of the cupcake side. There were only 4 seats inside. I would think they might want more.. They have tons of seats outside but who wants to sit in the sun and have your ice cream or cupcake frosting melt. Not I. After finishing part of my first scoop i deiced to dig in on the salted caramel. I realized after a couple bites why they had me try it. It gets saltier as you eat more. I finished the capt crunch with sprinkles but not all the salted caramel. I want to go back on a day the have lemon available. They only have certain flavors on certain days which i think is pretty cool, unless you go on the wrong day. All in all when I'm at the Linq on a hot day I'll defiantly run in and grab ice cream and maybe a cupcake to go.

I had a craving late at night like most of us do, I thought I'd look around for ice cream other than your basic ice cream stores like Baskin robins or Yogurtland. Found this place and give it a try, I ordered 4 different flavors ( Oreo, Coffee Chip, Black Cherry, and Vanilla) just to see what they were about. My absolute favorite was Black cherry followed by coffee chip, it reminded me of the Thrifty ice cream I used to get, but with so much more natural flavors. If your on the west side of Las Vegas, this place is a MUST!

We were staying at the Cosmo but even if we werent, we would have made the trek to try Milk Bar after watching the Netflix special. We tried various menu items: - The BFC - it was very rich but the flavor was well balanced - The perfect 10- this cookie was a little bland but still tasty, would be good dipped in ice cream. -The gluten free cake ball truffles- FAVORITE thing we tried, very flavorful and moist -My boy friend tried the crack pie and said it was okay but did not compare to the cake balls. The next morning we went back to try the fruity cereal milk ice cream and it was very good as well. We topped it with more fruity pebbles and sprinkles and loved that they also put toppings in the bottom of the cup so there was more left when we got to the bottom :)

Stop by here around 5pm, there was a long line approximately 25 persons at the front of us, no sure why the line was so long. I decided go to check out what they have when my friends waited in the line, I noticed the lobster croissant with cream inside, cheese cake....etc. If you keep eyes in your calories taken during day, you should NOT come here. Also their cakes aren't cheap. End up I didn't buy any because the cakes aren't healthy making and too much fat.

Decided to stop by Page Dairy Mart for the first time ever last night after a Riverhounds game and WOW am I glad we did - it completely lives up to the hype! We arrived and parked in their unassuming parking lot and got in (the very long) line. It was pushing 10pm and we were nervous about whether or not we'd be served before they closed. Amazingly, he incredible staff in PDM served every customer until the line was over. They were SO gracious and kind and they deserved every tip on the planet for being so awesome, in spite of the late night and the long long that remained at 10! By the time we reached the front of the line I decided to try the famous chocolate chip cookie sundae with pecans. When I say this was the best ice cream treat I've had in SUCH a long time, I mean it - an incredible warm cookie, delicious custard-y ice cream, hot fudge, and salty nuts? It was every bit as delicious as I hoped for, and again, the staff put their all into making great quality products despite the lateness of the evening. I'm so impressed and truly cannot wait to return. My husband (who enjoyed an enormous soft serve cone) said "it's a good thing we don't live closer, otherwise we'd be there every day." He's right - but that doesn't mean we won't be back as soon as possible!
I have only been there once, and I was disappointed. They didn't have any macaroons, and the ice cream looked sparse.

OMG!!!! I'm so glad I tried this place!! I purchased a cheese danish and chocolate almond croissant. Both items were crunchy, flaky, perfection!!! This is definitely a must try when in the Venetian!!!

Decor: 4/5 -If you want cupcakes, take the left door. If you want ice cream go to the right door. -There are seating outdoors dedicated to Sprinkles customers (though I see In-n-Out patrons eating at those tabes) Service: 4/5 -One person at the front which is the bottleneck to the increasing line of people waiting to satiate their sweet tooth Cupcakes: 4/5 -My favorite hands down is the triple cinnamon sugar cupcake. The red velvet, cuban coffee, dark chocolate were also good but wasn't a one hit wonder like the triple cinnamon. I would come back again to try the other flavors and even their ice cream and cookies

If you are staying in Venetian, you are in luck. Located right outside the elevators to the hotel tower and just opposite to the phantom theater, this is the best place to grab breakfast pastries and dessert. Bouchon Bakery is known for their French Macarons. Come here early if you want the freshest and puffiest cookie of love. Unlike many macaron shops, Bouchon only offers half a dozen flavors at a time. I often find their regular flavors better than their seasonal ones. Cafe, Chocolate, Vanilla and Pistachio were all very consistent among different locations. Nothing makes me happier than having a sticky bun for breakfast. I like their version here more than the one from the famous Flour Bakery in Boston. It is lighter but puffier and perfectly layered with nutty pecans. Do come here early for the best selection. Popular pastries tend to sell out quick.

although they do not have the "macarons as big as your head" like they do in the Yountville location...they still had macarons!! We bought the pack that had 6 in them with an assortment of flavors. They were absolutely amazing and i would love to eat them every day of my life. Now chubs from Bouchon would be worth it!!!

I'm always here to study and usually I will get a latte or macchiato while I study, but yesterday I tried their Belgian waffle for the first time, and it was so yum! If you haven't tried it yet, I highly recommend you do :)

Very mediocre...it's all just hype from the show. I was so excited to try their lobster tail after watching the show and was so disappointed. The cream inside was good but the pastry itself was so hard and dry. They were also out of half the pastries. Did I also mention that the lobster tail was $7??? Save your money and go to any other bakery than this place. I still love the show and am happy to say that I don't need to try his pastries anymore.

We got the kitchen sink sundae and shared it! Super good super delicious just be prepared to pay $8 for a Sunday. All the candy they had for sale was from my childhood! Very cute place. We sat outside on the back patio which had a very nice ambiance.

Great variety of flavors that taste absolutely amazing!!! I highly recommend doing the 4-scoop sampler to get a variety. Only downside is waiting in a long line (we waited about 25 minutes on a weekend evening) outside in the heat and then having to eat your ice cream as quickly as possible before it turns into a puddle. But I'll be going back again and again...

Sweet Republic is a dandy little ice cream joint - sort of in between a B&R (lots of flavors) and a Cold Stone (I don't think they do mix-ins at Sweet Republic?) Anyway - 2 good reasons to go right now. 1) The waffle cones - lighter, more crisp and delicate than most, with cinnamon, I think? 2) Mayan Chocolate ice cream - chocolate, cinnamon, and chile flavored ice cream - yes, please! It's hot and cold and spicy and sweet at the same time - wow!

What delicious treats they have. This bakery is known for their s'mores brownies but their oatmeal cream pies and puddle cookies are truly to die for. I do wish the opening hours were still 7am so I could stop there before work but that will just make when I can get there that much more special. If you're lucky when you go you'll see the owner Cristina who is so sweet!

Overrated soft serves, shakes, and cookies. Their marketing team definitely deserves some recognition though. Everything from installing those ig worthy neon lights/ signage to choosing the prime location inside Cosmo. Great work to those guys. At the end of the day, save yourself the $ and head over to McDonalds instead!

You just cannot beat a good cupcake! I've been to Sprinkles in NYC previously, so I knew what I was walking into when we found this spot on the strip. What a fabulous little store front, I wish they all looked like this. Service was quick and curteous. Instead of just a regular red velvet, I opted for the sundae and was not disappointed. The ice cream was incredible, honestly wasn't expecting it to be that great. Vanilla really balanced nicely with the red velvet. This however was dinner. I wouldn't recommend going if you already ate- it's quite filling and after eating that you'll be feeling like the ultimate fattie. Be sure to take a nice long stroll down the strip when you finish :)

Mixed Berry Tart is my favorite, you might as well get the regular size. The mini is a tease! If you are in the mood for a more savory dish their leek soup is amazing, I have traveled just to pick up a cup of soup before. Their atrium is a safe haven for studying. Sometimes their is music playing from various groups practicing.

You wait for hours because the service is slow. They don't mange the lines that well so people sneak in. I waited only because I wanted a cannoli and at noon when I entered they were out! If they are so popular they should bake more or at least post a sign saying they are out. I was very excited and now I'm just disappointed. When I watched the show they seem like a nice family run place now it's clearly all about the money. Good places like this loose credibility when they expand just to make money.

Massive menu with a lot of great options and huge portions. I am a fan of the Cookie Sundae (soft serve, hot fudge, fresh warm chocolate chip cookies, whipped cream and nuts) or the Blondie Sundae (same deal as previous, but blondies instead of cookies). My son is a big fan of the dip cones - soft serve dipped in a flavored sauce that forms a hard shell. He often orders based on color - with blueberry and cherry being his favorites. And if the massive amount of ice cream options aren't enough, PDM also has surprisingly good food options. The line can get long and parking is limited, but fortunately the employees really keep things moving. Page Dairy Mart is a Pittsburgh classic and one of my favorite places for ice cream in the city.

I have been to this bakery ranging from times when it was very busy to when it was not busy at all. Regardless of the unpredicted chaos, the staff was always courteous. In terms of the bakery items, there was nothing there that really knocked my socks. I did try different bakery items around the country so I don't know if i happen to compare the different items unfairly. However, this is still a go to place for most people in the area especially the students. This place is a walkable distance from the University Circle, and the items are very reasonably priced. This place also has lunch items (which I personally did not try) and has a very large seating area.

The marshmallow cookie Ice cream dessert is awesome. Everything tastes great and it has a nice atmosphere. My only issue was that rap and r&b do not work as the musical ambience. It was crowded on my visit and it was noticeable hearing suggestive lyrics how it affected the general tone and mood of the other guests. I would consider matching the tone of the penguins and pink and green with a radio choice, perhaps local radio of some sort that is more broad.

Four words: free. cookie. dough. samples. But trust me - the cookie dough is worth paying for! I work a block away from this place and it is my go-to whenever I'm craving a little mid-day pick me up. They have unique cupcake flavors that are so beautifully decorated, they are the perfect way to be nice and make someone's day. Though be warned, you will probably have trouble keeping your hands off of them yourself. I honestly have to restrain myself from coming here more often.

Delicious ice cream - environment is friendly....little loud but not too bad. I had an ice cream cake there and it was tremendous! You can check out the area that they actually make the ice cream which is nice as well. Has a nice feel and temperature inside... And the entire building looks nice and clean. If I am ever in the area again, I'd love to stop by this place for a nice treat, again!

Delicious, high quality pastries! We got the pan au chocolate, cherry almond coffee cake, blackberry cream cheese butter cake, and monkey bread. Highly recommend going here. Still had great selection at 10:30am on a Sunday.

Lovely French bakery in the Venetian Hotel. Pastries are fresh and deviously delightful. European style sandwiches are very good too. Good quality bakery in a day where most are below standard. Love Bouchon Bakery!

I have to update my last review. The last review was when they were completely out of cookies and low on ice cream. I went today and OH MY. So delicious and I can't wait to go back and share the experience. I ordered Captain Crunch ice cream, a fruity pebbles macaroon and toasted marshmallow. DELICIOUS!

I stumbled across this place and figured a sweet treat would be nice. The staff was very friendly. They welcomed us at the door and offered us samples and told us a little about what they serve. I tried the oatmeal and blueberry cheesecake and my boyfriend got the mango tango. They were all delicious! They have lots of unique flavors and a wide variety of treats. Prices were a little bit steep but to be expected as ice cream shops can be a little costly. I'd definitely like to go again and see what other seasonal flavors they'll have.
Absolutely delicious. Lots of choices, some very unique. I loved the one filled different cookies in it (forget the name). The mint is very interesting - very fresh tasting.

Great tasting ice cream BUT expensive. 1 cone $4.50. The vegan option was a giant glop of slush. Nothing like ice cream at all and I've had a lot of vegan ice cream. Disgusting. Only a super small amount of flavors to choose from.

I'm not the type of pig that actively seeks out for Donuts in the morning (see what I did there?) but I enjoy it once in awhile...while they have great concepts and crazy creative donuts and items the excution of the finished product could be better as it let it dry. If Yelp had half star ratings this would be a 3.5/5.... I got the: Creme Brulee Donut: I guess all big foodies have heard of this minus me...but my friends showed me the video of it. Like I said, concept is cool but execution was ehhhh... Birthday Cake w/ Oreo: So it was a birthday cake inspired donut with an oreo in the inside...but again concept is cool but execution was ehhh.... Maple Bacon: I guess this was my favorite one out of all of them just cause they actually executed this fairly comparable to a lot of other Maple Bacon donuts... I just felt that a lot of their donuts were dry compared to the place they replaced (O Face Donuts).

A little off the beaten path but well with the trip! We got the crÃ¨me brÃ»lÃ©e, blueberry Meyer lemon, vanilla bean, s'mores, Nutella overload, and Nutella glazed. They were all amazing! Hoping we have time to head back before we leave. The staff was helpful and friendly! Would defiantly recommend!

Very slow service. As soon as I was up to order he immediately rushed me and started rolling his eyes as if I was taking too long to order 3 classic crepes. I handed him my card he slams it on the counter instead of handing it to me. Very rude and disrespectful stay away!

Working night shift is hard. It is hard on any schedule in your life; family life, mental and physical health, and especially sleep patterns; however, I have never heard the night shift manager, Emily, be anything but positive and encouraging during those long night hours. Going to Amelies during my night shift in Charlotte is the highlight of my night; the staff there is exceptional. They are always cheery, helpful, and extremely generous when it comes to keeping the LEO of Charlotte caffeinated for their night shifts throughout the city. Emily is always specifically positive and actually genuinely enjoys engaging her customers in conversations past the generic "how are you?" She always is moving around but will stop her hardworking routine to check up on you and see if you are doing okay. She definitely runs a tight ship; but it is apparent that everyone who works there respects her and knows she is the example to follow. 5 stars for the night staff of the North Davidson location. I highly recommend going there for a cup of coffee and genuine real conversation with some hardworking people.

I want to start off by saying I've never actually gone inside the establishment, but I follow them on Instagram and all the fitness models post epic cheat meals with these donuts. So~ when my friend went to Vegas, I made him bring home a dozen for me. Little did I know, a dozen would actually be 2 big boxes! It was totally worth making him lug it around though. Because these donuts were so bomb! We do not have anything like these in Philly. I mean a donut with a poptart in it?! Anyways, after cutting a piece of each flavor to taste them, I ended up freezing them because I couldn't possibly eat them all in one sitting, well I could, but I decided I shouldn't. Well let me tell you, have any of you guys tried frozen donuts before? It was probably even better than when I tried it fresh! How could that be possible?! Well some of the donuts were too sweet when I had it fresh (the poptart one especially) and when it was frozen it was the perfect amount of sweetness. I still dream of eating these donuts. I need to make a trip to Vegas.

Pretty good donuts. Very tasty and fresh. I'm not good at describing donuts, but I had one with white cream and another with chocolate cream. I came at about 3pm and the selection was very minimal. Actually this was the second time I visited. I tried a few days earlier, but they only had six plain donuts left. Supposedly they are open till 8, but they are all gone by early evening. Looks like the locals love this place. I'll try them again the next time I'm in the area and be sure to get there when they open for the best selection. Minus 1 star for the run down dumpy external appearance. Minus 1 star for lack of selection 5 hours before closing.

I went as soon as I read the article in AZ Central that they'd opened! Of course I went for the Halo-Halo, one of my favourite Filipino desserts ever. Their Special Halo-Halo had ALL the ingredients that every awesome Halo-Halo should have - coconut jelly, jack-fruit, flan, sweet beans, ube ice cream, etc. It tastes refreshing and delicious, and it's absolutely authentic. You get 3 generous scoops of ube (taro) ice cream too! Y-U-M. Aside fro the Halo-Halo, there are loads of various ice-cream flavors which I will have to try when I go next time. As an added bonus, the owners are super friendly and very welcoming. They've just opened, but if you go and there are tons of people, my only advice is just be patient. It's worth the wait!

This tiramisu is the best! Definitely one of the places I want to stop when I'm in Cleveland. The bakery is full of delectable sweets and appetizing savory meal options as well. Check this place out if you haven't already!

DOES ANYONE JUST WANT COFFEE?! How many times can you scream that at a line of people before someone jabs you in the eye? Really? Just help everyone in line patiently and with the best humor you can muster. (No one ever did just want coffee and she never did help anyone who wanted anything else) Besides that annoyance and the extremely long line itself, there was also the demand that we get in line when my mother and I were just trying to look at the menu board, and the young man who huffed and said "That's nice, now what do you want" when I explained we hadn't been to the property before and hadn't had a chance to look at the board. We were rushed through start to finish. The only saving grace was that the cakes were good. Not good enough to make up for that, though. Definitely not going back.

YUM. I tried the cannoli, lobster tail, & crumb cake. To be honest the crumb cake was very very hard like a brick. But the others were very tasty. As for the line we only had to wait about 10 minutes. We came around 4pm on a Saturday, today. The workers were also very friendly and talkative so that was nice. :)

I had Presti's cater an event for my residency program. For the dinner, we ordered 2 vegetarian stromboli, 1 sausage strombolo, 1/2 pan of meat lasagna, 1/2 pan of vegetarian lasagna, and 1 pan of salad. Overall, our experience with the staff was phenomenal. Our order was done on time, and the staff helped me carry the order out to the car. They also had receipts ready as I left. Ordering over the phone was easy, and every person I interacted with on the way was wonderful. As far as the food goes, overall, we were wowed. Lasagna: Excellent. Both the vegetarian and meat lasagna were a hit, and definitely fed more people than we thought they would. There was a great amount of cheese, and everything was perfectly cooked and seasoned. Stromboli: The meat stromboli was a hit, but the vegetarian strombolo was not the greatest. Don't get me wrong: it was good, but I probably would order something else off the menu; the inside was a bit bland, though it was well cooked. Salad: Pretty standard salad overall: Lettuce, tomato, olives, cucumber. Fantastic balsamic dressing that everyone loved. I will absolutely have Presti's cater another event, and I am excited to eat more of their delicious food!

This place is amazing! First off, they have some of the friendliest employees you'll find anywhere. I was so excited just going through and trying the different flavors. I felt like I was doing something far more special than just ordering ice cream. Maybe that's because it's so much better than just ice cream. I ordered the fresh strawberry, not made with any frozen strawberries which is a big deal, on a donut...yes a donut!! With Cap'n Crunch Berries. OMG!!! The donut is slightly warm, the ice cream was amazing, and the crunch added to the overall explosion of texture and flavors. The prices are very reasonable, almost cheap considering the quality and the experience. My daughter, who made her own special concoction, summed it up best when she stopped eating hers for a couple of minutes and said, "it's so good I don't want to eat it cause it will be gone". Highly recommend!
Some of the best ice cream I have ever tasted in life. NO JOKE
Best donuts... Hands down! I love donuts and this place has whilst favorites and other inventive choices. I highly recommend the maple bacon cinnamon roll.... To die for!

Hands down, the best donuts in Northeast Ohio. I grew up in the neighborhood and I didn't realize how lucky I was to live right next to such a special shop. It can be hard to get to, but it's worth the drive. They have a wide selection of options and prices that can fit any budget, event, or taste. It's always a great day when someone brings Jack Frost Donuts to the office/hangout!

Service was friendly-ish, prices are pretty high and was bummed that they weren't accepting cash. Cakes are nice, but wouldn't return for one. However, those peanut butter cookie sandwiches are amazing. Cookies are a little salty and have the right amount of crunch. The PB butter cream IS perfectly peanut butter-y. Bring those to any event and people will LOVE them and love you for bringing them. Would definitely return for more of these sandwiches in the future.

Ran across this company on Groupon, thought I'd try. Stopped in to get my box of assorted truffles to be told rudely by a girl that I didn't read the fine print and needed to give them 24 hours notice. I still asked if I could just get 24 assorted boxed from the the mass quantity all out in the open, she attempted to ask another co-worker who was too busy on her cell phone to help and looked back and told me no... ... 24 hours later I come back to pick up my chocolates hoping it would be worth the wait. Terribly disappointed. The centers are chalky and dry, and taste like pure sickening sweet sugar (not the good kind). They almost taste old, like they have been sitting out for days. Worst chocolates I've had in a long time; 2 out of 24 were good (peanut butter and birthday cake blue center).
I loved the ice cream, it was really good. Mitchell's Homemade ice cream has a verity of the best ice cream.
I ended up getting a grilled cheese sandwich and it was ok. Not anything special. The have a few pastries and things that you can get here as well as hot chocolate.

This place definitely has a lot of hype surrounding it, but I would have to say it is just another tourist trap. The lines are about 1-2 hours depending on the time of day and day of the week you arrive. I guess it is part of the experience, but for a local, I don't find that very appealing or any thing that I would want to do on a weekly/monthly basis. It took us about an hour or so to get in last night and when we finally did we were served by a very friendly set of employees. We bought a mini chocolate cannoli, a pastry called a lobster tail, a cheesecake, and a Carmel cupcake. The best of the 4 was the lobster tail, it is a crunchy pastry filled with a cream that was definitely enjoyable. The cannoli was very gritty and I will probably not purchase it again if I were to return. The Carmel cupcake was mediocre at best and not worth the wait when there are places that specialize in amazing cupcakes all around the strip. The cheesecake was good, but for $11 you can get that anywhere on the strip at a larger size and better quality. We always try these tourists traps as locals just so we can see if they meet the hype, but with the long wait and price attached to all we got, I don't see myself standing in this line again.

A must-visit when in Charlotte. It's a cute place that is way larger than you would think with quirky eclectic (and a little bit sarcastic) decor that gives the place a cozy feel. It's a little bit on the pricey side in my opinion so be prepared for that however I ordered a meal and 2 desserts: turkey bacon sandwich paired with spinach asparagus leek, a Napoleon and a hazelnut treat. All very good. It was all kind of messy but worth it. My only complaints are dirty tables and the Napoleon which was very good however it didn't cut/break easily and the creme just kinda squished out when pressure applied. I fully intend on returning and trying out more!

I had tried this whole cereal mixed with ice cream craze in LA a few months back and was so stoked to see it pop up in AZ! I'm a fan of boba and my girlfriend loves cereal and ice cream so we were excited to check it out. The best of both worlds. The shop is new - really cute and definitely hit the mark when it comes to an instagrammable vibe. Neon sign on the wall, pretty drinks, ice cream with toppings, they know what they're doing. I saw lots of photos being taken. Service was incredibly friendly. We were asked if it was our first time and given a quick rundown of both menus: the ice cream and the tea/drinks. I went with a 16oz milk tea and added boba ($.50). My girlfriend got captain crunch ice cream in a cone topped with strawberry and sprinkles. The milk tea was average and the boba was solid. It was a little too sweet for my taste. Other places will let you pick your sweetness flavor.. didn't get the option here but maybe you just have to ask? It wasn't bad but I'd probably stick to ice cream next time if I'm going to get a lot of sweetness anyways. That's just my personal preference though! They have some really pretty signature drinks (rose milk tea, some type of lemonade) so there are other options on that front. The ice cream flavor was spot on and really tasty. You get a large portion of ice cream so don't be afraid to share, and don't feel bad if you can't finish. There were a couple larger chunks of cereal on the ice cream that tasted a little stale but overall it was quite the treat. We will definitely be back again after they have been open a little longer to try more items.

This place was so good! Like omg best doughnuts ever! We bought a dozen doughnuts for $10.95. The salted caramel doughnut and the maple bacon doughnut was our favorites. Overall my whole family thought the doughnuts were the best we have ever had.
Great! Huge, delicious donuts and super strong cold brew coffee. They are only open for a few hours a day so be sure to get there early before they run out!
Really cool ice cream shop...I had the Vietnamese coffee and Cookies and Mint...pretty, pretty, pretty good...
Frustrated. Don't put an end time on Yelp if it's different from your door. Walked from California casino, arrived at 12:15 to find it closed earlier instead of 1pm. Just put on Yelp- to call ahead.

I feel like this place is overhyped. The first time i had it, my boyfriend bought me a box of different pastries and it was okay and expected more. Second time I ordered cake for his birthday and side desserts. It tasted stale and wasn't worth the price. Haven't been back since and i don't think I ever will.

When entering Mitchell's Ice cream shop, you'll immediately be greeted with an aroma of sweet fresh baked waffle cones and sugar in the air; so be prepared that you'll start salivating right when you enter. I finally went on the tour, it's really one large room to see, but they do go into the thorough explanation as to how their ice cream is made and all of their procedures that separate them apart from their competition. Their quality is on par with HÃ¤agen-Dazs. And they explain a bit about the family, the local location and local distributors. The art around the shop is by the Mother of the owners, Bea Mitchell. Cute place, excellent location, and most fabulous cookies and cream ever!

So after the amazing opportunity to eat these donuts at an elite event, I wanted to come by and see the selection in person. Early on a weekday, I stopped off and picked up 6 donuts for the secretary and I to share. This donut shop is gourmet and heightened flavors. When I brought home the extra donuts for the hubby and kids, they generally ignored them. I was disappointed, but the hubby said that the flavors were outside of the kids wheelhouse. I know that the place has kid friendly options on the weekend and the chocolate milk on draft will draw my little one in. So, maybe, I need to bring them in and let them pick their own flavor options. Here's what we tried. The dipped old fashion was eh. The Pop Tart was amaze-balls. Coworker and I took turns with the plastic knife as we cut off sections. The jelly inside is tasty. The frosting is perfect and not too much.
