However there was little and big chunks of chocolate and the mint flavor was not too overpowering. Delicious and creamy! I also had a scoop of the chocolate reeses. The chocolate base was delicious and the peanut butter and reeses to chocolate ratio was perfect. Ahh! I wish I had more. The ice cream was very expensive tho.For two very small scoops in a cone it was almost $9. It was worth it tho! The atmosphere in the store is super cute. There are a bunch of kids toys. The wallpaper and the chandeliers are super colorful. Sadly, it's a little hard to find in the mall-area. The signs don't help. We had to walk around twice to find it but I'm so glad we found it. Best ice cream in Vegas!

We purchased two puppy and each of them is more than 50 dollars, nobody tell us any thing before we made any payment, when we opened the puppy in their store and checked if everything was ok, and the other puppy was broken and we ask for a exchange, they told us there's no exchange, how ridiculous they are, we just get this product one minutes ago, and the employees who ever ran us up admitted that she never tell us that she explained their policy and she said that her fault, but they didn't do anything and their manager who looks doesn't know anything and just tell me it not her fault and without doing anything, useless!! Never go back to them because they have no service at all and their people just want the sale and push you out! The most important is be aware to their quality!

I really wanted to like this nostalgic place, but the service was terrible. The line (we had been forewarned) was long but quick. We got to the window and my partner ordered a medium cake batter shake. I ordered a Yintzer sundae and we stepped away to wait. The male who took my order called me back over and said they were no longer serving the Yintzer. I asked if they had anything similar and he said the chocolate chip cookie sundae was "basically the same thing, but with a chocolate chip cookie instead of a blonde brownie". No biggie-I ordered it. When we picked up our order at the window, the sundae had chocolate sauce instead of caramel. I told him I didn't care for chocolate, and that I thought it was supposed to be like the Yintzer? He said yes, you CAN get caramel sauce, but it's a special request. Huh? I asked for a Yintzer-like sundae, you affirm one exists then play semantics? He offered to remake it, but I declined and asked for a simple cone with sprinkles. He returned (several minutes later) with a plain cone. I asked again if he could put sprinkles on it? He did, begrudgingly. If I wanted to pull teeth, I'd have gone to dental school. Pass this "gem" up-it's a cubic zirconia. 2 stars because the cake batter shake tasted just like cake batter and the building is pretty cool.
Almond brittle and cream puff are on point!!! Nice, clean, bright atmosphere. Super friendly & patient staff. You can even get to-go pints - that's just splendid! Highly recommend for a sweet treat.

oh nom nom nom! :] I managed to force my friends to go on a scavanger hunt through Venetian for Bouchon! haha! It was so WORTH IT!! I'm slightly obsessed with macarons and when I found this bakery I want crazy! Their macarons are the size of my hand! I have small chubby hands and it covers MY WHOLE PALM! Not only that but.. the flavor!? oh gosh! It was so tasty and fresh! The bite into the cookie! so chewy! I love it! The price isn't bad either! Usually I'll spend $3 on one that's 1/3 its size! I bought three for myself (i'm not lying i'm obsessed). I should have bought more.. I'm going back next time I'm in Vegas!
Pastries are delicious. Employees are very attentive and patient. The environment, even during COVID, feel free welcoming while at the sam time they take all the necessary precautions. Lovey place

This is definitely a five star establishment with some of the best donuts anywhere. From their classic, timeless glazed to the newer bacon-topped and creme-themed donuts, this westside wonder should be added to the itinerary of any northeast Ohio trip. Of course they have a selection of hot coffees, too. Go early to make sure your fresh donut hasn't been snatched by... well, me.

I heard about this place on the Food Network, which highly recommends the Toffee Binoffi Sundae. Instead of getting the TB Sundae, I chose the oatmeal, chocolate chip, walnut cookie with 1/2 scoop of brown butter ice cream & 1/2 scoop almond butter crunch. Good combination! The only downfall was, the cookie tasted really salty. Other than that, it was good & I would try this place again.

The best thing about this ice cream shop are the different flavor selections. I had the choco chili which was a nice kick for chocolate ice cream. The place is tucked back off central and is small. It appears to have a great following and was busy on a Saturday night. I wasn't wowed that this was the best ice cream in Phoenix, but it was deserving of 4 stars.
Lime basil w/ lemon olive oil - DELISH! Plus, you can play board games here! So fun!

We recently stumbled upon this spot while visiting the bar "the wayward" which is located next door. The dough melt is AMAZING which is basically a donut warmed with ice cream in the middle ! I ate mine within the blink of an eye, 100% worth it to go try! You won't regret it!

When I first saw the creme brÃ»lÃ©e donut on Facebook, I knew that I had to try it the next time I was in Vegas. Well, the 'next time' was much sooner than I thought. And for those of you who don't know what I'm talking about, go Google the creme brÃ»lÃ©e donut now and watch a video of it in action. It's just one those things where words won't do it justice. The thing about Donut Bar is that it is open until the store runs out of donuts. Therefore, I recommend getting there when it opens or going on a weekday. My friends and I got there on a Tuesday morning around 10am, and there wasn't a line. The best part was that there was a ton of creme brÃ»lÃ©e donuts available! We tried the pistachio lemon, maple bacon, strawberries & cream, and the creme brÃ»lÃ©e donuts. Out of everything I tried, the creme brÃ»lÃ©e is my favorite. The sugar coating is thick and tough, making it impossible to 'crack' with a plastic spoon. The cream filling inside is not too sweet and delicious. The other donuts are the cake kind, which is not my favorite. They're good -- a solid 4 where the creme brulee is a 4.5

my favorite part of the store is the whole kitschy vibe goin' on. tons of retro candies, cute cake platters piled high w/ obviously homemade baked goods, shiny espresso machine, cute menu, homemade ice cream.... the banana and blackberry flavors were really good. the husband and i shared a sandwich of banana ice cream between a white-choc-cashew? and a kitchen sink cookie.i dunno if i'd go so far to say that they (the ice creams) were a-ma-zing. but they were pretty darn good. (you have to understand that i'm judging based on all of my ice cream experiences... comparing w/ Bi-Rite Creamery, Humphrey Slocombe, Scoops, and myriad other "gourmet" ice cream shops). as far as my AZ ice creamery experiences goes... this is pretty up there. i think what stands out about churn is that it is clearly HOMEMADE. and i mean that in a good way. you can tell that they haven't industrialized or lost any of the "made with love" touch. which is nice! and different! the main drawback of such a small business is there can be a bit of a wait if you come in with/after a large group. and by large i mean 4 orders of ice cream. we were that large group. oops. summary: Churn is the PERFECT ending to a great dinner at Windsor. support local small businesses!!!

Delicious milkshakes. I had my reservations about a place using prepackaged cereal as a main ingredient in the majority of their dishes. But I was wrong. They. Are. Delicious. I also really enjoy watching the assembly process.

Want to spend some quality time with a group of friends over a beverage and snacks?? This is the place to be. Great ambience , good service- could be better if the queue wasn't that big, great beverages(dirty chai/latte) and some exceptional snacks. Do try it out.
It's a quaint little shop with friendly staff and the ice cream taste amazing. The quality is fantastic and I've defiantly been missing out since moving here in 2007
Amazing. This is a must stop for any foodie. From cakes to Italian pastries the only problem youll have is deciding what to to pick. Staff is super friendly and fast.

What's shaken,"sweet republic" thang? You're like the guy with the "hot" pictures on Match.com that you have to stop and look, and send a "wink" to. Yes, you are. I was in Scottsdale and wanted something "sweet", some "honeylicious" ice cream. So, where do I go? I check my Yelp app (my Match.com for food) and I come across this place. I stop and look at these pictures! Oh my - what a dime! You look good, you ice cream sundae, you! Damn, I want a piece of that! I ain't gonna "wink", I'm gonna visit you because you just look too damn good! So...I race over there and I get one scoop of espresso and one scoop of mocha crumble ice cream. No syrup, no toppings - I like it all natural! Sweet Republic, you are everything I expected you to be! Delicious and satisfying!

The cannoli's and the lobster tail were amazing! I was really hesitant after reading all the reviews online. But my husband said to give it a try anyway and good thing I listened! Oh and their brownie!!! O M G! It was amazing! I'm not the chocolate fan, my husband is. He had me try it and it was so moist and it just made my mouth water! Their customer service was good. We were greeted and helped right away! I'd recommend others to go and try it out for themselves!

We got the bacon cinnamon roll, caramel latte donut and the creme brulee donut. The creme brulee donut was normal sized, the cinnamon roll was just a little bigger than average, but thr caramel latte donut was huge. Even splitting them, we could not finish it all. To top it off, they came around and offered samples of the french toast donut. That sample made me wish we had gotten one of those for sure.
I want to scream from the rooftops "I LOVE THIS PLACE". There's always a line, but once you receive your milkshake or other dairy confection you'll realize why. Honestly everything is good.
We gave this a try on our Vegas trip. Had the bday cake and strawberry shortcake soft serve. It was good but not anything exceptional. Staff was friendly and helpful.
I enjoy the fruit tarts, the pecan pie, and the key lime tarts. The quality of the food used to be better so I only stick to the few pastries now and maybe a cup of tea.
The best ice cream!! Such a cute little walk up ice cream shop that's been there forever!! Def a must try if you like ice cream!

O.M.G! I can't ever get out of here without a piece of cassata cake & either apple or cherry fresh danish (or BOTH!) Of course the soups are always delicious, any entree or a la cart item I have ever tried is amazing (tortellini, eggplant parm, etc.) Never disappoints & warms the tummy & soul. Absolutely recommend.

Ironic that I'm giving Bouchon BAKERY such high marks, considering I am NOT a fan of Bouchon restaurant (eaten there twice and not impressed nor satisfied both times). I have yet to try the MUCH reviewed macarons here. However, this is what I have tried: 1. Strawberry croissant...AWESOME. Fresh made strawberry jam inside a buttery, flaky croissant that's dusted with confectioner's sugar.. Not TOO sweet IMO and OH SO enjoyable. 2. Chocoloate Bouchon...Imagine the best brownie you ever ate, but more moist and less dense; then add some semi sweet chocolate chips in the middle, dust it off with some confectioner's sugar and you have a chocolate Bouchon. They clearly used a very high quality dark chocolate, could be a Valrhona 60%+ dark baking chocolate. Who knows? But I do know that I will be buying more of these bit sized treats. 3. Almond Brioche...The edges have a slightly stale and burnt taste to them. While some may prefer this texture and flavor combination, I did not. After discarding the edges, I was left with an amazing piece of soft and moist brioche bread with a wonderful almond paste and sliced almonds. I thoroughly enjoyed it. 4. Pretzel sticks...Personally, I love pretzels and pretzel bread. So while this was nothing special, I still enjoyed it quite a bit. If I could take it home and heat it up in the oven and dip it in some great mustard or cheese dip...then it would be GREAT! There are still many things I plan to try soon, will update this as I try them.
California Cheesecake well worth the wait, great assortment of different flavors, not to mention the free samples, line wrapped around the side of the building. ..
So many yummy flavors! Just a bummer that the line is always so long. Worth the wait though!

Creamy, decadent, awesomeness. Such a cute little place and the sundaes are perfection. I had the s'mores sundae and the chocolate ice cream was so good and the toasted marshmallow was the cherry on top! It was gooey and complimented the ice cream so well. Loved it! My husband had the strawberry shortcake and said it was really good too.

I have dreams about the Chocolate Almond Croissant. Bouchon Bakery is one of our must stop places on each visit to the Las Vegas strip. Grab a coffee and pastry, take a seat outside at one of the five or six tables available and spend the next 30 minutes people watching.

We came here after my coworker watched Chefs Table and learned about this place We came for the cereal flavor ice cream. It was good on it's own, not omg but good. (See TIP below) We got a slice of the crack pie and that REALLY lived up to it's name. Wow it was good. TIP: Put the ice cream ON the pie... and your tastebuds won't even know how to handle it. Flipping a, I want it right now.

When I lived in Queens, there was an adorable bakery called Martha's that was open 6 am - 2 am, and it was perfect for the nights where you wanted to go out but not drink. Somehow I missed that Butterwood opened a few months ago, and I am sad it opened as I get ready to move out of Pittsburgh! Everyone needs a late night bakery in their life. The atmosphere is amazing. There are Victorian couches and chairs, and the whole place has a cozy but intimate vibe. They only have 6-8 desserts to choose from so don't expect to see walls of cakes here, but all of the options were unique. We decided to split a slice of the Lavender blackberry cake with vanilla buttercream, and while light in flavor, it was delicious. The cake was really moist, and the icing was not sickly sweet. At $6.49/slice, I thought it was super reasonable, considering the late hours and cute vibe. The other cakes looked awesome as well, and I would love to come back before I move. Coming in on a Wednesday night at 8:30, my roommate and I were the only people here. By the time we left, three more parties had come in. Parking was super easy in this part of Lawrenceville, which was also nice. They accept credit as well, so there is no reason not to test it out.

I have been here a few times, and I really truly deeply think it's great for a treat. I have ordered food other than the desserts and it's pretty good. Of course the fan fav is the salted caramel brownie!

I'm always on the hunt for ways I can meet the tooth fairy sooner than later. This little hidden gem is perfect for sweets and desserts for my cravings. I can see why the Halo Halo is a hit and their best seller. The right combination of sweet and goodness. I had the large and overstuffed myself off the grass jelly and taro topping. That pirouline straw is bomb. Not to mention, it's pretty to look at as you stuff your face with it. My nieces got the taro and peach and lychee boba. They thought it was a bit sweet but good flavor. The owners are so sweet and they have regulars that bring in more guests. Aside from the sweets, they serve food too. The day we were in their daily special was noodles but I came for just dessert. I definitely will be back to try the other items if I can be persuaded to give up the Halo Halo. Life is short, make it sweet. Besides, who counts the calories when you got memories of goodness to bank on?!

We got the brownie, chocolate chip cookie and the strawberry cheesecake. Everything was delicious! Went later at night and there was not a long line at all. It is extremely hard to find if you come in through the Venetian. I would recommend heading in closer to the Palazzo. The ONLY reason this doesn't get 5 stars is because there were no prices listed for anything other than family trays of goodies. Other than that, it was fantastic.

The ice cream was very good. We did the choose 3 flavors deal which was actually priced very reasonable I thought. They have plenty of seating outside, we were just unfortunate enough to go on a rainy night which turned into a torrential downpour! Other than that the ice cream was good. This was the only place we found that was still open until around 10:30pm on a Saturday night! Overall good ice cream, good bang for your buck, just don't go on a rainy day.

I've always wanted to try sprinkles! So good. Not overly sweet. Well balanced cupcakes! I tried the banana, pumpkin, and strawberry. All delicious. The location is great! On linq promenade so there's other stuff in the area. Nice walk. Near the high roller.

Amazing!!! Just went there with my wife to get prepped for Nee Year's Eve. Great staff offering help with the menu. Decided on the pretzel cone with double chocolate and a how now brown cow. Both were great. The pretzel cone is a first for us and an amazing idea mixed with the sweet cream. We've got to bring the kiddos back to this place!

I give the Confetti Cookie 4 stars - delicious! The Chocolate Chocolate cookie's flavor leaned a little too heavy on the dark chocolate side for my husband's liking (and for mine). I tried the Cereal Milk White Russian. I think it would be better without the cereal milk flavor. Husband had a chocolate cereal shake and found the cereal milk flavor to be too overpowering. I guess it's just not for us, but if you are someone who lurvvs cereal milk, then this place might be perfect for you!

Disappointing to say the least. For a place that closes at 10pm they were out and had empty shelves and it was only 6:30pm. And when I asked one of the girls if they were baking anymore pastries she said no, because they didn't think they would be as busy as they were and that they only baked a certain amount for the day. I realize they have been open for just a few days but they have quite a ways to go before they meet the standards set by their California bakeries. Didn't matter what time of day I went into one of the California locations they had fresh, just out of the oven pastries and they had at least 2-workers walking the floor and communicating with the bakers what was needed on the floor. Not only that, they greeted you as soon as you walked in...the staff at this location looked beat down and exhausted and I had the girl tell me she hates they have to pack the pastries at the register. I was thinking I wouldn't know since you have nothing to offer. The location is roomy but they have wasted space that could have occupied more pastries. Then again no reason since the shelves are empty. To top it off, they had one cashier and a long line. Yet they had at least 4-people standing behind her, huddled and talking about who knows what and since the girl confirmed they weren't baking anything, why was no one else helping with the long line? Again, they are new but take a page from your California locations and take the initiative to keep the ovens baking so you can meet the demand for your product. There is no reason for you to be open till 10pm yet have empty shelves 4-hours prior to close. Why bother staying open? And my drive down there is a ways away and was a waste of time. The hype behind this place is not living up to the expectation. See Jeremy's review below and that is what the shelves looked like last night. Seems to be a trend...
Best ice cream in Las Vegas. The blueberry cobbler and graham central are my favorites. Get it baby, trust me
In my top 5 of best ice cream stands. The highlight here is the coconut. Friendly staff, quality choices upon choices make this place a can't miss if your in the area. Highest recommendation.

Went to grab dessert at night and figured why not try the gourmet chocolatier shop here as it's close to the Linq, where we were staying. Unfortunately, their machine broke or something which meant my cravings for a shake were crushed. Didn't think I came to a McDonalds, but alright. Four stars for a slightly above average experience despite not being able to snag a shake. More like a 3.5 probably. Line was extremely long but the staff were great. Location is amazing as it's in the heart of the strip and on the promenade. Prices and value suck but you come for the experience at least once. Anyways, the ice cream scoops are generous and I regretted opting for a triple scoop. I contemplated throwing away my bowl because it was so much but as an ice cream fanatic, I couldn't bring myself to do that. Friend got a scoop in the sugar cone and the cone was challenging to hold because the scoop was ginormous. Another friend opted for the Drinking Chocolate. Well, it's literally melted chocolate, extremely dense with chocolate. It was a debate between that or the hot chocolate and he noted he would get the standard hot chocolate in the future. The Drinking Chocolate is for true chocolate fanatics, not just anyone.

Average cupcake. Honestly, it didn't taste the freshest. Top heavy, as are most cupcakes. I went right at opening, so I didn't have to wait in line, but I can see why the lines build up as the staff does not seem to be the most efficient. If I happen to be in the area with company, maybe I'd get another cupcake, but for the most part, it's just worth it. Not worth the price or the calories.
Everything was perfect I wish there was one closer! Soooo yummy! Please come to Longview Texas!!

Went to the smaller location in the Venetian near the elevators. It's a good place to grab a quick bite or pastry. I didn't try the macaroons but I don't really go crazy for them anyway. Here's what I did try: Oatmeal raisin cookie (4 stars): Soft, chewy, and rich. Chocolate croissant (3.5 stars): Nice and flaky but needs more chocolate. The chocolate is only right in the middle, which I guess works but if you love chocolate like me you want some more! Grilled cheese (4 stars): Crunchy bread and good cheese. Surprisingly, a pretty good grilled cheese.

I love ice-cream and absolutely love going to an ice-cream parlor to bond with loved ones. I was visiting my mother from California and wanted to treat her to ice-cream, so I yelped and found this place. I got the caramel apple pie float which was good. I tried my mother's cherry cola float and liked hers better. She said she liked mines better so we switched. It was in the later evening and a little chilly, so we both were really happy about the heat lamps outside.

Stumbled across this spot walking through downtown Phoenix one evening. The staff there was very helpful with answering questions about flavors and let you have samples. And o boy! This ice cream is very good. Probably jumped straight to top of my favorite phoenix spot above other power houses.

The ice cream is good and plentiful. The mix concept is different and the mixer is kinda cool to watch. The teas were decent and definitely pretty. Overall, it's a good spot and if I'm in the area again, I'd get an ice cream and a Tea to go.

Ice cream was great. Price not so much, but I guess that is what happens when you ask for homemade ice cream. I ordered 7 "Dips" of ice cream expecting a solid amount but that was not the case. No matter how I look at it, I feel gypped. It felt like just barely one scoop from the Sugar Bowl in comparison. That is my only gripe. If you are looking for great homemade ice cream this is the spot, but expect to pay for it. Sadly, I don't think I will be back but it was definitely worth a try.

Oh I love Handel's! All flavors are to die for. When stressed out, we look forward of going here and everything will go well most specially having the pistachio flavor ice cream. Kids love it here all the time

I was underwhelmed by my experience at Jeni's and so were my family members. First of all, the line is incredibly frustrating to wait in. It was hot and service was slow. I know scooping ice cream takes time, but for the time it took, it was not worth it. My husband and I both sampled several flavors and did not like many of them. My husband said that both chocolate flavors he tasted had bizarre aftertastes. I tried vanilla and honey and didn't taste any honey. I did end up getting cream puff flavor which was fine, but nothing to crave or rave about. The flavors have the illusion of being interesting, but are not great flavors. This, of course, is just my opinion. But I feel the appeal is in the boutique shop style and reputation rather than actual quality. We also felt it was far too overpriced for what you get. I much prefer Golden Cow Creamery down the road. I have no reason to revisit Jeni's again when there are better ice cream shops in Charlotte.

The ice cream is delicious. The servers are friendly. The wait....had to wait in line, only 2 windows open, then again it was a Monday around 3pm. But, it appeared to me that it's social hour for the employees. They spent more time talking, and less time working to serve the people in line. I would definitely go back, but hopefully service will be faster. After all, I spent over $40.00 while I was there. When I was a kid, the boss used to tell us "no talking" while it was busy. Ah, the good ol' days.

Can you believe I used to live in the southside and never once went to Page's? I know, it's blasphemy. Luckily, I made up for lost time by visiting TWICE in two days when I was in the neighborhood recently. The shop itself gets zero points for ambiance. It's in an odd location at a busy intersection, with limited seating and parking. Well, I should strike that last part...there is parking, but it's a little bit of a chaotic free-for-all (especially behind the building) and can be hard to navigate when it's crowded (when I was there, I watched a BMW back into a telephone pole trying to leave....talk about an expensive ice cream cone!) As others have mentioned, the lines get crazy long (it was literally 40 degrees and windy the two times I went, but it was still insanely busy), but they move fast. Soft serve ice cream is their thing and they have about a gazillion flavors served up in a gazillion different ways....definitely scout out the menu beforehand to avoid indecision paralysis when it's your turn to order! I got the strawberry shortcake sundae on my first visit and then went with a parfait the next time. Note that although they have a zillion different options, your ability to customize is somewhat limited. I had wanted to get a parfait with peanut butter ice cream, but the only thing they let me choose in the parfait was the topping (they forced me to get vanilla, so that's kind of a buzzkill). The portions here are comically large....easily enough for two people and should probably be served with a complimentary side of insulin. But friends, I tell you, it is worth the calories and ensuing sugar coma! The strawberry sundae in particular is divine...soft pound cake nestled underneath 673 lbs of vanilla ice cream, smothered in sweet strawberries....mmmmmm! My hubby got the cookie sundae, and it was a beautiful amalgamation of warm cookies, hot fudge, and ice cream (I'm drooling just thinking about it!) The parfait I had during my second visit was also good, but it wasn't particularly better than parfaits I've had elsewhere. Stick with their specialty sundaes, kids...I think that's what truly sets Page's apart from other ice cream joints. Cash only. See ya next time I'm in the southside!

This was a very quaint and cute ice cream and candy shop. They make homemade ice cream and sorbet, and they tasted amazing. I tried the vegan coconut sorbet, and I absolutely loved it. I don't usually eat vegan, but this was so good.
Great spot for a quick cup of coffee and bite.tried the almond croissant it was flaky and delicious. Coffee was good. Tables are available outside shop

My friend and I got the Supreme crepe(I don't remember the name, but it is the one with all the fruits) and the mango raspberry crepe. They are generous on fillings and the crepes taste so so so good 10/10. Add ice cream because that enhances the flavor by 100x. The cafe is well-managed and clean. The employers are all really kind and nice. I would come here again! If you want drink recommendations, I really liked the mojito drinks!

Brown Butter Almond Brittle! I recommend getting the 3 half scoop ice cream flight. Make sure you are full of patience. You will need to sample every flavor and so does the person in front of you. The night we went there was no line. Halfway thru our samples, someone got in line behind us and we took 10 more minutes before we were able to settle on 3 flavors, relationships lol. Now we went after dinner this fall, I can't imagine the capacity of ice cream foodies that Jeni's accommodates during the summer. Jeni's is a great end to a date night in the Southend.

Bouchon Bakery in Vegas is not as nice as the one in NY, but the goods are still, er, good, haha. The macarons & Oreo cookie are both good, just as they are in the NY location. I make it a point to stop by here at least once when I'm in Vegas & my only complaint is that some of the counter people can be very holier-than-thou. Ironically, the ones working @the NY Bouchon Bakery are pretty nice & friendlier than the ones @the Vegas Bouchon Bakery. Which is pretty ironic considering the Vegas counter people work at a lower-level version of this place which is really just a small counter in front of a theater, with no place to sit to enjoy the food & coffee. But still ... the macarons always draw me back here. Cannot say no to all that almond-ey goodness :-). Note: Do not shove bagged macaron into your shoulder bag & eat in hotel room. I made the mistake of doing that once & had to eat the flattened contents by licking them off the bag they put it in :-b. Not my finest moment!

Lived in Cleveland Heights for 5 years (1987-1992) - Presti's was a place to go for donuts and other goodies. During wife's pregnancy I found myself at Presti's at odd hours (3 AM cravings! for half a glazed donut!) and even at that ungodly hour I was never alone :-). From 1992 I had to drive from far side of Mayfield RD for our donut fix. great bread too.

Combining the two best things in this world: donuts and ice cream. Where could they go wrong?? They didn't! Both items were delicious, and they were even more delicious together! Be aware though - the blue ice cream will turn your mouth blue!

Sprinkles located in the middle of the strip!? Talk about dessert heaven especially with their cupcake ATM for late night sweet tooth's when the store is closed! I'm such a sucker for dessert and call me Queen of Desserts. I went to this location with a few friends and got the red velvet waffle & watermelon sorbet talk about balance. Haha I also had a bite of the chocolate and red velvet cupcake, which I wasn't too big of a fan of since my mouth was still stuck on the sorbet. Haha Overall, cute ambiance and great souvenirs to buy from in Las Vegas Sprinkles!

You literally cannot beat Mitchell's ice cream. I eat it daily (hate to admit it?).. I buy it at the local grocery stores as well. Favorite flavors include the seasonal campfire s'mores and cold brew. Also love ALL the vegan flavors.. even the "plain" chocolate.. seriously the best chocolate ice cream I've ever had. If you haven't tried Mitchell's yet, you are waaay behind the times. Get there ASAP!!
Toasted Coconut Sorbet was absolutely light and refreshing with every bite. Only drawback about this place was the wait. it was under 30 min but haha who likes to wait?!

The ice cream is delicious. My favorite thing to get is the ice cream sandwiched between two cookies. The available cookies can vary but my favorite is the coconut macaroon cookie mixed with some other cookie with the Vietnamese ice cream between them. So good. Also, the people that work here have always been really nice to me even when I want to try a multitude of ice cream flavors. The other random trinkets and candies in the shop don't interest me but make for a cool visual and nostalgia. Only downside is that parking can be complicated/inconvenient. Highly recommended ice cream!
Wow they got some yummy chewy macaroons here, a bit pricey like $3.50 for the jumbo sized ones. A good place for a quick sweet snack.

I tried the mango and strawberry shake and it was so refreshing just what I needed. The employees were nice and working really fast. Every time I turned around the line was out of the door. There is plenty of sitting inside and outside. They also serve hot food but we didn't try any this time around.

I'm not much of a "sweets" person but I do like French macarons - Bouchon Bakery makes a darn good macaron! =) The macarons are really good here - all the flavors are great. It's very light & crisp outside but chewy & rich in the middle. I can't eat too many sweets in one sitting so I've left them in the fridge. Even several days later, the macarons are still great! If you love pastries, definitely go to Bouchon Bakery. It's located in Venetian...near the Grand Lux & the theater. They have lots of yummy looking pastries here but I specifically went for macarons which cost $3.50 each or for a box of 6 different flavors, $17.50.
GREAT pastry - pricey - long lines
A true beacon of snacking perfection! You will not be disappointed! Also the owners are some of the nicest people you will ever meet!

It's hard to find real ice cream in the valley. There are hundreds, if not thousands of frozen yogurt spots, but real ice cream really is rare. After reading some interesting articles on Sweet Republic, we finally decided to drive on down to Scottsdale and check it out. It''s in a strip mall (of course), and the interior is pretty cute. Modern and clean. Plenty of tables to enjoy your ice cream, and a few scattered outside. Their ice creams are made in house, in small batches, with local, all natural ingredients. I had the az mint..you can actually see the mint leaves. It was different, but good.

I was lucky in college. I had friends with cars or I had a car to drive to Jarlings. It's kind of hard to get to otherwise and I wasn't that in love with public transportation back then. Whenever I'm in town for work, I figure out how I can maximize trips to Jarlings. I'm not kidding. Things I love: - Strawberry shortcake snowstorm - Pumpkin pie snowstorm (seasonal. Lucky me visits during the season) - Vanilla custard with chocolate/butterscotch sauce. - Strawberry custard - Any float There's nothing that hits the spot as well as Jarlings.
Generic ice cream . Shitty quality. Nothing tastes fresh. Huge disappointment after looking at the positive ratings. Was expecting much better.

An apparent local institution and Tom Hanks recommended. The good: Classic frozen treat stand. Fresh, smooth custard (we saw a couple of the extruders working while waiting). Tons of flavor combinations with their snowstorms (mix in shakes or blizzards). Reasonable prices. The bad: While all three lines and drive through were open, the lines do take longer than I would think, even with what looked to be a full staff. While I appreciate that this is a tough job, with what propably seems like endless lines of hungry customers, I would have liked a bit more friendliness from our stereotypical surly teenager. The unknown: Perhaps I ordered wrong, but while delicious, my turtle sundae seemed a little light on the custard. I was left with quite a bit of hard chocolate/nutty shell and had to steal some spoons of custard from Cheddartarian's double custard root beer float. The other treats ordered by earlier guests looked quite a bit more generous. Ultimately, I would go back though, and that is as good a measure as anything.

I love Mitchell's. There is ALWAYS plenty of parking. They are all clean. Love the sundae combinations!! The Buckeye Brownie is the MOST amazing. The mint chocolate chip ice cream is so crazy good! No crazy dies. Real mint is used. My other weakness is the banana cream pie ice cream. You can get pints to-go. Be sure to get the free cones with your pints! They have the cutest water dispenser! PS. The covid 19 inspired Curbside ordering and pickup is BRILLIANT!!

I'm a donut gal. Now, this may interfere with living a 'healthy lifestyle' but I really don't care. These delicious treats are my lifesaver after a rough workweek! This place is a gem because of the wide selection of donuts (and low prices). My favorite is blueberry, but maple is a close second!

Just randomly discovered this place one night after parking on the street. Have a ton of great flavors which all seem to be great. Had Cookie Monster which was amazing. I mean how can you go wrong with cookie dough and Oreo! Also they serve ice cream in Chinese takeout boxes with a fortune cookie. Ordered a small (one scoop) which was the perfect size because of how rich the ice cream was.

I love Mitchell's ice cream. I think it is way better quality than Jeni's. Yep, I just said that. This store is really a bit sterile...but I love the view of the factory and the choo choo train overhead. When I saw that the Porter chocolate chunk was out of stock, they offered to pack me a quart if I could wait a few minutes. They rock...

The macarons here are truly amazing. The texture is absolutely perfect! Just the right amount of subtle chewiness combined with light flaky crispiness I recommend buying a box of their mini macarons (they're actually the same size as regular macarons you would find anywhere else) for $12 (which comes out to $2 per macaron); then, you can try them all and determine which one you like the most before you buy the bigger individual ones for $3.50 each. I wish they had more flavors. They have a total of six flavors: vanilla, chocolate, pistachio, raspberry, coffee and caramel. My favorite flavors were vanilla and raspberry. The chocolate and coffee macarons were too rich for me. Pistachio and caramel were descent. Definitely check this place out when you're at The Venetian!

I love Jeni's... they are consistent and always so friendly. Their ice cream never disappoints but these waffle cones they have... GIRL! These are fresh made and so good!! Trying the rotating, unique flavors is nice too. I like that they use real spoons for taste testing. I tried a few but landed on peanut butter. Wish I could have Jeni's everyday!
I ordered the frozen hot cocoa 10/10!!! Must have. We also got the Nob Chill Hill. It was okay. We didn't like it. 3/10

Came here while in the city; it had the best reviews for ice cream and honestly the pictures looked so cool. We navigated here on a Saturday night and there was a huge line. It moved relatively quickly though, took about 25 mins to order. Was this the best ice cream I've ever had? Nope. Was nothing special honestly. The place is cool and very photogenic. They serve up good portion sizes (I don't know if it's cause it's American or if they're actually big portions) but I wasn't a huge fan honestly. I ordered a small sundae that came with almost no fudge and maybe 3 peanuts worth of peanut topping lol. My SO did order a medium twist cone though and it was disgustingly massive. Overall, my opinion of this place is to come here once, take some pictures and be done with it.. there's much better ice cream elsewhere.
Cannot resist from their macaroons, it's so good. The sweet level is perfect, not too sweet which can make my sweet tooth happy :)

It was a nice clear evening. The air was cool and flowing gently. Suddenly, the most amazing smell pe etrated my soul. I asked a passerby what the smell was and they informed me that it was Jenni's making waffle cones. I had heard a lot about Jenni's Ice Cream. I even did a brief study on the founder and how she began the company. I'm not a big ice cream eater so I didn't have any major urge to try this spot. The smell got me. I took a moment and read the menu from outside. An employee came out and I invited me in for a sample. I should have never stepped inside. I sampled things I would have never picked by choice. People were literally call put their favorites for me to try. Everyone was excited that it was my first time. After the first sample I started to understand why. Brandied Banana Brulee changed my entire perception of the possibilities of the vehicle that ice cream could be for flavors. My entire world was opened up and I dove I head first. I even loved the goat cheese and raspberry flavor. I hate blue cheese for some reason this was delicious. It is now my mission in life to try every Jenni's flavor I can get my hands on. By "try" I mean eat triple scoops of each. You should join me on this creamy journey of remarkable deliciousness. See you in line.

Was here for a baby shower and they had a nice private room set up. The food and sandwiches were delicious and the pastries and sweets were to die for. We even went in stood in the long line to grab some treats to take home. Macaroons and the salted caramel brownie were mouth watering!
It is so good I loved the warm donuts. I will recommend this place who loves ice cream and donuts together !!!
Average pastries coupled with the poor service makes this place worth skipping. They could also improve on their efficiency. Really poor way of doing business. If you're a fan it's worth going ONCE.

I can't say enough great things about this place! My aunt recommended this place since she said the ambiance was very cute and the food was great! She was SO RIGHT! As soon as you walk in, you're transported into a different world that is so unique and warm. They have so many different dessert and drink options. And the food was so fresh and delicious. I tried the turkey and brie and it was absolutely delicious. For dessert, I indulged in an apple pie which was the perfect ending to a great meal! There are plenty of places to sit and I noticed there were several group meetings going on. The place is also open 24 hours! Just perfect! I look forward to visiting again soon!

We were craving an Ube milkshake and in our search, Scooptopia came up. This was a great find! The halo halo was SO good, one of the best I have ever had. Sadly, we missed out on the Ube with white chocolate chips cookies. The owner was so nice explaining her specialty desserts. Not too far, so we will definitely be back.

Lavender Honey Just gave me life. I found Novel in July 2017 just before my flight to return to Savannah after finding a place to live in Phoenix on a whim. I have introduced a number of friends to Novel, who have introduced a number of their friends as well. Everyone loves it...and you will too. Hands down...best ice cream in Phoenix...quite possibly America.

Stopped here while in Cleveland for work after hearing great reviews. The girl working the counter was super friendly and helpful. I ended up with maple, german chocolate, samoa and turtle doughnuts. All were delicious but the maple was my favorite! Yummm!!

Don't get the big deal. The almond croissant bore no resemblance to a croissant. Was a doughy undercooked chunk of bread loaded w overwhelming almond paste. Are fans of the tv show really thinking this is what an almond croissant is? The cupcake was good, and the dark chocolate mousse tart was ok. Very sweet. Only reason to come here was the cannoli which was excellent.
Visited amelie's while visiting charlotte. O.M.G. you must go. life changing everything was so good i made two trips to this bakery within 2 hours of each other. authentic fresh french goods
Fast and friendly service.....and the most delicious Birthday Cake Shake. Wow! What a treat. I like this place and will happily return next time I am in Vegas.

Page Dairy Mart--truly a Pittsburgh summer staple for me. Don't let the location under a bridge scare you off, they have some delicious ice cream!! The prices are great too. Beware, it's cash only but they do have an ATM on site. You really can't go wrong with any Arctic Swirl. My personal favorite is the cookie dough Arctic Swirl. Most use vanilla soft serve, but you can upgrade to any flavor, which I highly recommend. Their birthday cake soft serve is amazing! It has sprinkles and cake pieces in it (though mostly sprinkles). If you have a bigger appetite, the cookie sundae is a crowd favorite. Just come here. It's ice cream. You won't regret it

Delicious ice cream combined with excellent service. The owners have done their research and are putting their all into this adorable little ice cream shop. They have a rotating menu with several unique flavors including sorbets. And if that's not enough you can add toppings or put your ice cream between a honey bun or on top of a waffle. When you come here you feel like you're helping the little guy and making the world a better place. Plus you get ice cream out of it so it's a win win!
Appreciate the cool style, flavorful and perfectly done ice cream. Recommend the milkshakes.

Why 4 Stars? Because I'm a fan. It's located inside the Venetian: it's not even a shop, rather just a small stand. Anywho, Thomas Keller, I love you. I can eat TKO and macaroons forever. The TKO is like a big Oreo cookies but a super high class & fancy distant cousin. The 2 chocolate cookies had the perfect blend of crunchiness and cocoa flavor. The cream in the middle is amazing. The sweetness & sugar crystals are so smooth & perfect texture with a soft organic crÃ¨me aroma. What type of butter or cream did you use? Taste expensive. Your macaroons are big & perfect amount of chewiness & crunch. It's still one of my favorites across the nation, comparing to Paulettes in LA or sleek macaroon shops in NYC. The macaroons can get too sweet sometimes, so just make sure you enjoy it with coffee or milk. But I do love your raspberry and blueberry macaroons as I can taste the fresh fruit in all parts & not just the filling. Well, all I know is that whenever I'm in Napa or Vegas, I shall always come & visit you.

Was looking for a local ice cream establishment. I looked through yelp to find an establishment worthy of this indulgence. I stumbled across Novel Ice Cream. Located in a very unassuming location I was greeted by the owner and a couple workers who were all very friendly. The owner was very passionate and proud of the donut and hand crafted ice cream they make. Apparently the donut has won awards along side the ice cream. Since it was a slow night It appeared to be ok to try Most of the flavors. I ended up with chocolate stuffed inside a warmed donut cut in half. It obviously was not part of my food program however when I'm Phoenix a donut stuffed with gourmet ice cream has no calories so I was ok. I strongly recommend paying this establishment a visit and trying the donut stuffed thing they make. It's pretty outstanding.

I've been to many bakeries across the country... but I can honestly say that this is not as good of a bakery as I was lead to believe. I came to Charlotte for work and I told by everyone that this was likely the best bakery in Charlotte, with some of the best coffee. I have got to say that Amelies is a good bakery and it's definitely worth a visit. However, I can certainly attest to having better coffee at 7th Street Market and know at least 2 bakeries in Durham, NC that have better pastries and bread by a LONG shot. To the average person who's use to WallMart croissant this is certainly a breath of fresh air - but don't be mislead into thinking this is the best of the best!

From a distant land of NY I come to this establishment, all for tiramisu. As I approach the delectable sweets I ask for my prize and yet, nothing is delivered. I am told, this is a 'fwench bakewy' and the most desired dessert is not within the walls of this cluttered palace of Knick knacks and oddly positioned tables. My head hangs dejectedly. My life is at a standstill. I must return to my land of NY tomorrow without a whisper of that layered dessert my heart yearns for. All because... this is a 'fwench bakewy'.

I Love Batch Bake House!! The Service is nice and Helpful! The Pastry/breads are so good! My favorites are the Baguette bread so fresh!! For pastries I love the Monkey Bread and the mini cherry Pie so good !

Heard the hype and decided to go and try it. Interesting taste of ice cream that is blended so definitely something new and very tasty. Enjoyed it very much definitely be back again to try other varieties.
I came here for ice cream and the line was out the door. I got the double chocolate on a waffle cone. This place had one of my favorite waffle cones!

A better-than-average bakery with wonderfully unusual atmosphere. The pastries here are tasty- their eclairs are fruit tarts are especially delicious. These are a nice snack, but nothing there is going to win any awards. It's a great place to meet with friends and have some tasty treats.

I had to stop here after seeing all the hype from Yelp and Buzzfeed recently and let me tell you...it's soooo worth it! They were recognized as being one of the best ice cream sandwich shops in the country! They offer sandwiches on waffles and warm glazed donuts yummmmmm. The ice cream itself is amazing too and it seems like they always have unique flavors! I tried the waffle sandwich with cookie monster ice cream topped with Oreos and I've been thinking about it ever since! My boyfriend and his friend got the donut sandwiches and they were both in love too lol. Highly recommend checking this place out!!!
Great ice cream. One of the best ice cream places located here in Charlotte, NC. Keep up the great work

I stayed in the Venetian and this kiosk was right by my elevator bank. I got breakfast here a few days: pain au choclat one day, an "epi loaf" (mini baguette) with butter and preserves another day. Both were incredible. The pain au chocolat was super flaky and had a very respectable amount of chocolate inside. The epi loaf was just plain good bread, but the preserves were unexpectedly delicious: blackberry jam, just bursting with flavor. I picked up the large box of macarons on my way home, which comes with a flavor assortment (raspberry, pistachio, salted caramel, vanilla, coffee, and chocolate). Laduree is still my favorite (airier, more delicate) but these were pretty darn good. I'm not sure they were as fresh as they could have been, they had a date sticker on them that was two days old. I think that may have been when they were baked? I was in a rush so I didn't notice until I was in the cab. Regardless, they were pretty great macarons. Look for this place near the Grand Lux cafe in the Venetian (confusingly, there's also a Grand Lux cafe in the Palazzo). Don't be discouraged if there's a line, it moves fast!
Very good donuts. We enjoyed them all. We also had the grilled cheese donut. Super yummy. The staff was very nice and patient with us and helped us makes choices. We will be back when we are in town.

The downer part about Bouchon Bakery is that they aren't consistent with what goodies they have, but I don't care because there's always something good to eat here! I really love the cranberry scone which I often get at the bakery located in Yountville. They didn't have any the last time we came here...bummer. I did get to try their massive macarons! (and expensive) They were really yummy! I want one now... I also ordered a TKO (can't go wrong with that) and different scone since they didn't have the one I wanted. If anything, come for the macaroons. I think they always have those in stock.

Okay, this place isn't all hype. Listen. The interior has super cute decor that is perfect for all your Instagram shots. There is plexiglass at the counter to protect the staff, and they all wear masks. They enforce somewhat of a social distancing with stickers on the floor but when we went there was only 1 other party so not sure how it is when its busy. They have a bunch of desserts and let me tell you. SO. GOOD. I'm not a fan of overly sweet things so I was hesitant to try their macarons and salted caramel brownie but everything was the perfect amount of sweetness with a good balance of salt. The brownie was fresh out of the cooler so the brownie felt like a cross of normal and crispy brownie with a soft and velvety caramel on top. Also their seasonal pumpkin cheese cake is TO DIE FOR. Souffle cheesecake consistency without the tart flavor of cream cheese, pumpkin puree in the center, coated with pumpkin maybe? If I could, I'd eat like 5. At once. Their almond flour cake bite things are 3rd rate compared to the other things. Everything about this place is amazing. Already recommending their pastries to all my friends!

Quite a lot of good choices in ice cream flavors that made it difficult to choose. I ended up with (3) flavors in a waffle cone for about $10. A bit expensive, but that's Vegas these days. Tam, my scooper, was smiling and pleasant during the transaction. Hope to try more flavors next time in Vegas.

Went to carlos for the first time and purchased 1/2 dozen lobster tails as well as some chocolate covered strawberries. I had really been looking forward to trying the famous lobster tails only to be beyond disappointed. I don't know if I received an old batch given that I've visited the bakery at 1030am, but they were leathery and tough. I had expected a light crispy flaky pastry and this was not that by any means. The only redeeming quality of them was the pastry cream inside. The chocolate covered strawberries were decent, just like any other chocolate covered strawberry you could get from any other bakery in town there wasn't anything special about them.
A coworker just brought donuts from this place, the s'mores donut is delicious! Great flavor
I love this place but today when we entered we were overwhelmed with the smell of an open sewer. Don't know what's going on in there but please, get that fixed ASAP!!!

WHEN YOU HAVE THOSE SWEET CRAVINGS (Warning: Young adult from Central Florida in for vacation) The Cookies, Crack Pie, and Coffee all fell to my cravings- sadly since these snacks were just to top off a meal, I had no room for the (very cool and crazy looking) Milkshakes... which can be made boozy! COMPOST COOKIES- NAME SAYS IT ALL ... and I also took a Cornflake Cookie. With ingredients like Coffee, Potato Chips, or Cornflakes, the end result was actually more like a 'more complicated' Chocolate Chip Cookie. I barely (if at all) tasted those weird ingredients individually so it was a bit of a miss. The best part were the bursts of salt from the Pretzels or Cornflakes. I also enjoyed the changed texture, ore similar to a soft (but not gooey) Oatmeal Cookie. IT IS ALL IT'S 'CRACKED' UP TO BE? The Crack Pie was a decent dessert. I liked the butterscotch flavor a lot- something I don't see in many pies. But the hard texture and strange way of serving it (packaging it in a cardboard, roundish box) were curiosities. Overall, this place is a bit pricey... but I also know you're paying for Strip resort prices. Keep in mind there's no seating here- just a walk up counter.
Lots of flavors to choose from. I liked the chai tea and chocolate marshmallow I tried. Didn't care for the icing which was hard as a rock.

I _think_ I've located the right spot to review. Three bakeries in the same place and two on top of one another... who do you think you are, Starbucks? I visited and purchased food from the Bouchon Bakery on the first floor of the Grand Canal Shoppes area. It's just off the Strip near B&B Burger and the outdoor gondola ride. We happened upon another Bouchon Bakery when we went upstairs afterward, and the original location is somewhere inside The Venetian. We found this one to be the most convenient, and it had a slightly wider selection than its overhead neighbor. I took two items to go and ate them within a few hours. The Croissant ($3.75) is a go-to pastry, and the version here is golden brown outside and chewy outside, with enough buttery flavor for anyone but diehard butter fans. Aside from how easily some of the outer layer flakes off, it's comparable to any other versions in town both on-Strip and off-Strip. The Kouign Amann ($4.50) is another classic, although it's tougher to find. It's both more difficult to make and less popular. This version does have a lot of the right crispy and chewy textures and the expected sugary flavors. I think this one cheats a little though; you can easily see a glassy sugar layer on the flat side of the kouign amann, and the dough just doesn't have enough layers. It's way too flat compared to other good versions that I've had. However, if I was blindfolded, I would likely have no issue. As long as parking stays free at the Palazzo and the Venetian, I'd consider making regular stops to this Bouchon Bakery for some pastries. My first taste was good enough (let's say 3.75 stars averaged between the two bites), so I'm optimistic about similar results if I venture into the cookies, macarons, or other baked goods (cinnamon rolls, monkey bread, and so on).

This place is certainly a diamond in the rough. Chances are if you never saw it on yelp, you would have never noticed it. I kid you not when I say that their red velvet cake is the best I've ever had I'm my entire life. No red velvet cake comes close to villani's. Every other item I have tried there has been out of this world delicious but I frequently dream about their moist red velvet cake with its perfect cream cheese frosting.

Their cupcakes and ice cream are okay. The hype is too real about sprinkles cupcakes. Everyone talks about how amazing the place is and how whenever someone goes to cali they have to come back with sprinkles. Now that it's here in Vegas and I finally got to try out what it's all about, my expectations were really high, yet I don't think they were met. They serve certain ice cream and cupcakes on certain days so make sure you keep an eye out for what day you're going. The cupcakes were kinda dry and I didn't really like the frosting on top. I've had better cupcakes and desserts. But this place is cute and have a friendly staff that's willing to help you no matter how busy it gets at the Linq. It's a great location though! Outside seating is fun since you get to see everything going on. I also like their clear glass walls and set up on the inside.

My best friend introduced this to me years ago and I can't describe how much I love this place. Their baked goods are freshly made in house and you can really taste it. I'm super picky about macaroons & they have the best ones I've personally tasted in the US. Customer service is always quick and friendly. Prices are fair for the quality of food/drinks you get.

One of my favorite stops in Charlotte. The decor/ambiance is absolutely perfect. The food, suburb. I wasn't a big fan of lavender lemonade, it wasn't particularly lavender or lemony. The macroons were perfection, however.

I stopped by here for an interview at Case Western for lunch and had an overall satisfactory experience. I ordered the spinach and sausage stromboli (with marinara on the side), and shared a bread pudding. First thing I noticed upon walking in was the chaos. They follow the take-a-number system and this means a lot of yelling and squeezing through crowds of people when your number is called. They do have a wide assortment of foods, ranging from pastries to paninis to pastas and more. My stromboli was decent - flavors were a bit muddled and it was really oily, but I was satisfied with my purchase. I definitely recommend that you get the marinara sauce on the side. The bread pudding was rather bland! I appreciate that it wasn't sickly sweet, but I don't eat dessert for bland flavors... so that was disappointing. One thing that I do love about this place is the pricing. Lunch for two (2 strombolis and a dessert to share) came out to $11-12, which is unheard of for me (I can easily pass amount for just myself). Would I visit again? Maybe. Especially if I were a student in the area, I'd say this is a great place to visit for decent, cheap eats.

This is a decent bakery, above average. However, since it carries Thomas Keller's name as an offshoot of Bouchon Bistro, which is an excellent spot for a meal, it doesn't quite measure up. The turkey sandwich comes with cheddar(?), onion, and watercress on pecan bread. It was ok - you can tell the ingredients are good - but the sandwich itself wasn't outstanding. Most of the items seem to just miss the mark: the bacon(?), egg, and cheese croissant comes with a beautiful, fat slice of omelet but it's topped with a thin sliver of cheese; the Cobb salad is huge but bacon wasn't listed as an ingredient so I passed on that. The macarons are a nice size, great for splitting with a friend, and the croissants are buttery without feeling greasy. I'll be back for that Kouign Amann.
I've tried every single snowstorm on Jarling's menu. Go for the Chocolate Chip Cherry. You won't be disappointed.

I'm in a chocolate wonderland! This was my first time at Ghirardelli Ice Cream Shop! Let's just say there were so much chocolate selections to choose from! Perfect for gifts. Not only do they sale chocolate, but they sale ice-cream and desserts. You walk in and they give free chocolate samples to you which was really nice.
Absolutely delish! I love the atmosphere. My first visit and I can't wait to go back on a day that I need a pick me up....I can grab a treat and a corner and be in a great space.
As always, the best ice cream ever....never disappoints, Cookie Monster all the way for the win.

I might have been hella drunk at 6:30 in the morning but the ham and cheese croissantwich was delicious!!!!! We were behind a guy that bought $150.00 worth of pastries and was telling the people behind the counter how he was going to recommend this place to everyone... As I was devouring my crumbly croissant, I was already full halfway through it... but I kept eating cause it was too damn good! I took out one star because I really was drunk..... so i need to come back here and try everything while I'm sober. Haha

Holy cow-worth all the hype!!!! Best dessert on the south side of LV. I don't even know what to compare it too but those little fish come things are a little crunchy, a little soft and a lot delicious. Very clean, love the vibes. Vegetarian friendly Good services, no complaints

On our way home from house warming party in North Scottsdale, I remembered I had a coupon for buy one get one free for Sweet Republic. This was my first visit at Sweet Republic and after tons of great reviews, my expectations were set and they were met. We both had the apple pie and Real Mint Chip. This is unlike any other ice cream I have ever had, it was delectable. I am happy I got to try this place. Thanks Yelp!

This place can have quite a long line. But luckily I caught it at a great time. We went yesterday around 3p, the Thursday before Christmas. The line was short and things moved pretty fast. I picked up two treats for mom and me to share. One Chocolate Hazelnut Lobster Tail - the Pastry on the outside had quite a Crunch, but the inside was nice and soft thanks to the glorious Hazelnut Custard! It also had a thick drizzle of Nutella on top. I have to say I wish they hadn't automatically packaged it because the wrapping paper ended up getting more of that Nutella than my stomach did. Our second treat was unmarked, so I'm not sure of the name. It looked like a big, glossy, chocolate cookie. I'm pretty sure it was some kind of meringue because of the light, chewy texture and it's shiny exterior. It only had nuts inside and I have to say I would've preferred chocolate chips. But it was yummy! Next time I'd love to try a cannoli!

It was ok! Idk what the hype is all about. I will admit one thing the cookies are awesome! And the crack pie is good. Well I guess 2 things.. haha Today we tried the ice cream for the first time.. and I honestly did not enjoy a bit of it.. the name was Inviting Cereal Milk ice cream... gave me a flash back of my child hood watching cartoon and having my bowl of cereal and always making sure To savor the left over milk... lol But it was just what ever.. for an additional charge There's is topping to add I chose to have the cereal crunch topping.. both combined together it left a salty after taste I couldn't ignore.. I had maybe a quarter of it and tossed it out... I'll stick to the cookies

This place is completely and totally awesome. I came here to burn some time and wanted to buy everything in the store. I love chocolate filled croissants, and had to try one. The ones here are most definitely the best I've ever had. I also got a chocolate chip cookie which was soft and gooey and phenomenal. I would definitely go back to try other desserts.
Just the very best homemade ice cream! Cute store with nostalgic candies and treats. Staff is always friendly.

Jarling's is a local ice cream gem! They offer a huge assortment of frozen custard, as well as ice cream staples like a banana split or sundae. I had a banana split and my partner had chocolate in a large waffle cone. Some words about our choices - you definitely get your money's worth and a little extra! They were very generous in their servings and the staff are just as sweet as the products Jarling's sells. So why is this a 4 star review and not a 5 star review? If you are craving ice cream on a weekday or weekend evening (like we were), you will be waiting for a *long* while. Additional word of caution: you *will* be cut in line. Stand your ground and get your ice cream - it will be well worth the wait!
I scream! You scream! We all scream when we see how long the line for this place is but then we get the ice cream and remember that it is 100% worth it. Order online and save a little time, though.

Everything looks amazing the moment you walk into the store. Every item I have tried so far from pastries to breakfast sandwiches to their lunch soups and salad has been delicious. The atmosphere is very casual and perfect for a breakfast/lunch. Would highly recommend!
My favorite place to study on campus. Great ambience, friendly staff, and extremely clean. After leaving campus, I have yet to find a cafe as good as Caffe Bene.

This is the place to go to satisfy your late night sweet tooth. I got the carrot cupcake and it was divine. Great flavor with lots of shredded carrots and really yummy frosting. I didn't feel it was overpriced at $4. Wish I could remember the guys name at the cash register. He was super friendly and nice. Will definitely be back!

Wow! Novel Ice Cream sure is a novelty. Their flavors are new, original, and magically unusual. Between the unexpected mix of a hot donut and ice cream to the flavor profiles ranging from an amaretto with animal cookies in a cone to a perfectly not too sweet honey lavender scoop it's pretty amazing. Love that their menu rotates and the possibility of trying even more flavors on my next visit.
Although the folks that they hire to work in there are a bit outlandish, the bakery goods are the best! Can't wait until they come back uptown!

well known for their cakes and pastries, but what s disappointing experience. The line was long and just when you reach to make your order; they get your order completely wrong. It was too long of a line plus too long on waiting for my order. Everything was sealed and package nicely, but to my horror it was not what I had ordered. Very disappointed that I could not taste what I had wanted.
Awesome donuts they were very moist, soft and fresh! I found my new donut bar! :). They also make cake donuts!

I'm ashamed to say I get the same thing every time I go... an egg sandwich on a buttery soft and flakey croissant. The coffee is great and the atmosphere is even better. It's a great place to have quick business meeting or sit and focus to get work done.
I'm disappointed... Cupcakes and cheesecake were awful!!! Not worth waiting in a long line!

The formula of the ice cream tastes very rich & creamy. One of the best ice creams I've ever tasted. Although it's overpriced for The works. They charge $1.50 for one marshmallow. Ended up paying $10 for an ice cream for two. It was tasty but other ingredients apart from the ice cream could have been better.

I loved this little..."boutique" bakery. Loved the decor and the laid back vibe. Loved the options for vegan or healthy choices (none of which I selected, mind you). Loved the blondie I had over coffee late at night (they're open late...another thing I loved). It was huge and delicious. Pretty much my only complaint was the dent it left in myfitnesspal calorie budget. And...by dent...I mean it obliterated it. That said...I didn't go there for the healthy options. I'll be back.
yummy macaroons! not the best, but they are pretty good. if you get the box of 6, you get a bit of discount. also, these macaroons are huge!

(3.25) ~ pretty good overall MENU: * Glazed Donut = (3.75) Good * Oreo Cupcake = (3.5) good, but prefer it to have Oreo filling. * Oreo Parfait = (3.25) pretty good * Triple Chocolate Chip Cookie = (3) ok, but prefer Cookies to be soft/fresher, not hard/crispy, which signals they were sitting out for awhile:(

I'm happy that Cosmo Vegas houses all these popular food spots from around the US (Hattie B's in Nashville, Pok Pok in Portland, Eggslut in LA) as I can get easier access to these foods when I'm in town. I've always been interested in Milk Bar and I missed my chance in trying it in NYC but I'm glad to see it has it's own place at Cosmo. Milk Bar is in the same space at Momofuku but separate so you can just wlak up and get your desserts. I did a YOLO Vegas move and got the greatest hits, which included 4 of their best selling items: birthday truffles (which came in 3), crack pie slice, compost cookie, and a cereal milk soft serve ice cream. I ate the ice cream right away and ate the others slowly in the coming days. The cereal milk ice cream had a great salty and sweet flavor. I am pretty sure that Afters Ice Cream (based in Orange County in CA) copied this flavor into their traditional non-soft served based ice cream, which is just as great. I really enjoyed this ice cream with the corn flakes. I tried the other desserts little by little, and I wasn't too impressed. The crack pie was good but way too rich and buttery; I would recommend sharing a slice with 2 or even 3 people of the same taste buds. The compost cookie had more of a coffee flavor which I wasn't too much of a fan of. The birthday truffles were good, but a little too rich as well; I probably could eat half of more truffle in one sitting. Overall, I do think Milk Bar is overrated and overhyped (sorry!) but the ice cream is something I would definitely get again when I visit Cosmo Vegas.

We did a Google search to find the best ice cream in Cleveland, and it directed us to Mitchell's. What a fantastic recommendation. We had cotton candy ice cream, which took me right back to my childhood, and strawberry cheesecake ice cream. The girls that worked there were so friendly and allowed us to sample different flavors. Overall a wonderful experience!

My favorite ice cream ever. I highly recommend their salty caramel truffle flavor, followed closely by Buckeye. I've never had anything but a dish of one of those flavors. No toppings, no shakes. I don't feel like I'm missing anything. There is no indoor seating and if you go on $2 Tuesday, expect a line. It will be worth it.

I want to love Amelie's. I'm a baker and lover of all things artsy and weird. But to me, that fifth star just isn't there. Let me explain my conundrum... The concept of a French bakery in Charlotte makes me swoon. Heck, the concept of any kind of bakery not inside a grocery store is a great. I have a long-standing affair with Parisian pastries and flaky breads. Caramel salted brownies? You guys go ahead...I'm going to hang around. The atmosphere is kitschy in a way that works. Incredibly odd light fixtures. Doorways in random places, a framed mirror that wraps around the corner, and a menagerie of random chairs and tables, like a home show for the Island of Misfit Toys. And, open 24 hours. In Charlotte. No further details needed. But, it is crowded. Very, crowded. With so few other options for the people still awake at 3am, the lines are always long. It's rare to find a table in the cafe-proper (better luck in the atrium common area behind their spot). And, (this is me being picky), there usually seem to be a few too many high schoolers who are just so cool and trendy it hurts (no, it really does hurt...my eyes can't take that much skinny jeans and awful plaid...but I digress). In my opinion, they are a bit pricey, too. Yes, they make great food. But $1.50 or $2 for something that is barely one bite? Amelie, I think we will have to continue our love-hate courtship. Let's just not assign a label and see where it goes.

Ice Cream Social is incredible! I started buying pints from Katrina during the pandemic - I've probably bought at least 20 so far. The flavors are unique and delicious. And the ice cream stays reasonably soft in the freezer, which is a huge bonus. My favorite thing to get at the shop is a flight so that I can try 3 different flavors, because it is hard to choose just one! I highly recommend getting waffle cone pieces as your topping. It's too hard to choose a favorite flavor! I don't like the ones with jam as much (personal preference), but I've enjoyed every flavor I have tried.

If you love soft serve, you'll love this place. There's always a huge line when you drive by, but it moves fast. Bring your cash, but if you forget, an ATM is around back. I live so close that if it's 9:55pm and I want some ice cream, I can squeeze it in prior to closing. So far I've had a chocolate shake, cake batter soft serve, and a brownie sundae - all were amazing. If you want actual ice cream, however, I suggest you mosey on over to Sugar and Spice.

I didn't actually end up trying anything because I was really low on cash and try to avoid using my credit card in places I haven't been before. But they were nice and let me take a photo of the menu and let me know they actually make ice cream on site, next time I need to literally walk down to the FBI building and back, maybe I'll stop in for a treat afterwards.

I'm pretty sure the Daily Scoop is half the reason I eventually ended up at UW-Madison. Between fourth and fifth grade I participated in College for Kids, and part of the routine was coming to the Union to get ice cream. They hooked me young, and I ended up back at UW despite relocating to the east coast. Chocolate peanut butter always has been and most likely always will be my favorite. You don't have to hunt for the peanut butter - there are big ol' swirls throughout. The prices are inexpensive, and a small is not that small. Hot tip: you can ask for half-and-half if you don't want all one flavor. On my most recent visit, I decided to mix it up with half cookie dough. Lots of cookie dough pieces and a nice smooth vanilla base. Definitely got two full scoops in my small dish. Are the lines going to be long in the summer time or during large events? Yep. In the summer the outdoor scoop stand is also usually open, though, and let's be real: you came to spend some time at the Union, you're probably not in an actual rush. Take the time in line to decide on the perfect flavor combination.

The pastries are absolutely divine! We had a bacon egg croissant and best cheese danish on the planet. That being said, the service was terrible. My husband had a 20 min break from his conference so we came here to grab a "quick" pastry. After 15 min of waiting for our croissant, my husband went to ask... well it was still in the toaster oven! The workers never apologized they just got another croissant and began toasting it again. Wish the staff was better trained on what to do in these kinds of situations, they were flustered and just gave us the new croissant and brushed us on our way.

Had the red velvet cupcake with red velvet ice cream. Cupcake was delicious and ice cream was just okay. My husband had the Capn' Crunch ice cream and it was the bomb! they do have their own outside seating so it's a nice place to take a break, just make sure you order something from Sprinkles or they will boot you out, saw it happen to a couple trying to eat their In n Out burgers there.

Ordered a small Coffee Oreo Snowstorm. I think it's a local favorite and definitely worth a try! The place is super cute and very homey, they have a lot of really interesting flavors and the service sizes are huge.
Very sugary, don't recommend having more than 2 haha. I liked it. Free parking in the back. It was just confusing leaving the parking lot.
The vegan dark chocolate was amazing. Other flavors were so creamy and good. Love seeing the ice cream being made. Fresh and local ingredients. Love this ice cream kitchen.

There are very few things in life that can make a grown man cry to the point of dehydration. Properly filled doughy plumped creamy confectionary dream deserts are definitely one of them! These little donuts come in various crafted toppings. Each cake is finished to perfection. I have bought a dozen with my family and alone have eaten 6 in one sitting while the car ran defrosting the windshield before heading back home. Did I mention this jaunt is a 30 minute drive from my home and worth every minute of travel and gas?
Me & my kids love the Vegan donuts at this place!!! Best Vegan donuts in town! They have a nice lil patio area in the back that we also enjoy. Everyone is super nice & friendly.

Wanted to participate in National Ice Cream Day. No specials, but the ice cream is bitchin'! So, why not! Settled on the Goat Cheese, Honey, and Pistachio. Holy F!!! I'm not one to seek out ice cream and if ever I do, I'm always for Ben & Jerry's "The Tonight Dough". Happy to make this a new alternative! Staff was friendly as well. I love receiving genuine customer service during moments of high volume and just before closing. Hope to see this place around for years to come!
Some of the best ice cream I've had! The Vietnamese coffee and Whiskey Toffee Almond are must gets.
Delicious, fast service, the macaron was perfectly cooked and the ice cream is incredible. A must visit in Charlotte. I would definitely go back.

Nice ice cream parlor in a small plaza even has a bak patio setting. Awesome choices of ice cream. Not ur average ice cream, just a tad bit different. Service good and prices fair, taste great. Id come bak. My son loves it!!

The rose milk tea latte is my wife's favorite in AZ. I enjoy their immunity-teas. Haven't had an item I didn't like yet. Plenty of parking and seating at this location. The ice cream looks great too but I don't have much of a sweet tooth to try. Looks like you can get it mixed with your favorite cereal.

Went here Tuesday 9/2 and there was only a short wait. The workers that helped me were very friendly and helpful. Everything I ordered was delicious especially the cannoli and lobster tail!!!!!! I will definitely go back on my next trip to Vegas!!!!
