Dripps also offers a soy milk option for their drinks too so rejoice! I'll be back again and again for that Rose Milk Latte. Pea flower tea? Sign me up!

Stopped by on recommendation from a local police officer. She was spot on. Great bakery. Muffins were cake like and addictive. Cookies were great. Cannoli was great, yet I have to say I do not eat it often. Staff was very helpful and friendly. I did give 5 stars yet I did not eat any other food. It looked great. A must stop for Little Italy.

Best cannoli I've ever eaten, but very pricey! We got 3 original cannoli and a traditional lobster tail and it totaled $23 seriously? $5 a pastry is pretty steep but like I said the cannoli was the best My husband and I have ever had and we will definitely come back for more cannoli next time we're in Vegas

Hands down the best macarons I have ever had. I saw the bakery and wanted to try some sweets so I got the chocolate almond toffee and a few macarons to snack on. The toffee tasted mostly of chocolate with a slight hint of toffee which was a disappointment. However.... the macarons were simply amazing! I have tried to find macarons that delicious and I've had no such luck. I'm ready to fly back just for some more sweets especially the salted caramel macarons!

Not much of a sweets fan but considering it was a highly anticipated and popular place to pop up, which branches in LA and NY, ... why not? lets try it ! My friend had gotten the Red Velvet. Prior to this place, our favorite was from a local bakery called Mad Hatters. Their cupcakes are about $4 ea, with a discount if bought in 1/2 or full dozen quantities. Despite the frosting being a bit sweet and a little hard, especially the candy cupcake topping (ours was a bunny), the cake portion of the cupcake is incredibly moist and flavorful. Something different about this specific place is they have a cupcake ATM outside. I believe their may be an additional charge (price comparison to purchasing inside, difference of maybe 50 cents - entertainment charge? haha). Select cupcake on the touch screen and out it comes like an ATM. Fun to watch XD Especially those who are trying to take a picture when the door opens, and it closes before they get to grab the cupcake. They freak out but somehow they are able to open the door again =X lol Little unique side note is their utensils are wooden vs the usual plastic. Outdoor seating next to the water fountains. Good to sit and relax on a nice day (had a little breeze but was still hot Q_Q)

The HYPE is real! Lol I actually really like this place, although my random craving for sweets is rare! Cupcakes and Ice Cream! What more can you ask for?! Had a scoop of the Cap'n Crunch (available all days of the week) in a Red Velvet Cone! Not too sweet, lil crunchy pieces in the ice cream were delicious! And the cone was amazing, only because I love anything red velvet! Lots of flavors (both cupcakes and ice cream) to choose from! Line gets long but worth the wait! Great place to check out especially if you're enjoying the new spot in Vegas, The LINQ!

I have been going to Jack Frost Donuts ever since I was a little kid. Their donuts have only gotten better over the years. I haven't ever visited during a time where I've had to wait in a line. They offer all different types of crazy varieties that would cost at least double in a large city. One of my favorites is the Fat Elvis. Jack Frost is a serious gem in Cleveland, and if you haven't been yet, you're missing out!

Since we live in Cali, the chances of us getting out to Hoboken, NJ are extremely slim. That's why we were excited to see a Carlo's Bakery in Vegas! As fans of the show we felt it our duty to buy a handful of desserts and sample them all. We bought the chocolate and regular cannolis, chocolate and vanilla cupcakes, sugar cookies, chocolate chip cookies, and a cheesecake with chocolate mousse on top. Overall, we weren't too impressed. The cannoli's were ok (chocolate was best), cookies tasted a day old and were hard, cheesecake didn't taste much like cheesecake but more like the cannoli cream which didn't have much flavor. We didn't sample the cupcakes, we are leaving those for the kids. It was a fun experience but honestly, not the most delicious desserts we've ever had. We ageed, though the desserts were fun to eat, they weren't anything to rave about. Hopefully we just came on an off day.

I have debated even writing this review because the situation was tainted with a mistake I made but overall terrible service. I purchased $50 of cannolis and lobster tails. I didn't realize they needed to be refrigerated. I thought it was similar to a cupcake. I didn't realize it was made with cheese. My bad. I don't fault the store but they all went bad except the cannoli I ate right after leaving which was okay tasting. As for line. Only 3 or 4 in front of me. I told them 2 cannolis and 4 lobster tails. They said they only had the lobster tails in hazelnut so I said that was fine. Then they went in back to get them and I didn't realize they had to wait for them to bake and fill them. Took 20 minutes and nobody came out to check on me or tell me a time frame. I only knew because of the see through glass. Then it all spoiled. Such a waste of time and money l.

I don't normally write review reviews for donut shops but Jack Frost Donuts is the exception. My wife and I were traveling through Cleveland on one of our road trips and stopped in to Jack Frost Donuts as it was highly recommended. We were impressed by everything. The store was immaculate, the staff was friendly and most of all the donuts are exceptional. We had the good fortune to meet Fred who is the owner and he gave us a sample of some of the donut holes. We had a great conversation with Fred and he is an amazing guy who we won't soon forget. We ended up taking a dozen donuts home. They really are the best donuts we've ever tasted. If you're ever in the area you really should try some for yourself.

Their apple fritter was a complete fail. No flavor, no sweetness, nothing special about it. Apple fritters are my absolute favorite donut, so I'm very let down by theirs. On a positive note... the Homer donut was amazing !!!! Very soft, very sweet, a complete 10 out of 10 score. Also amazing is their Strawberry Cheesecake donut. The perfect amount of filling and also very soft donut, oooo sooo yummy. I wouldn't mind if they added more graham cracker crumbs on top. I've never had a bad Chai Latte, so I was very pleased by theirs. My junk food sidekicks ordered the following: Creme BrÃ»lÃ©e, maple bacon bar, triple chocolate threat, bacon cinnamon roll, and the caramel latte donuts. No complaints from them. Apparently the bacon cinnamon rolls was out of this world delicious.

They got my order wrong. I told three people, the strawberry shortcake NOT the chocolate strawberry. I pointed at it, told them explicitly not the chocolate and at the register she said chocolate and I said, "no I told two people not the chocolate!" Charged me for the vanilla I wanted, I opened the box and what do you know, it was chocolate. Mind you, the vanilla/strawberry thing was the only thing not labeled and I assumed it was strawberry shortcake but apparently wasn't exactly what it was called and that's what got everybody confused and it turns out it was what it's called but I'm not the one who didn't label it. So they got my order wrong, and the Oreo and the chocolate/strawberry tower I got wasn't even that good. The vanilla cupcake wasn't any better. The buttercream tasted like buttercream from albertsons cupcakes. And mind you, this isn't a bad review just because they got my order wrong and I'm salty about it. I was hoping the cake and pastries would make up for it and they sadly didn't. You pay for the name and that's it. Sprinkles has WAY better cupcakes. Which is where I went after to soothe my pain of a terrible cupcake I spent 6 dollars on, I got a 1000% better one for half the price.

I brought my children along with 2 nephews to Las Vegas for my sons birthday. They were excited to go to the bakery. On Saturday we got there and got #67 they were on 25 an hour later they were on number 33. The staff was extremely slow and seemed to be in no rush whatsoever. Sunday morning we went again at 830am thinking they wouldn't have such a long wait, and again we got number 67! This time they were on number 47... This is what I don't understand if they have two people helping the customers and they each take 10-15 minutes per customer then the cashier isn't doing anything for 10 minutes at a time. After 30 minutes we left they only moved up 4 numbers. My son was extremely disappointed and it was a sour end to his birthday. A person would think that they would put at least 4 people during peek times.
I stopped by around 11 pm they only had one flavor available . The soft serve was terrible and expensive! . Mc Donald's ice scream tasted better than this !

I love Mitchell's. I wish yelp would switch to either a point system, so I could give a 4.8, or allow us to give 1/4, 1/2, or 3/4 stars, so I could have left 4-3/4 stars I always get the hot fudge sundae, with different ice creams. I always get it to-go, and ask for the toppings on the side, and they are very accommodating! The only thing, they're a little stingy with the fudge, especially given the amount of ice cream you get. That's why they didn't get that fifth star .So I request extra fudge topping, and though I'm happy to pay a little for an extra container, sometimes they charge, sometimes they don't. I live pretty close to the W25 St. headquarters, and always go to that store. I like that they left the lobby the way it was! The only problem, and it is a HUGE one, is the extremely limited parking. I am disabled, and there's a HP spot around the corner, but I have never seen it unoccupied, so I have to park further away or just go home, depending on how well I can walk that day. I would have docked them a star or two for that, because they chose to open in that location, but that's life in the city! Every business in the area has the same problem. I did explain my disability (above knee amputee on crutches) to an employee and asked if I could park in the back for a few minutes to get my to-go order, and was told no. I don't see why they can't put an HP spot there, for to-go only. I think that would be a reasonable accommodation.

I adore this place located on The Linq Promenade. The baked goods and service are both equally exceptional. I had the pineapple upside down cupcake. It was cute and delicious. It had a moist rich taste with yummy pineapple goodness in the center. The icing was perfection. They have window seating to allow customers to look out while dining. I also appreciated the environmentally paid decision of bamboo forks, I noticed that and it was a nice touch.

This place is insanely good! Honestly Ice Cream is Ice Cream its the additional things that are what I look for. Thus, it's no wonder that this place would tickle my fancy. I love marshmallow topping, not fluff and not actual marshmallows but the liquidy marshmallow syrupy goodness. That is what they have at Chocolate Shoppe, Thank God! Also the fact that they have bomb ass italian ices is a definite A+ in my opinion!

Mitchell's has a strange combination of delectable sweets along with a sterile lab look right behind the cashier. It's an interesting concept to have glass walls so everyone can peer in to the workers dressed in white coats and masks working to make delicious ice cream. There is also a second floor which made it feel a bit more like a zoo. But who am I to complain about an ice cream zoo. They have different and unique varieties of ice cream so I will definitely come back here if I ever visit again!
Good ice cream, but nothing spectacular. Had the brownie swirl, which had good taste but felt like it was missing something to make it special. Good service as well.
4 stars for Americano, was a little watered down. Will try asking for extra espresso next time. We had pistachio macarons, cream danish and focaccia -- these get 5 stars!

I think the most entertaining aspect of Fatty Daddy's is the people that work there! I've only been later in the evenings, which is awesome because they are open late! Their ice cream flavors are unique and not something you'll find at any other ice cream place. Their macaroons and toasted marshmallow are sometimes stale-tasting, which is why I didn't give a 5 star review. But they still taste good and it's just a fun experience when you're not in the mood for DQ or Dreyers. Lucky for them they are the only ice cream shop in the surrounding area. I hope they stay in business and do well because it really is a fun treat to eat! My hubsand LOVESSSS them and thinks they deserve at least seven stars...

Best ice cream ever? Is that too much of a stretch? I don't think so. The bacon ice cream is a must. If you haven't had it, you need to try it. If you had it and didn't like it, give it another chance. It is fantastic. Over the holidays I had their candy cane ice cream. That was probably one of the best ones I have ever tried there. I first got it at the ice cream truck at the Scottsdale Farmers Market, then I had to stop by the store and get two more scoops on my way home. Yeah, it was that good. Bonus: I just saw that they serve the ice cream fresh at whole foods a few weeks ago. I knew they sold the pints, but back by the cakes/cupcakes/goodies they have the scoop-able Sweet Republic ice cream bar. If you ever need an ice cream fix, this is the place to go. When family and friends come to visit, this is the place to go. Pretty much a must eat in Scottsdale.
Once again. The guy taking orders is so rude. Why does he even still work here? Get rid of him!!! Management needs to do something.
We loved it here! We had a hard time deciding on which donut we wanted.....so we had to buy a dozen variety.

I tried Crack Pie, Cereal Milk ice cream, cheese and eggs bread. Food tastes bland, monotonous in flavor, overly sweet, and definitely overpriced. I would not eat here again. Desserts do not need to be overly complex but when they are like at Milk then they'd better be amazing. They are below average. I do not understand the hype. Any dessert at the Wicked Spoon buffet would hands down beat what Milk sells. They were nice to give us a cup of cold water which was refreshing and good!

You want a fantastic dessert, head to the Day& Night Exotic Cereal Bar!! The hardest part was deciding which shake to have. After a few minutes of reading all the different shakes, we decided on the Homer Simpson and the Buttercup shakes - so so good!!!

What could be more perfect on Friday for lunch than Amelie's? Nothing! Everything was perfect, from the croque monsieur to the salted caramel tart...yum! It is so hard to narrow down what I want to eat when I go there; everything is amazing. The quirkiness of the decor just adds to the overall experience. I love Amelie's and will continue to come back often.

Bad news SR has been hit with the ghostly, unsolvable "sulfur / egg / sewer / hair salon" stink that attacks all Scottsdale businesses that don't complain to the city. I swear there's a valve the city opens and closes to push the odor to the next business when the previous one complains. I've smelled it from Frank Lloyd Wright to Shea. Make no mistake about it, when you walk in it smells putrid. Service - Older lady working all alone that can only do one thing at a time complaining about how her arm is going to get a good workout today. Slow to say the least and theres hardly anyone in here. Ice Cream - Delicious, original, something that sort of makes the comments above worth it. Please, remove that funky air you got up in there.

My boyfriend has lived in LV in nearly 40 years. Me: 8. He knows every spot for everything, so, when I pull a trick he hasn't seen from my hat, and he loves it, it makes me super happy. Handle's is the bomb. No tables. No fussy nonsense. Old-school all the way! Casua, order at the window and chill on a bench or in the car goodness. Hand made, fresh everything. Ultra clean kitchen. Hand paked pint to-go for his son, because it's that good.

my husband & i came to scottsdale to enjoy a staycation. came to sweet republic bc it looked amazing. walked in, no one greeted us for at least 5 minutes. there were 3 other customers as well & none of us were being helped. looked as tho the one worker present was doing online orders? not sure, but not even a "welcome in/i'll be right with you" .. finally a girl came out from the back (still haven't been greeted) & all she says is "do u have a mask?" my husband did & i asked if there was one there & she said "they're 50 cents" ... she then leaned into her coworker & started whispering. fair assumption that it was about us. we walked out while she glared at us. will never go back & never recommend.

After seeing this place pop up on my yelp, I thought id give it a try since we were in the area. We went on a Sunday afternoon so there was no waiting and we were able to order right away. My husband ordered the Thai tea and I ordered the vanilla soft serve infused with fruity pebbles topped with circus animal cookies. You can order from one of their pre made menu or create your own. They offer a variety of ingredients you can infuse into your ice cream. The way the mix the ingredients into the ice cream makes it taste so good. I got mine in a cup so I can share with my little one or you can order your ice cream on a waffle cone. They also offer drinks & teas if you're not in the mood for some ice cream. Definitely come try this place out :)

If you are a Gen Z'er, my apologies, but...         We are going back to the 80's!!! To my fellow Millennial's...                  Welcome Back!!  Bust out that Walkman, pop in that mixtape and let's break it down with M.C. Hammer.  Translation for Gen Z:    Bro, Did you just see drakes Live Stream of Toosie Slide drop on TikTok.                (Or something like that) In the 80's, we had commercials that we had no choice but to watch with catch phrases like `Milk Does a body good' or those `Got Milk?' Ads.  Today... You can fast forward to the best part of your buddy falling head first while attempting The Milk Box Challenge all for receiving those 8 trillion views.  FUN FACT: My fellow Millennial Co-worker said that they used Elmers glue, not actual milk to portray the milk mustache's in those Got Milk? Ads.  Today, Times are different, but I'm 100% positive the Gen X'ers once thought all Millennials were straight up whack.  But one thing we can All agree on... No matter what generation you are from, Milk & Cookies are NEVER going away!  ------------How the cookie crumbled------------ During a recent trip to Las Vegas, I tested the 80's theory that Milk does a body good and went to the Milk Bar located inside the beautiful Cosmopolitan Resort.  Im gonna be honest... not to detour you,  not to shape your opinion, not even to make you think twice... But my family and I were just not fans.  True story...  You know the saying, "Don't cry over spilled milk?" Well, crying we did not. (Read more for why)  We ordered a cup of their Cereal Milk soft serve with sprinkles and a prepackaged confetti cookie.  The cereal milk soft serve looked pretty, but was way too sweet and just was not our thing.  The cookie although fresh, tasted a bit chemically/processed and we landed up tossing it after a few bites.  About 100 feet from Milk, our 3 year old dropped the soft serve on the floor after each of us just having a bite or two.  Normally, I would cry after dropping 14 bucks on a dessert that I only got 1 spoonful of, but because 1 spoonful was all I needed to form my opinion of whether milk truly does a body good, I think next time I will just order a bottle of Elmer's glue and call it a day.

I am very particular about bakery, I don't splurge on it very often, so I want it to be excellent when I do. The Batch house Bakery never disappoints! I usually get a filled croissant but their Buttercake with raspberry and cream topping was to die for! Well worth the visit and I plan my next trip already.
Loved the interior design, the music and the staff. It's a nice little shop, with outdoor seating and nice lights. Mucha Lucha was so tastyy, that I will definitely have to come back for some more.
If you like PB & chocolate ice cream w/ salted caramel, nuts all in one place try the "kitchen sink" omg ! Great atmosphere on the shady back patio !
No line no wait and think the price is slightly cheaper then the in west 4 NYC location. Always love their cereal milk soft serve with crunch.

This is now one of my favorite places in San Francisco. My son took us to this spot on our last visit to him in Oakland , and believe me it was well worth it. If you are a Ghirardelli chocolate lover already then this place is the cherry on top. The smells are amazing. The ice cream shop located in the store on the upper level is, I have no words to describe it. It was a cold day and we decided to have hot chocolate. The best cup of hot chocolate I've ever had. While we were there they were giving out sample candies for Valentine's Day. Again heavenly. The building is historic and evokes memories of a time passed. Picture opportunities galore and cool spots to just hang out and talk. If you're in the Frisco area bear pier 39 look them up and stop by for some good old fashion chocolate.

Came from Los Angeles to visit . We fell in love with this ice cream parlor. Love that they add little toys on the ice cream for the kids . Life the banana flavor ice cream. I will drive here just for the ice cream .

This place is awesome. Do they have 300 flavors with 600 toppings? No. That's probably why this place is so awesome. I need to start out with something about the lady who was working. I'm assuming she was an owner or someone else deeply involved in the whole process, and she was more than willing to fill us in on where the ingredients came from or any other details which she deemed necessary. They mostly weren't necessary but when you have someone that is that into what they are doing, you gotta have some love for it. Between the 4 of us we probably had 12 or so samples, and we did so without a bad look or skip in the record of our servers in depth guide to the flavors. I settled on the salted caramel ice cream, which was phenomenal. Silky, smooth, and buttery like a kobe bryant jump shot. Its 9AM right now and my mouth is watering thinking about it. There are so many flavors that you just generally would never see and as weird as they may seem, they all taste great. Next time in Scottsdale, theres a good chance I will hopefully be able to visit this hot spot (cool spot) again.
Friendly workers and patient with the customers trying different flavors. The perfect place to bring a date. Try the UBE!!!! Masons does me dirty every time!!!!

The absolute best dessert place/bakery in Charlotte. My wife and I have been going to the batchmaker before she had a brick and mortar location and she never disappoints. Her second location and the quality and consistency remains. Do yourself a favor and order 2 oatmeal cream pies if there's any in stock!

I would recommend this place to anyone, nice place to grab coffee, do work and grab food. Staff is easy going, and the owner is super nice and inspiring. The Noda location is open 24/7. Great community partnership! Thanks Amelie's!
Hands down Best Bakery in Cleveland!!! My absolute favorite is their peanut butter brownies. They are like crack!!!! Rich creamy and oh so delicious.

Okay their food is top notch. Fresh baked pastries, sandwiches, and creamy gelato. You can't go wrong here. The staff is friendly and the service is quick. Love it! What I didn't love was seeing flies in the case with all the desserts. I guess I expected controlling the flies to be better when in a bake shop in Little Italy. That was so much of a turn off I had to give Presti's 3 stars. However, the case that didn't have flies were the cakes. I had the tiramisu which was so creamy and light! I took some hazelnut biscottis home and paired them with a chai tea. Despite the flies, (I'm sure it was just a busy or off day) I will definitely go again because honestly, you just can't find delectable Italian baked goods in many places in Northeast Ohio that are sold at a very reasonable price.
Every Sprinkles is good. Oh so good. Mmmmmm. (recommend the dark chocolate, and if you want to try a ton of cupcakes, get all the minis). PLUS THERES A SPRINKLES ICE CREAM SHOP TO THE RIGHT.

This is a bittersweet post because my favorite ice cream place of all times for the past 11 years has now been trumped by JENI'S!!! All I can say is WOWWWWW! She is a chemical genius!! Literally she uses her secular chemical engineering education to satisfy our sweet palates! I tried almost every flavor and they were so creamy and heavenly! My favorite was the gooey butter cake which literally had a freshly hand made butter cake mixed throughout the ice cream. My husband had a flight of three flavors and wanted more right away. We are visiting from Houston and KNOW this would kill out there! So Jeni if you are listening, please bring this gem to HTown! The people need better ice cream!!!! Please please please and thank you!! Oh and you can order them shipped to you online in pints from her original location in Ohio. $12 per pint and you have to order at least 3 at a time which when you taste them you will see is not a problem lol they also sell her ice cream in select Publix grocery stores.

Meh. We were there at 11 am on a Saturday morning after we'd gone to Donutmania and found a poor selection. Donut bar had even fewer...maybe 20 but not a great variety. We got a maple bacon apple fritter--the last one. It was the only one left that wasn't just a "regular" donut. After all, we went there to try a fun, different type of donut, not just an old fashioned or a glazed donut. So, the "bacon" is just bacon bits that you buy in a jar--not real, fresh bacon crumbles like I expected. The fritter was dry and didn't have nearly enough apple in it nor glaze on it. Had it been real bacon, and more apple, maybe it would have been worth the $4. Otherwise, I'd just stick to a national donut chain who knows what they're doing.

Wow! A hot delicious soft donut with the most delectable Madagascar vanilla ice cream I've ever had in my life. This place is incredible. It is located behind Third Space in a pink little house. Great flavors but I'm a purist and went with vanilla...it was incredible.

Cupcakes are to die for, the cake is delicious and the frosting WOW!!!! Hands down best frosting I have ever had. I tried the lobster tail, original filling. I feel like there was too much filling, but the pastry itself is so crispy fresh and really good. Went on a Sunday morning and unfortunately they didn't have cannoli's made yet, so picked up some cupcakes. Don't skip on the cupcakes!!

FYI, this is review is of their truck that was at First Friday... I would like to state that I am observing no-meat Fridays during this Lenten season. I managed to avoid meat at the other food trucks, but decided to break it for dessert. It was sinfully delicious........ Some of the flavors they had on hand were Belgian Chocolate, Mint Chip, Salted Butter Caramel, White Rose and I Heart Bacon. They also had a pomegranate sorbet. I think it was blueberry pomegranate. After reading reviews of Sweet Republic, I knew they were known for their gourmet flavors so my choices on Friday were between White Rose and I Heart Bacon. I'm not a big fan of rose flavor.. so I ordered a single scoop ($3) of bacon flavored ice cream. The initial bite was confusing. My mind knew I was eating ice cream, but didn't understand why there was a hint of smoked bacon with my dessert. It was an unusual flavor, but after about 3 bites it grew on you. In the ice cream were pieces of bacon and I think some maple flavored toffee. Those sugary, maple-y pieces were a really good accompaniment to the bacon. All in all, trying this bacon ice cream was worth the three dollars, plus a few Hail Marys.

Hands down the best ice cream in Arizona. The flavors are exactly as described and always flavorful and delicious! If you want ice cream that is hand made and worth the price come here. They have seasonal and holiday special flavors as well. My favorite is a honey lavender flavor I think should be added to the permanent menu it's that amazing. A little pricey but worth it! I think they deserve to be at a better location and in a prettier shop! Because this is top notch ice cream. The shop is in a very unassuming low key shopping area and is a little out dated in decour, in fact you might miss it if you drive by. But if you stop In, it will be worth the effort. I would call this place a hidden gem! They even put chocolate in the bottom of their cones so the cones don't drip, and they will give you ice if your traveling with your sweets!
Favorite ice cream place in Phoenix. The area is safe and located next to a little shopping plaza that's great for a short walk while eating Churn's ice cream.

Oh Bouchon, you've made me an addict. I trekked to your enclave under the escalator in the Venetian three times in a 24 hour period and spent $20 on your crack-like goodies. I was dismayed that you didn't offer the almond croissants that your Yountville sister has in abundance, but your kind worker comforted me with a strawberry croissant with a light taste of almond paste. Too bad my buzz from Fat Tuesday prevented me from tasting it properly. But alas, it was this buzz that helped me shell out $4 for almost every baked goody I ordered. The macarons were heavenly, and much bigger than those in Yountville. I fell in love with your $3.25 goodness. The chocolate chip cookie was a tad brittle, but the buttery fluffiness of the croissant and pain au raisin helped numb the pain in my teeth. If only your prices were a tad lower (why is it cheaper in Yountville of all places?), I would love you forever. Bouchon does wonders with butter.

Visited Mason's for their winter ramen a few weeks ago and it did not disappoint! We tried the pork and the mushroom options that were available that night, both were delicious. I also ordered the homemade chamomile ginger iced tea which was delightful, only slightly sweet (how I like it) and went well with the ramen.
Amazing frozen custard. I like to stick to the basics -- vanilla or chocolate on a waffle cone. The stuff is just great.

This is one of those businesses that makes you reassess your whole rating system. Novel Ice Cream is such a perfect business, it makes me wonder if I've been too generous with most of my previous ratings. Novel is located in a tiny little house(?) in a strange little section of downtown Phoenix, right at the corner of a residential neighborhood. We happened to walk in at an apparently uncommon moment (Sunday around 4pm) during which there were no other customers in the store, so I cannot speak to the typical crowds or parking situation. The people working that day, including one of the owners, Brandon, were incredibly friendly and helpful and clearly genuinely passionate about their store and their ice cream. They encouraged us to try lots of different flavors and excitedly gave detailed descriptions of the ice cream, its ingredients, and the hand-crafted process involved in making it. It's always special when you find a family owned and operated establishment in the Phoenix area, but it's especially rare and invigorating to find one this full of passion and enthusiasm. For the experience alone, this place is a 5, and then there's the actual ice cream. It's incredible. The flavors are unique and interesting, and the exceptional care that goes into crafting their flavors is immediately evident. Everything tastes real, flavorful and balanced. The doughnut used in the dough melt is warm and soft and perfectly compliments whatever ice cream you choose to put inside it. I had the Thai Tea ice cream in a Dough Melt with Captain Crunch topping, but I tried samples of most of the other flavors on offer that day as well. My partner got a scoop of the Raspberry sorbet and the Lemon Basil sorbet, both of which were also excellent. This is definitely a place you can bring your vegan and dairy-free friends and you will all leave satisfied. Novel is one of my favorite types of places: the kind of place that, for a moment, makes the big city feel like a small town. It's a rare gem, and owners Brandon and Jennifer deserve every bit of praise that's been heaped upon them.

French cafe with vibrant and eclectic decors. The dark roast drip coffee was smooth and nutty. Although the spot is known for its caramel brownie, personally it did not impress me that much. it's too little brownie for too much money, and too sweet for my taste. Regardless it's a fun place to get coffee

I was really excited to visit this famous Charlotte patisserie not only because everyone was raving about the their delicious tarts, croissants, & eclairs, but also because it's open ALL THE TIME (24hrs/day, 7 days a week, 365 days a year) and they are welcoming of all kinds of people to hangout, read, study. First off, the good: - Salted Caramel Brownie (5 stars): the PERFECT contrast of smooth sweet/salty caramel atop a thin but dense (and slightly crunchy) chocolate brownie. You must try this if you love either caramel or brownies! - Their creme brÃ»lÃ©e was delicious, and the fact that they flambÃ©/torch it only when ordered so it's warm, fresh, and crispy was a nice touch. - Finally, the chocolate eclair and mixed-berry tart were both very decent and I'd happily order them again. The only downside is that it was abundantly clear that those long hours really diminished the quality of at least 2 of their items: - The croissant: I had already ordered a few items so I wasn't planning to get anything else, but I'm a sucker for a great croissant and the lady at the counter said it was fresh baked that morning, so I happily ordered it expecting a soft, flaky, buttery snack. Unfortunately what I got was hard and dry; honestly, I've had day old croissants taste fresher than this! I have no doubt that if it were fresh out of the oven it would have been amazing, but someone definitely wasn't keeping track of how old/dry these were. - The sticky-bun (mini cinnamon roll + raisins & extra sugar glaze on top): it also was was disappointingly "aged" liked the croissant, and although I've got a notorious sweet tooth, this tasted way too sugary too me. Overall, I'd definitely come back for their delicious snacks/desserts that are not too perishable and to try their famous macaroons. As for the disappointing croissant, I'd be willing to try it again if I KNEW it was fresh, but otherwise skip it.

This one is my favorite of the Amelie's. Maybe because it was my first but I think it's because of the quaintness of the place and the many places you can sit with friends or get some work done. Their bakery is endless. Never know what to get but typically select something that has raspberries. Bottom line... you can't go wrong. Located in Noda I love going to Amelies any time it's open. The smell Itself will wish you away. Enjoy
Generous portions friendly service and great location. Great and everything, but this ice cream is incredible. We tried blue moon, iced latte with chocolate chunks, and cookies and cream. Wow

great ice cream and great location! the only down side is it's more on the pricy side. we got the order of the Trio, i believe it was $6. one friend of ours got a pint of the pineapple upside down cake flavor (sorry not pictured) and I got to say that might be my favorite flavor so far! most jeni's ice cream are more on the sweeter side but the pineapple upside down cake had a hint of sourness to it. it was just amazing I would highly recommend!

If you are looking for a fantastic and unique ice cream shop, stop by Mason's Creamery! Upon arriving, I was extremely surprised to not see any of the original flavors such as chocolate or vanilla on the menu. Instead there were unique flavors such as ube and cookie butter. I ordered the two scoops of cookie butter and peanut butter butterfinger and it was delicious. My parents also ordered the root-beer float with vanilla malt ice cream which was perfect for a sunny hot day. The service was very nice and patient and the ambience was a plus. They had nice outdoor seating in the back that made the environment feel homey and fun. You can tell the team of employees are working very hard to create new flavors. I would definitely return here for more deliciousness. Fun rumor: I heard they also serve ramen in the winter time. I will need to check that out for sure!

Let me start by saying I'm 9 months pregnant and due any day...Tonight I had a random craving for a warm donut with ice cream on top. My husband laughed and said I would have to invent that because he didn't think it existed. I googled exactly that "warm donut with ice cream" and the skies opened up and and heaven sent down this amazing little shop! We drove 20 minutes to get here and after having it I would have driven twice that far. It's a good thing I didn't find this place sooner in my pregnancy or else I'd be the size of a whale, but dangit it'd be happy. I had a warm glazed donut with peanut butter and jelly ice cream and captain crunch for the topping....yes, that. Just. Happened.
This place is legit! Good location, extremely good ice cream (tried the Wildberry and Almond brittle combo) Flavors are very fresh and the waffle cone smell mesmerizes

Early morning Coffee and pastries in Vegas. The line was pretty long but the staff was efficient in getting orders out. The pricing was average for the resort. I got the cream cheese danish which was really good and a latte. Great place for grab and go.

It was okay. I was really excited to try this and looked at the menu. Personally I wanted to try the cereal soft serve since it sounds so delicious and just make you think that you're back to a being a kid. Also the crack pie! Heard lots of good things about it. When my boyfriend and I came there, they let us have samples which was pretty cool. The consistency of their product is pretty good. Their ice creams were smooth and silky but I didn't grab them cause they were too SWEET! I love sweet stuff but this one went over. After buying a crack pie and the cereal soft serve, I tried the cereal first and it was just meh. It's literally some upgraded vanilla ice cream. I didn't let that bother me cause I thought the cereal around it would make up for it. But no. It was just meh. It literally just tasted like regular corn flakes from Trader's Joe. The crack pie was good tho but was really reaaalllyyyy small for the price.

This is seriously THE BEST ice cream I have had. EVER. IN MY LIFE. Like better than Sprinkles or Cold Stone or anywhere seriously oh my goodness. I'm lactose intolerant but I ate every bit of my butter pecan ice cream and #noregrets!! The place is super cute inside too!! Also the girls that were working were very nice and they gave me another ice cream cone after I accidentally dropped mine on the counter right after they gave it to me.... Lol thanks guys!! :)

This place is lovely! We just went to the new one in Van Aken! It sells all the classic flavors like sea salt Carmel, cookie dough and rocky road. They have large Sunday's and delicious milkshakes! This is a super fun place to bring kids or just get a quick treat!

I love Jack Frost donuts because they have delicious, large classic donuts that come in a variety of traditional and newer flavors. And the pricing is very reasonable especially compared to other donut shops of similar offerings in the Cleveland area. Bought a dozen to share with friends. Pictured here include maple bacon, fruity pebbles, Cocoa Puffs, Banana cream pudding!

3.95 for a regular croissant????? Get real! And it wasn't even that good. I've had better at Lee's sandwich or even La Madeleine. Though they did have fresh squeezed orange juice... but I think they may have added some sugar. Boo... I was hoping to eat a great croissant each morning. Maybe if it came out fresh... I totally forgot to try the chocolate one though.

Bakery heaven. After hearing so many raving reviews about this place I decided on a Sunday afternoon that I had to make the trek to Willy St. to try it out. And whoa, yeah it's that good. I only tried the Ham and Gruyere Croissant and the Cranberry Walnut Scone with Orange Glaze but holy crap. There was so much filling in that croissant! Probably the biggest and most tasty one I've ever had. The ham was so yummy (saw it was from Jordandal - yay!). The perfect amount of ham and cheese made for a delicious snack. I ate the scone the next morning for breakfast and it was still moist and delicious. I may just have to make this a new weekend routine.

So we really wanted gelato but there are almost no legit gelato places in Charlotte! The best one closed down. Anyway searched for ice cream and found this. We had the ice cream bun sandwich. They have some on the menu with specific ice cream flavors but you can get any. We got the dark chocolate truffle.I have no idea how they prevent the icecream from melting in the hot bun! It was delicious!! We also got the mango drink which is SO FRIKKIN AMAZING!!! It's spicy and sweet, love the mango Chile straw and the tamarind candy!!! Oh my! I highly recommend it. I liked it more than the icecream!!

both times I've been, their boba is cooking and won't be done for about 30mins. What is the point in offering boba tea when your boba isn't ready ever. Maybe start making the boba before you open? Giving up on this place.
This place is awesome! Get the Cookie Cup. Delicious ice cream sandwiched between 2 macaroons. Awesome!

I am not impressed and quite frankly I think this place is overrated. Yes, for local standards their bread is better than the usual horrors of American bread. That said, the bread is not great. I bought a baguette at Batch Bakehouse on a Saturday morning, by 3 pm it was hard and stale. This tells me that the bread was either already a day old when I bought it, or they don't know what they are doing. I spent the better part of my life in Europe and believe me, fresh bread does not behave like this. The brownies they sell are way too sweet and the croissants are just meh. While I am willing to pay $$$ for good bread and baked items, I don't think that their quality and price match.

What was I thinking???? I love everything about this place but the food I had. So how in the world can I give it four stars? First, I LOVE French Bakeries. I have the best story about Alon's in Atlanta but that can wait for another day. I drove this morning from Raleigh to Atlanta and realized quickly that Charlotte could be the location for a late breakfast. Then I realized there was a French Bakery in Charlotte that was on one of Google's experimental sites that I visited this past weekend. It was a 24 hour bakery that had a 360 degree camera going in the kitchen so you could watch the food being prepared any time you click the link. The site is: chromeweblab.com/en-GB/t¦ . I got there at 10-ish and starved. Instead of a getting a great pastry (and I have zero doubt that they make an astounding eclair, I got the breakfast sandwich with sausage and egg. The croissant was amazing but the "other stuff" was just too overwhelming. Like I said, I can't blame anyone but myself. If I wanted breakfast, I should have stopped at an "Awful Waffle" The deco is great. It was full but not packed (10 am on Wed:) ). The service was punctual, but not overly friendly. No snide remarks about the French, please. I am going to give this place another shot, for sure.

The. Best. The. End. Kidding, Yelp makes me say more in order for the review to be 'recommended.' First, you get to try any and all flavors you want. They don't want to feeling guilty to keep asking for tastes, and do a great job of encouraging it. They only do small batch ice cream, so the flavors are constantly rotating. I won't say every ice cream was my cup of tea, but that's just fine since they let me taste until I find perfection. Price point is very fair, and the portion size is perfect-- it's small enough that you don't feel like a glutton, and big enough to be fully satisfied. I've been here three times now. I went for my first time on a Friday night, and loved it so much I had to take my roommate the very next day. I'll keep on coming back! Service, price, flavor, ambience-- every part of this place is five stars.
Real ice cream, natural flavors that do not taste artificial at all, and friendly service. There really is not much more to say. Best ice cream place in Vegas that I have tried.

Best egg tarts I've tasted! I've tried all The bakeries in Chinatown, Vegas . I also tried a few in San Fran! The crust is flaky and buttery and the egg tart it's self is delicious! I also got some chocolate strawberries and cream puff pastry. All of the pastries look yummy the establishment is very clean I think they've been here for a little bit over two years maybe but I love this little place and I went early because this parking lot gets very busy

Enjoyed their classic hot fudge sundae last night. Delicious as always. I typically get these at Giants games in San Francisco. I never thought I'd be paying more for these anywhere else than at the ballpark, but Vegas managed to do that, $14 each. Oh well, I'm on vacation. Nevertheless, it's always fun to visit a premium chocolate shop. We didn't buy anything else besides a couple sundaes, I'd have had to sell an extra kidney to do so. You're better off financially buying their product at Costco. Staff were friendly, pleasant ambiance.
A little pricey but top notch and service is exceptional! Everyone's so friendly and helpful.

Batch bakehouse has so many wonderful pastry and other baked good options! I got the almond chocolate croissant, which was so delicious. The almond icing on the top makes it a much sweeter pastry, but I am generally never one to say "no" to more sugar, so it worked for me. And, the almond chocolate croissant was the same price as the regular chocolate one ($3.25). Overall, the croissant was a great mix of flaky on the outside and soft on the inside... yum!! The bakery is in an adorable area, has friendly staff and nice, bright lighting! A great place to stop in for a treat or meet a friend to enjoy some delicious Madison sweets.

Hands-down best ice cream I've ever had. The fresh, local ingredients and careful preparation make their ice cream not only a delicious treat, but also a refreshing one! Every location I've been to has been consistent (which is hard to find with a chain), but the original Ohio City location definitely has an awesome atmosphere!
One word, OHSOYUMMY! Worth every penny, smooth creamy, great flavor selections. Unless you are lactose intolerant, you won't be disappointed, but you better eat quick or it will get messy

We got the Trio flight with an additional scoop since it was hard for us to narrow down to 3 flavors. My favorite is the Brown Butter Almond Brittle and the Honey Vanilla Bean. Brown Butter Almond Brittle has the most texture and has a vanilla base, which I love. Honey Vanilla Bean is a slight twist on a classic and it's not too out there so if you're a creature of habits, then this is for you. Brambleberry is more on the sour and tart side. It has some texture like a nice blueberry cobbler. Salted Peanut Butter is great for someone who loves peanut butter since the flavor is strong. The salt adds a nice dimension to the flavor profile.

I am not even a huge fan of donuts, I will only eat them from one of 3 places and this is one of them. Not only are they aesthetically appealing, but equally delicious! I am over 20 minutes away from them, but the drive is worth it!

You ever take a bite of something so good, and for just a split second you're mad? Like you've wasted so much time on other things? Their oatmeal pie is incredible. It's without a doubt the best oatmeal cookie I've ever had and the cream filling is a perfect compliment. It's not too sweet. It's a hefty sandwich about the size of a hamburger with a price to match, but it's worth every penny. We bought some other treats that we haven't even touched but if they're even half as good as the oatmeal pie they'll be fantastic.

Ice cream shop in the central Phoenix area, on Central north of Camelback. Great shop with lots of options and sweats. Coffee served as well. Great outdoor seating with cool misters. If your ever in this area, you'll love it

The Bouchon Bakery is a convenient place to enjoy the spoils of Thomas Keller's food genius if you forgot to make reservations at the Bouchon CafÃ©. It's a small to-go shop and they sell coffee, pastries, and sandwiches. They also sell macaroons in a decorative box ($16.99) - a perfect gift for the pet sitter, or for that co-worker covering for you while you're in Vegas. There was virtually no line when we went there (twice), and the service was attentive.

I love ice cream no matter what but this place was amazing to me because of the people behind the counter. So fun! So cute! So nice! The guy was really excited to torch the marshmallow fluff i ordered and it was perfect. Ice cream was amazing as expected. I got a double scoop because my eyes are bigger than my stomach and it was too much. Peanut butter tastes like a cookie as opposed to from out the jar. Tiramisu has the right hint of amaretto. Oh I also grabbed one of those salted caramel things in the front. I assume it's house made but wow it's so buttery salty and 50 cents! Hehe get one on the go. So worth it if you're a caramel lover like me. Can't wait to go back. It's a really hip and crowded place.

A cute little ice cream and candy shoppe owned by the guy who brought us Postino and Windsor, conveniently located next to Windsor. I love me some sweets and this place hits the spot. I am a big fan of the banana ice cream with choc chips or gummy bears. They also have cookies, cupcakes, candy, etc. They even have pretzel cones, now that I've never seen before. The staff is very friendly and is good and helping a lot of people when the line gets long. You're never waiting for long and it's always worth the wait. It's dangerous to live only a few blocks from this place.

I wanted to be wowed and just wasn't. Well the bagel bomb was good it was way over priced for what you got. We also a slice of crack pie and was shocked at how small it was for $6.50. All food seems overpriced in Vegas I was just hoping for more. The hot chocolate was good but nothing special. Maybe cake is where it is but we will never know. Also we went in the morning and cashier was either high or hung over but she wasn't on this planet.

i came in with friends and we all couldn't be happier with the service provided. i've come back two times since then, and received the same exact energy. the staff are extremely friendly and went out of their way to make sure my friends ice cream looked HAPPY. every flavor is so good, the place is clean, and they even offered to serve us as they were closing. i will always tell people to come here first, it's my favorite ice cream place

I love this place! The cupcakes are moist and fresh; the icing on top is the perfect amount, not too little but not too much. I'm not someone who likes too much cream or icing on the top of my cupcake so the amount that they provide is just perfect. However, the cupcake is a little small for the price ($5/cupcake) but other than that it is phenomenal. They have an ATM cupcake machine outside of the store which is really cute and fun to order through. But even better, inside they have a ton of cupcake and ice cream combinations to choose from as well as toppings. They cut the top of the cupcake off and put ice cream in between the top and bottom of the cupcake. It is a match made in heaven! I highly and strongly recommended it if you are in the Las Vegas area.

Best ice cream place in town! Pistachio is my all time favorite flavor, however they haven't been making it anymore! So, my new favorites are the Belgian chocolate and the coconut sorbet! The ice cream sandwich is a true delight! :) Thank you Sweet Republic!!!
I thought classics like this were all gone. I WISH we had one of these where I live. Outstanding, real deal ice cream! Real authentic flavors and great service!

Absolutely amazing ice cream place with super reasonable prices! The chocolate chip cookie sundaes are game changing. They actually heat the cookies up in an oven before putting them on your ice cream. Portion sizes are huge. This place is totally worth visiting!

This is a must see when in Vegas. Found this place just by chance while charging the car. The overall vibe gives the local feel but with a new twist. I had the Mexican chocolate donut and was not disappointed.
Expensive but soooo goooood and moist. You can never go wrong with Sprinkles cupcakes.

Love Mitchells! So many delicious flavors including several vegan options! Parking is pretty good in the back, and it's not far from many bars and the west side market which makes it very convenient. Decently priced. Highly recommend!
I got the rhubarb cake and a cheese filled croissant. The croissant was second to none. Amazing. The rhubarb cake was good too. Seemed like nice folks as well.
All the desserts here look amazing. I ordered the mini pecan tart pie and vanilla macaron with an iced vanilla latte on the side. The best macaron I've tried so far!
They have amazing ice cream and boba tea.Great customer service, employees where super nice and friendly. Explained everything on the menu and let us try many flavors of ice cream.
The most wondrous cupcakes ever await you here. With flavors too amazing to wrap your mind around. They have the best Red Velvet.....ever!

I don't understand how this place has as many stars as it does. PLEASE do not go here! I am saving you a TON of money. There are literally hundreds of other places in Vegas that have wayyy better ice cream for the price (including the grocery store.. or your local 7-eleven...). My wife and I came here based on high recommendation from a friend. We were told to get the brownie sundae - Lands End. But they didn't have brownies.... I guess I should have offered to run to the local Walmart to grab them a box of Ghirardelli brownies... so instead we got the cookie bits sundae. The ice cream/sundae: I'm not joking - it was completely flavorless. Everything was. From the vanilla and cookies and cream ice cream to the hot fudge and cookie bits. Shockingly flavorless. The "hot fudge" wasn't even hot!? The service: The person behind the counter was rude and completely unhelpful. When I asked for the the Lands End sundae, they responded like I was out of my mind for even asking for such a wild thing cause obviously I should have known they didn't have brownies! It felt like my wife and I were such a burden on them for even being in the shop. The price: It was $15.00 people!! I'm telling you, go to McDonald's for their $1 sundae and you'll have a better experience.. at the very least, McDonalds fudge will be hot.. I PROMISE you, don't go here. Go somewhere else. Your taste buds, family, and wallet will thank me.
Great ice cream! The line is usually long, but a lot of the times they have an employee that will take your order with a handheld device, making it much quicker.

I haven't had a bad thing here. The ambiance is amazing, as are the pastries, teas and coffees. I haven't had much from the full menu, but the soups are all amazing. I always stop by when I'm in NoDa!

Love! Love! Love it!!!!! DOOOONNNUUUTTSS. What am fun place to visit. It's not super big plane but the variety of specially donuts will leave you dizzy. So a selection of you get there early. We arrived at 930 and this place was more than 65% sold or. So don't think they pulling your leg about how fast they sell or... Wake up early!!! Going back today to try to get other donuts that we're sold out. The doctors were decorated to well, they had a fun atmosphere in the store and the customer service was so warm. In the light of everything that is going on most businesses their customer services have failed at this place makes you feel like you're welcomed and they treat you as so they really appreciate your business what a wonderful experience.

I love donut bar! They're so friendly and I stop in every time I come by Vegas. My favorite is the creme brulee donut! The pop tart donut is definitely extremely sweet (what do you expect for a donut stuffed with a pop tart), but it's a nice donut to share!

First time here, and it was awesome! I came a couple minutes after they opened and it seems they were hard at work setting everything up, the display was jaw dropping. I was given a first timers huge hello from the lady in front and she was super friendly I tried the creme brÃ»lÃ©e (was smaller than expected, but good!) Nutella overload (somewhat dry, but just the right amount of Nutella to keep me going) And what I thought was the best out of what I tried Blueberry cheesecake (not expected to be my favorite) I'll come back and try the rest!

Always a treat when I get Mitchell's! Seasonal special was lavender honey, amazing! Personally could do with a little less honey but that's just me! Mango sorbet is always refreshing and smooth! One of the classics I often get!

The cereal milk ice cream truly tastes like cereal milk. Glad I came here to try out what the hype is all about. The ice cream isn't life changing, but it's worth a try. Apparently they changed the "crack pie" name to "milk bar pie." People need to stop getting offended over everything.

Love this place. Its not just about the ice cream, but all of their flavors are amazing, it's walking in the door and having instant flashbacks to my childhood. It's a must try place in Phoenix and absolutely love treating myself to some Churn. Churn baby Churn

This place is a joke! We ordered almost all their popular pastries lobster tail, canoli, rainbow cake, cup cakes and chocolate cake. Spending more than hundred dollars only to find out that the pastries being sold at local grocery stores taste better than this. I think their pastries are over priced! Their icing in the cakes are really really sweet just like the cakes in the grocery store. Canoli is not that good the crust is so hard and taste blunt not creamy. Lobster tail is ok, the inside is creamy. I don't know why people are lining up for this. Not worth it...waste of money!!!

This place had good reviews online so we decided to check it out (we are not from AZ). I got the sweet cream in a waffle cone and it was a generous amount for 2 scoops. However, the staff was a little awkward! It was almost like they were mad at us for coming in half an hour before closing. There were 4 employees behind the counter and none of them greeted us when we walked in, they just gave us a blank stare. The ice cream was really good though!
The staff is very courteous and lets you sample before ordering even when the lineup is very long. Tried sweet corn, peaches and cream, peanut butter chip and carrot cake. All were delicious

This location in Las Vegas is not up to par to the one in NYC. The 2 stars is for service and quality of the macaron and croissant. First, it was obvious I was next in line and the counter girl took the guy behind me. There were 3 other workers milling around; either inside the kitchen or doing inventory. None of them acknowledged me even with my irritated face. Finally one of the workers asked what I wanted. The macaron was cold; meaning it was not fresh. I also got the almond croissant; if I've known this before hand I would've never wasted my money. Again, it was not fresh; it was dry and lacked almond cream filling. The vanilla macaron that I usually get at Bouchon's in Columbus Circle is so fresh, decadent and service is great! If Thomas Keller knew about the quality of the products that they're serving here, he would be appalled! Two wrongs will never make a right! Service sucks and so do their products. Shame on you!

Batch is the best bakery in Madison, hands down. That's a tall order because there are some damn fine breads and pastries in this town. I've had the baguette, demi baguette, ham and gruyere croissant, mini pies, cheese & fruit butter cakes, bacon and cheese biscuits and I always grab a raspberry oat bar for my neighbor. Nothing spreads happiness quite like Batch.
Super delicious donuts, friendly service. It's almost like a meal and I was full after just one donut.

Their pastries are really good! But their customer service sucks! And for that reason I think I'm gonna take my business elsewhere. I called on Monday to ask about getting a cheesecake. They only have it by the slice which I can buy 8 slices to make up a whole cake. No problem. $3/slice of $24 for the whole cake. Verified their whole business hours since the COVID reopening and they said 10am - 6pm. I got off work at exactly 5:30pm the following day, start hauling ass and called them on my way, only to be told that they're closing early. This was around 5:40pm and I'm around the corner already. I asked why, and they said they ran out of bread. I told them I'm not buying bread. I'm buying a cake. And it's for a birthday gift. Didn't matter. They're closed. I decided to drive over anyways. Parked my car, and the door is locked with a sign posted that they are closed. There were about 4 other vehicles who parked while we were there and tried to go in but no luck. I had to tell them what I was told over the phone "that they closed early because they ran out of bread". Sucks to be then really. I started looking for other bakeries at that time and found one across the street. Better YELP reviews! Awesome customer service! Great prices!

Their 4 scoop sampler is great for trying many flavors. My favorites are banana cream pie, New York cheesecake and cookie and creme. The syrup they use for strawberry cheesecake is a little too sweet for me.

Ice cream is one of very few foods I will admit to being a snob about (as in, "I am an ice cream snob"). Tortillas too, but that's for another review. Anyway, Sweet Republic has the best ice cream, gelato, fro-whatever, etc. I've ever had. Hands down. What really makes the place special, though, is their help. Whether it be one of the owners or staff, they're always very knowledgeable about their product, will engage you to talk about their product and help find the best flavor for you, and are fast so the line doesn't get too backed up as we've all seen in many an ice cream parlor. Whoever does the hiring deserves a special award. Sweet Republic's people are the best.

I moved here from Austin, TX and missed the Keep Austin Weird vibe you find in a lot of the restaurants. Amelie's has that vibe. Late night when I needed a treat, it was off to Amelie's, and totally worth waiting in the line that wrapped around the restaurant. It's also a great Saturday morning spot to sip coffee and read (if you're lucky enough to find seating). So, why 4 stars and not 5? It's a bit pricey. It's delicious for sure, but you end up spending a lot of money because the cheaper items are still overpriced and small. Also, I sadly developed a gluten allergy and while I enjoy their tea cakes, mousse, salted caramel brownie, and macaroons, obviously I wish there were still more options.

INTRO: A unique Asian cafe that specializes in matcha desserts, Matcha Cafe Maiko is prepared to bring some matcha into your life. I can guarantee that this special experience will make you say "I love matcha so matcha!" after finishing your first dessert. I normally get their matcha soft serve, but you also can't go wrong with their other desserts and drinks on their menu. DESSERT 1: Golden Shogun ($9.50) - This is the ultimate flex move. A soft-serve flavor of your choice (matcha, hojicha, seasonal) topped off with a 24k edible gold sheet in a waffle cone will make you feel like a millionaire. The matcha flavor is present, but it's definitely not one of the strongest I've tasted. I've made stronger matcha milkshakes at home. WORTH IT? YES, it's worth it for the experience and whenever you're in town (Overall 7/10)
Donuts looked really good I only tried one of them so far was not wowed I would go back because there was other ones that might be better

How Disappointing. A "French Bakery" that makes awful croissants. One would think they would make the best ones in town. My advice for the best croissant in the area, go to The Fresh Market. (And that is the only reason to go to The Fresh Market.) Although the product comes in frozen (I know, I know) at TFM, when they are baked just right, they are excellent. Some blueberry preserves smeared on it and I'm happy... I did try some pastries at Amelie's but nothing to write home about. I tried a baguette and it was edible. I still can do better pastries and bread in my galley kitchen. Not worth the drive from Cornelius.
Love this place! They have the best maple walnut ice cream! Wish they had outdoor seating or more seating when you have a bigger group. Very reasonably priced.

Creme Brulee in a donut....need I say more!!! Not a lot of seating, but I think it's more of a "to go". Very friendly and informative staff. A little pricey for donuts, but for donuts as unique as these TOTALLY worth it!

literally the best place ever. doughnuts are so good- even to people who are not vegan! mornings are really busy and there is usually a 20+ minute line, and holidays can have up to hour long waits, so plan when you will go wisely(10-closing there is typically no line but flavors may be sold out). CHECK THEIR INSTAGRAM OR FACEBOOK BEFORE YOU GO! they often sell out, and occasionally announce closures day-of. i go once a month to tryout the monthly menu items, and although my body weight doesn't thank me, my taste buds certainly do!
Best cookies ever!! The birthday truffles and blueberry cream are to die for! Whenever in New York I stop by and now that they are in vegas another sweet excuse.

Worth the twenty minute drive from our hotel. We ordered a half dozen and had leftovers. You can't eat more than a couple at a time. No complaints but surprisingly very filling and of course delicious.
Churn is a friendly neighborhood ice cream place. The ice cream is great, flavors distinctive and unique and the ambiance is friendly

Delicious cupcakes! My kids love the cupcakes here a lot. This is our first time visiting this place but won't be last. I like the cupcake atm idea. It was pretty ordering cupcake from theough the ATM.

This is probably the best ice cream I have ever had. I had the Blue Monster and I love it. I went in wanting the Graham central station but it was sold out. My 2nd choice black Walnut was too, that is ok because my 3rd choice was so good. Great customer service skill as well.

I'm certain there is an urban dairy farm on the back end of this joint...this is the most well-balanced, freshest-tasting ice cream I've ever had. The flavors are just unique enough to stand out among artisan menus but classic enough to pull on your cravings. Vietnamese Coffee, for instance. Who doesn't love coffee ice cream? But, who the heck has ever had Vietnamese Coffee? Do it. You won't be sorry.

What a lovely spot west of uptown! This bakery is decorated beautifully! I had the strawberry pop tart & oatmeal cream pie. Delicious! The employee working was very nice too. This is a great spot to grab a treat with a friend. Love the little play corner too. I hope they eventually do tea, this is the perfect spot for that. Love the tea decor on the wall.

Not looking forward to the long line but I will defintiely be back... Its not your typical ice cream you can definitely see why there are so many chains across the nation. they know what they're doing when it comes to ice cream.. Me and the wifey tried the 4 flavor sampler Banana Cream, Spouse like a house, Butter Pecan, Chocolate Malt Caramel The ice cream is very thick and creamy also you can taste that it has high content of butter fat so it made your eyes roll back on first bite. I cant wait for us to try more stuff when we come back. I think the chocolate malt caramel stood out for me as well as the butter pecan. I dont really like banana ice cream but wifey sure did enjoy it.

Might not be fair to rate this because I didn't try the cake. I had a birthday cake shipped from this store to a friend for his birthday. He had thanked me for the cake but didn't say anything about liking it. I asked him if the cake was good. He hated to tell me because he loved the gesture, but he said it was not even average. I heard the founder on How I Built This (NPR) and was so excited to send a cake from Milk Bar. I haven't tried anything from Milk Bar, sending this was my first purchase. I read great reviews so I will try it again. Would love to know if anyone else has had a disappointing experience with the shipped cakes. I planned on them being my "go to" gift for family birthdays.

What's not to love? It's a little taste of Paris, right in NoDa. The coffee, pastries, sandwiches, atmosphere and staff are all superlative. If you haven't been yet, get in your car NOW. You can thank me later. With a cream puff.

OMG, this is the best ice cream that have ever had. Thank god Mitchell's isn't around the corner from where I live. My absolute fav is the pistachio,ummmmmmmmmm. My daughter had me addicted to this place. The staff is always friendly & the store is always neat and clean.
Delicious treats , friendly staff , The Villani's team went above and beyond to assure our special birthday order was ready and perfect at pickup

This is a small unsuspecting spot. Although not friendly for colder weather as far as seating, we ordered ours to go. I got the red velvet...the slice was huge but moreover the quality ingredients of the moist red velvet with complimentary crÃ¨me cheese frosting - absolutely delightful. I ate on it for three days and it was still good. I sparingly eat white sugar desserts so when I choose to indulge I want it to be great. They did not fail cause this treat was worth every morsel and bite. Not over exaggerating I promise (I recently had some cookies from a popular spot and was deeply disappointed). Stay with that quality Villani's! My out of town friends enjoyed their dessert as well.

This place did not disappoint. As I walked in my mouth was already watery and everything looked delicious. I had to go here and see what the hype was about. You can't go wrong with their desserts here.

Pretty good savory crepe. Service was quick and easy. I ordered the maple glazed apple with walnuts. I really liked it. They are open to suggestions as they make it if you want a little more on the crepe. Now I went at 4 pm so there were only 2 other people which might have helped in my service. Decent deal and I would stop back here and try another crepe in time.

My favorite pastry here is the milk pudding buns. I didn't see any around when I first looked around and ended up with other items. I asked the worker putting the items out if they had any and she said not today. I finish paying and while waiting for my drink decided to walk around once more and guess what! MILK PUDDING BUNS!! I was upset at first, but quickly grabbed 6 buns and headed over to check out again. The guy at the cashier noticed I had an 85C bag in my hand already and welcomed me back while he was ringing up the people in front of me. The store smelled quite off today, not fresh baked goods, but smelled like sewer today. I can smell it through my 3 layer cotton mask . Hopefully they get that fixed and due to covid they removed the tongs. I rather they offer tongs cuz there were multiple people touching pastries and putting them back. Hand sanitizer is only available checkout where you pick up drinks. I think having one available as people enter the store would be a great idea. As for the worker who I asked if they had any milk buns, she asked what kind and named a long list of buns until I recognized a name just to tell me they didn't have any. Which was inaccurate, at least check before answering me if you're unsure but she answered back with a quick solid No. Shoutout to the Gambit, the cashier today you attention to detail actual made up for the somewhat poor experience I had earlier.
Nice restaurant! Prices were good and their bacon was wonderful. The patio outside is nice too. Went for breakfast right when I arrived in Vegas. Great start to the trip for sure

We've been to the San Francisco Ghiradelli and now the Vegas one, and they're both great! We went on a Friday evening, and the store wasn't crowded at all and there was no line. Lots of great options to choose from, the smell of chocolate is everywhere. Be prepared with a sweet tooth, we split a large sundae and couldn't finish! Good location and nice service.

I've never had anything bad from here. Anything from the amaretto soft serve, to the marshmallow milkshake, to the south side hot dog (which I get with only mustard), it's all amazing. They're open most of the year, too! It's cash only, so bring cash with you (or pay the fee at the ATM they have). They also have the famous Nancy B cookie in a sundae. I always take out of towners here

Buttery croissants and bakery items. For Vegas this is a decent quick breakfast. The staff was nice and helpful. Coffee was ok, I would have expected a stronger brew. I do seek this out as a go to while in town.

After visiting the Bouchon Bakery in Napa Valley, I just had to visit the one in Las Vegas when I was there. I brought my friends along because they wanted to see the huge macaroons. Be careful though because the place is pretty difficult to find (I even had trouble with the directions given by the Venetian associates). The only thing I purchased at this Bouchon Bakery was the full set of MACAROONS (a total of six pieces). NOTE: If you buy 5 macaroons, you get 1 free. The macaroons were about $3.50 each. I purchased a pre-packaged set of six macaroons, which containedVANILLA, PISTACHIO, RASPBERRY, COFFEE/CAPPUCHINO, CHOCOLATE (brownie?), AND A SPECIAL BOUCHON FLAVOR. Truthfully, since they were pre-packaged, I'm assuming the macaroons were made that day hopefully rather than the day before. Just to be safe, for anyone purchasing six, one of each flavor, go with the regular boxing where they grab the fresh ones made. I wanted to bring it home to Orange County to enjoy with my boyfriend, so I stuck it in the trunk and drove on home with the others. Need I remind you it was summer, but I never would have thought anything would have happened to the macaroons, sensitive creatures they are. Sad to say, never ever leave your macaroons out in heat, even if it's not in direct sunlight. Room temperature is best. Why? Because when I opened the truck, my poor chocolate/brownie macaroon sort of melted and oozed out this liquid and traveled down the box and ruined my other macaroons. Some were also cracked already (dang, sensitive pastries)!!! They all looked horrific by now, so I dare not show them to my boyfriend. As a result, I enjoyed them by myself. :) :) :) Hahaha. Anyways, onto the review of the tastings and enough of my ranting. In the end, I prefer the Napa Valley Bouchon over this one. Overall, all the flavors were actually perfect and light. The only thing I have to say about the CHOCOLATE/BROWNIE macaroon was that it was a little too dense and chocolatey (probably because of the melting though). My favorites were the VANILLA and PISTACHIO. The coffee one was alright. If you like coffee flavored pastries, you might like this one. As for the RASPBERRY, I never got to taste it. *sobs* I accidentally left it out and the dang ants got to them. This was a bad luck batch of macaroons is all I'm saying. On my part though, not the bakeries.
So good! I've tried key lime custard, chocolate ice cream, and a blueberry milkshake. The milkshake was amazing! Definitely worth a stop.

My Dear Butterwood, I'm still in love with you and think you have the most delicious cakes on this planet and the most adorable space in which to enjoy them. And one of your charms is the fact that you are open late, making you a great post-date-night spot to grab dessert and coffee. But Butterwood....don't be open late if you keep running out of desserts before closing!! The last four (count 'em, FOUR) times I have been here after 9, your dessert case has been nearly wiped out (the last two times, in fact, it was literally *empty* save for one sad-looking piece of honey bread). What's the point of being open late if you consistently run out of desserts to offer your cake-loving customers?! I would think by now you should be able to have a better idea of your customer flow (I'm no business whiz, but it's painfully obvious to me as a frequent customer that you do not regularly keep sufficient quantities of desserts on hand to fulfill demand for an entire weekend day). Now Butterwood, I'll give you one more chance, both because I love you and because I think I might have a diagnosable cake addiction disorder. But if you expect me to continue to spend approximately 95% of my bi-weekly paycheck on your cakes, I'm going to need you to start keeping your case stocked during ALL of the times that you are open. Otherwise, you might as well just close early and save us the trouble of making the trek only to be continually disappointed. Still your biggest fan (for now), Tricia
Yum yum yum! Stop by for the amazing options and creations. A favorite place and so happy to support a local place. They have cookies, ice cream and tons of nostalgic candy and thing.

The cupcakes aren't really cupcakes per se. Instead, they are cream and a little bit of cupcake below. The chocolate chip cookie was hard, but the ice cream was good. Overall overpriced and not really worth checking out given the low quality.

The green tea latte and macarons were delicious! Service was very friendly too! I love studying here because it's so quiet and has good seating. The coffee is good quality for a chain cafe and I would recommend the caramel macchiato. Regular customer here and they recognize me!

I can't believe how long it took for me to finally come upon this gem in Little Italy. I came here for lunch the other day, and I ordered the sausage and spinach stromboli with a side of marinara sauce. This was so delicious and so incredibly CHEAP! I also tried a bite of my friend's gnocchi, which was also bombdiggity! I definitely recommend trying their hot foods, which are located to the right side of the registers. They're affordable and yummy in the tummy! You also should try their apricot linzers and mini chocolate macaroons--they're to die for! Two thumbs up for Presti's!

I had an excellent experience at Churn. The dessert I had was phenomenal. I tried the lil Dragon freezie and it was delicious. I'm located on the west valley but I will definitely be making the long drive for Churn again. I highly recommend it. Fun staff and awesome environment, plus unique and tasty desserts!

So we've been coming back to try something sweet and I have to say that the birthday truffles are absolutely fabulous!! I totally recommend this! Last visit, we got the truffle box, which had 4 (3 truffle) bags. I choose 2 double chocolate, strawberry shortcake, and birthday flavor. The cost for the truffle box was $27. We will also grab a few cookies. The price is a little high but we figure, hey we're on vacation :)
